home_pitcher_note: Acquired from the Orioles for five players, Bedard makes his regular-season debut hoping to pick up where he left off last season, when he won nine of his final 10 decisions before an injury in August.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is making his third straight Opening Day start for the Rangers. He was the losing pitcher in the past two, going just five innings both times.

home_pitcher_note: The Mariners' Opening Day starter a year ago, Hernandez starts the season as the No. 1a starter behind left-hander Erik Bedard, but he definitely has ace capabilities. He would gladly take a first start like the one he had a year ago, when he shut out the Athletics for seven innings, striking out 12.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla was limited to 23 starts last year because of an elbow injury, but he was 3-2 with a 3.86 ERA in eight starts after coming off the disabled list in August. He was a 15-game winner for the Rangers in 2006 and was 1-2 with a 7.20 ERA in three starts against the Mariners last year.

home_pitcher_note: An innings-eater when he pitched for the Twins the past four seasons, Silva is being counted on to do the same for the Mariners. He has worked at least 200 innings two of the past four seasons and logged at least 180 in the other two, giving the Mariners a potential staff workhorse. He relies on getting early-count outs and should benefit greatly by Seattle's rock-solid defense and pitcher-friendly ballpark.
away_pitcher_note: Jennings was signed as a free agent in the offseason. The National League Rookie of the Year when he won 16 games for the Rockies in 2002, Jennings spent last season with the Astros and had his season cut short by injury. He finally underwent surgery to repair a torn flexor tendon. He is 0-1 with a 4.97 ERA in two career starts against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Once he got through the final barrier and was able to cut loose after off-season surgery on his ulnar nerve, Moseley showed that he has the right stuff to claim the fifth spot in the rotation with John Lackey sidelined by a strained right triceps. Moseley is a finesse pitcher who pounds the strike zone and relies on quality defense.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard was one of three players acquired from the Boston Red Sox on July 31 for reliever Eric Gagne. He was 2-1 with a 5.58 ERA in eight starts for the Rangers before being shut down in September because of soreness in his forearm. He has a 7.04 ERA in two career appearances against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: For openers, Weaver wasn?t razor-sharp, putting too many fastballs in good locations to Twins hitters. But he was resourceful in getting out of jams and kept his team in the game while yielding three earned runs on eight hits and two walks in 6 1/3 innings. His endurance (106 pitches) was excellent, and he struck out five hitters.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers are going with a four-man rotation for the first two weeks of the season because of two off-days and won't need a fifth starter until April 12. Luis Mendoza won that job when Brandon McCarthy went down with severe inflammation in his elbow. Millwood, who lost to the Mariners on Opening Day in Seattle, is 2-2 with a 3.59 ERA in seven career starts against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Garland�s debut with the Angels could not have been much more impressive. Getting 17 of his 24 outs on the ground, without the need of a single strikeout, he held the Twins to a run on six hits, with 64 of his 95 pitches strikes -- most of them hard sinkers down in the zone. He walked one man, on a full count. He�ll look to follow the same script, working fast and getting quick outs from a stellar defense, in his home debut.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla's first two starts are on the road. In 2007, he was 2-7 with an 8.04 ERA in 13 starts on the road. He was 0-2 with a 7.36 ERA in three starts against the Angels last year and is 3-2 with a 5.11 ERA in nine starts against them in his career. He is 2-1 with a 5.33 ERA in Anaheim. Vladimir Guerrero is 16-for-39 (.410) with three home runs against Padilla.

home_pitcher_note: Jennings went to high school in the Dallas suburb of Mesquite and then to Baylor University, but he will be making his first appearance at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington at their home opener. He has made just one career start against the Orioles, pitching seven scoreless innings in a 2-1 victory for the Rockies on June 17, 2005. Jay Payton (4-for-17) and Ramon Hernandez (5-for-15) are the only Orioles with more than four at-bats in their career against Jennings.
away_pitcher_note: Burres threw a scoreless inning in relief on Opening Day and will move to the rotation on Sunday. The lefty narrowly edged Matt Albers for the last slot and will be watched carefully this season.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood is making his 34th career start at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, where he is 15-11 with a 5.04 ERA in his career. He was 8-4 with a 4.78 ERA in 15 starts there last year. Millwood was 2-0 with a 0.69 ERA against the Orioles last year and is 7-2 with a 3.49 ERA against them in his career. Going into the season, that was tied with the Mariners for the most victories against one American League opponent.
away_pitcher_note: Trachsel pitched into 10 three-ball counts in his season debut, but he worked out of trouble enough to pitch into the sixth inning. Last year, Trachsel allowed three earned runs or less in 17 of his 25 starts as an Oriole. Baltimore traded Trachsel to the Cubs at the end of last August and signed him as a free agent right before Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Gabbard is making his first start at home. In his brief Major League career, he has never lost a home game, either with the Rangers or the Red Sox. He was 1-0 with a 4.50 ERA in three starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington after being acquired from the Red Sox on July 31, and he is 6-0 with a 2.36 ERA in eight career starts when his team is at home. He was 1-0 with a 2.53 ERA in two career games against the Orioles. The one victory was in the Rangers? 30-3 victory in August.
away_pitcher_note: Loewen returned to the mound on Saturday for the first time since May 2007, completing his comeback from corrective surgery to repair a stress fracture in his left elbow. Loewen said that he felt rusty in his season debut, but he was fortunate to escape with a no-decision. Loewen has an 8-6 career record in 26 big league starts.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla was 4-3 with a 3.28 ERA in 10 starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington last year and is 12-8 with a 4.24 ERA in 27 career starts there. He made two starts against the Blue Jays in 2007 went 1-1 with a 3.21 ERA, and he is 3-1 with a 3.25 ERA against them in his career. That's his second-lowest ERA against any American League opponent behind his 2.08 ERA against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Litsch earned the win over Boston in his first start of the season on Saturday. Despite struggling at times with his location, Litsch threw five innings, allowing two runs on five hits. The 23-year-old right-hander walked three and struck out two batters in the 83-pitch effort.

home_pitcher_note: Mendoza is scheduled to make his first start for the Rangers. He started the season on the disabled list with a blister on his right middle finger, but that has healed and he should be ready to go. Mendoza, who relies on his power sinker, made the rotation in Spring Training after Brandon McCarthy went down with severe elbow inflammation. He was 1-0 with a 2.25 ERA in six games for the Rangers last season, including three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is coming off his first win of the season, allowing four runs on eight hits over eight innings against Boston on Sunday. Halladay has not fared well pitching in Texas, posting a career 3-3 record with an ERA of 7.00 in 54 innings at Ameriquest Field.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is being recalled from Double-A Frisco, where he has made one start. He had a no-hitter going against Springfield before giving up a run on three hits in the seventh. He was still the winning pitcher in a 2-1 victory. Feldman has made 73 career relief appearances at the big league level over the past three years but this will be his first start. The Rangers turned him from a reliever into a starter at the end of Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: In two starts this season, the Blue Jays have seen two different sides of Burnett. In his first start against New York, Burnett stifled the Yankees bats through six innings, allowing two runs on five hits, with three strikeouts and a walk. In his second start against Oakland, the hard?throwing right-hander was not as successful, allowing six runs on 10 hits over 4 2/3 frames. Burnett has been solid in three career starts against Texas, posting an ERA of 3.27 to go along with 25 strikeouts in 22 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jennings has lost his first two starts of the season. He has allowed 12 hits in 9 2/3 innings, including four home runs. He has also walked six while striking out two. He was supposed to start on Sunday but the Rangers are pushing him back one day to give him extra rest. He has made two starts against the Angels in his career and is 1-0 with a 4.26 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Back-to-back solid efforts by Santana are highly encouraging. He held the Indians to two earned runs across six innings despite giving up six hits and three walks, repeatedly pitching out of trouble while striking out five. His fastball was crackling, and he had quality breaking stuff to go with it. Texas has not been kind to Santana, who is 1-4 with a 8.92 ERA in seven career outings on the Rangers' home turf.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood started against the Angels last Saturday in Anaheim. He pitched a complete game against them but still ended up the losing pitcher in a 2-1 loss. He allowed two runs on 12 hits and a walk while striking out five in eight innings. He is 2-3 with a 3.38 ERA in eight career starts against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Moseley, the emergency starter, rebounded from a drubbing in his season debut with a solid winning effort against the Indians. Using his two-seam fastball to good effect and keeping hitters off balance, Moseley blanked the Tribe for five innings before yielding four runs, two on gopher balls, in his sixth and final inning. Moseley wants to push past the sixth inning this time and show he can get deeper in games and save wear on the bullpen. He has not yielded a run in 7 1/3 career innings at Texas, and has a 2.53 career ERA without a decision in six appearances against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old right-hander faced the Rangers for the first time in his career Friday in Arlington, holding Texas to two runs on six hits over 5 2/3 innings. Litsch is 4-4 with a 4.13 ERA through 10 career starts at Rogers Centre.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers are slotting Gabbard in between Kevin Millwood and Vicente Padilla so they can split up their two power right-handers. Gabbard pitched seven scoreless innings in his first start against the Angels and then allowed three runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Orioles on Thursday. He has made just one relief appearance against the Blue Jays in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay is coming off his first complete-game victory of the season over the same Rangers squad. He pitched well on Saturday at Texas, allowing one run on six hits with a walk and strikeout. It was Halladay's 32nd career complete game. He passed Pat Hentgen for third on the all-time Blue Jays' list.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is making his second straight start against the Blue Jays. He was the losing pitcher on Friday, when the Rangers lost, 8-5. Padilla allowed five runs, four earned, in six innings. He's 1-0 with a 2.77 ERA in his first two starts on the road this season after going 2-7 with an 8.04 ERA in 13 road starts last year. Padilla is 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA in two starts at Rogers Centre.

home_pitcher_note: The Red Sox have won all four of Matsuzaka's starts. However, he is the first to admit that he doesn't deserve the credit for his last win, which came over five shaky innings against the Yankees. Matsuzaka threw 116 pitches, walked six and struck out two. He allowed five hits and four runs. Matsuzaka pitched just once against the Rangers last season, getting the win despite giving up seven hits and five runs over five innings. In that one, Matsuzaka pitched through an extreme case of the flu, which made the performance a heroic one in the eyes of manager Terry Francona and his teammates.
away_pitcher_note: The Red Sox will get a firsthand look at what they gave up when they sent Mendoza to the Rangers on July 30, 2006. Mendoza was signed by Boston as a free agent out of Mexico on June 12, 2000. He lost his first start of the season to the Blue Jays on Saturday, when he allowed four runs in five innings. Three of the runs were unearned.

home_pitcher_note: Lester is growing frustrated with his inability to pitch deep into games. Control continues to be the problem. In his last start, Lester walked five and allowed four runs over 4 1/3 innings. He threw 97 pitches, 55 of which were strikes. This will be Lester's first start against the Rangers since his Major League debut in June 2006. In that game, Lester gave up five hits and three runs over 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Jennings has lost all three starts this season, and he allowed six earned runs in 4 2/3 innings on Monday. When manager Ron Washington was asked whether he was concerned, he said, "Not yet. The next time it?s time to give him the ball, we'll give it to him." Jennings has a 2-0 career record against the Red Sox, but he hasn?t pitched against them since 2004. He won his only start at Fenway Park, allowing three hits and no runs in seven innings -- but that was on June 11, 2002. Jennings was 16-8 that season.

home_pitcher_note: As usual, Wakefield has been steady. He took a no-decision in his last start, giving up seven hits and two runs over six innings against the Indians on Tuesday. He has given up three earned runs or fewer in all three of his starts. He?s holding opponents to a .254 average. In his career against the Rangers, Wakefield is 9-14 with a 5.66 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is 0-9 despite a 4.02 ERA in his last 11 starts on the road going back to June 17, 2007. The Rangers are 0-11 in those 11 starts, having averaged 1.80 runs per nine innings of support for Millwood. He is 4-3 with a 4.15 ERA in 10 career starts against the Red Sox. He is 3-1 with a 3.44 ERA at Fenway Park. David Ortiz is 6-for-12 with three home runs off him but Manny Ramirez is just 4-for-17 (.235) with a home run.

home_pitcher_note: The righty is coming off a tough start against the Yankees on Wednesday, when he was belted around for eight hits and seven runs over 3 2/3 innings while walking one and striking out two. The Texas native will be making his first career appearance against the Rangers. Buchholz hasn't gotten to 100 pitches or pitched into the seventh inning in any of his first three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard is making his first career start against the Red Sox. He began his career with them before being traded to the Rangers on July 31, 2007. He is 1-0 with a 1.38 ERA in two starts on the road this year, but 2-4 with a 5.09 ERA in 16 appearances on the road in his career. He was 5-0 with a 1.60 ERA in five starts for the Red Sox at Fenway Park.

home_pitcher_note: Until this season, the Tigers had never lost more than two of Verlander's starts in a row. Now, his outings have accounted for four of Detroit's losses, the latest a resounding defeat Thursday at Cleveland in which Verlander battled his command from the start and never quite found it. His fastball control has run off and on this season, and without it, the power aspect of his game is much less effective. The good news for Verlander is that a much more invited foe awaits in Texas, against which he owns a 3-1 record and 2.49 ERA in four career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is making his fifth start and his fourth start on the road. He is 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA in his first three starts away from Arlington. He was 2-7 with an 8.04 ERA on the road last year. Opponents are hitting .292 off him so far this year but just .192 with runners in scoring position. He is 3-0 with a 2.08 ERA in four career starts against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers picked up his first victory of the season with an impressive performance against the Blue Jays in his last start. The veteran left-hander allowed just three hits over 6 2/3 innings. His only real struggles came during the bottom of the fifth inning when he started battling some control problems. He is 6-3 with a 3.80 ERA in 15 career appearances against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: After starting the year on the disabled list with a blister on the middle finger of his right hand, Mendoza allowed seven runs in three-plus innings against the Red Sox. He is a power sinker ball pitcher but he needs to complement that with a better breaking ball and/or changeup. In eight Major League appearances over the past two seasons, left-handed hitters are batting .346 and right-handers are hitting .205.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman struggled with his control during his last outing against the Blue Jays. He issued six walks and required 108 pitches to get through five innings of work. His most dangerous inning came in the bottom of the second. After allowing a leadoff single to open the frame, Bonderman issued three consecutive walks but was able to escape with just two earned runs after inducing a key double play. Bonderman is 2-1 with a 4.83 ERA in five career starts against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers wanted to give Jennings two days of extra rest but decided they couldn't do that because of their overworked bullpen. So Jennings pitches on his normal four days of rest. Scott Feldman was recalled from Double-A Frisco but will be in the bullpen. The Rangers were going to start him but were concerned about not having a long reliever behind him. So Feldman will be in long relief behind Jennings.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood is 1-0 with a 3.75 ERA in two starts at home this year and is 8-1 with a 3.52 ERA in his last 13 starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington. In 35 career starts in Arlington, he is 16-11 with a 4.97 ERA. He has never beaten the Twins in his career, going 0-5 with a 5.64 ERA that is his third highest against any American League team.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander made it two straight impressive outings at the Metrodome to start the season. After holding the Angels to just one run in his first start of the year, Blackburn delivered a nearly identical start against the Indians. He pitched 7 2/3 shutout innings, holding Cleveland to eight hits while not issuing a walk in the outing, although he did record one hit-by-pitch. Blackburn has settled in to mix in all of his pitches and most importantly, has started to rely on his sinker, something he'll need at hitter-friendly Ameriquest Field.

home_pitcher_note: The 31-year-old Aruban-born right-hander is expected to be recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma to make his Rangers debut, pitching in the big leagues for the first time since May 12, 2007. Ponson was 1-2 with a 3.47 ERA in five games (four starts) for Oklahoma. He arrives with a career record of 82-101 with a 4.94 ERA in 10 Major League seasons and will be making his 246th career start. He is 9-2 with a 2.62 ERA in 14 career games (13 starts) against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up three solo home runs in a start at Detroit, Baker worked on making some mechanical adjustments during his windup and those changes paid off in his last start against the Indians. Baker made his third quality start in four outings. Over seven innings, he allowed one run on five hits and struck out a season-high eight. The Twins want Baker to concentrate on keeping pitches down in the zone and making sure that he doesn't give opponents too many chances to hit the ball out of the ballpark. Next up, Baker will face the Rangers in his first career start at Ameriquest Field.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla has made just one of five starts at home so far this season. He lost to Toronto, 8-5, on April 11 when he allowed five runs -- four earned -- on seven hits and three walks in six innings. He is 12-9 with a 4.31 ERA in 29 career starts in Arlington. He was 1-1 with a 4.22 ERA in two starts against the Twins last year and is 1-2 with a 4.32 ERA in his career against them.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez cruised along for the first four innings of his last start in Oakland. But the pitcher found trouble in both the fifth and sixth. Hernandez got some balls up and watched what had been a 3-0 lead quickly disappear into a 4-3 deficit. Hernandez was able to walk away with the no-decision, but the Twins will need him to continue to extend deep into outings and limit the damage. Hernandez will start the last contest of the six-game roadtrip when he faces the Rangers at Ameriquest Field.

home_pitcher_note: Jennings is facing the Royals for the first time in his career. Jennings is 0-2 with a 9.64 ERA after two starts this year at Rangers Ballpark, where opponents are hitting .341 off him with 14 hits, including three home runs, and eight walks in 9 1/3 innings. He has a a 5.73 ERA in his last two starts, holding opponents to a .211 average but with seven walks and three home runs in 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Tomko felt like he never had control in his last start, a loss to the Indians. He lasted just four innings, allowing seven runs and 11 hits while throwing 108 pitches. The high pitch count can be contributed to control issues. Tomko thought he let the batters get ahead in the count too often. The outing was his worst of the season. Tomko had gone seven innings and six innings in his previous two starts and allowed a combined seven runs.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood, coming off a Friday start against the Twins in which he coughed up five runs in the first three innings, will be making his ninth career start against Kansas City. In the previous eight, the right-hander posted a 4-3 record with a 4.66 ERA, as Royals hitters have batted a collective .303 against him with four home runs in 46 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister had gone 18 innings without giving up an earned run at Kaufman Stadium before the Indians' David Dellucci hit a solo home run off him last Thursday. Bannister allowed another run that inning, which was all Cleveland needed for a 2-0 victory. Those runs came an inning after Bannister got drilled in the shin by a line drive, an injury that severely affected his performance, he said. Bannister's latest performance came on the heels of his worst one of the season, a loss against Oakland in which he gave up five runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson, on Saturday, made his first Major League appearance since May 12, 2007 when he started against the Twins at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington. He allowed five runs, one earned, in 51/3 innings. Prior to that he was 1-2 with a 3.47 ERA in five games, including four starts, at Triple-A Oklahoma. Ponson is 9-7 with a 4.60 ERA in 19 starts against the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Trey Hillman called Greinke a stable force, someone the team could depend on, after his performance on Friday against Toronto. Greinke got a no-decision but allowed just one run in seven innings. Hillman considered keeping Greinke in for longer but decided he'd rather sit the pitcher because of cold weather. Greinke has allowed only four runs in 29 innings so far this season.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton has been a tough-luck pitcher all year, and it looked like that way in his last start Sunday against Seattle. He was behind 2-0 and Felix Hernandez was pitching a gem. But Hernandez lost it in the eighth, giving up four runs. Blanton kept his team in the game and was rewarded with the victory, just his second in six decisions. He leads off the Texas series at home. He was 2-0 with a 4.12 in two starts against the Rangers last season.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is making his first start in Oakland since Sept. 16, when he faced just two batters and was ejected after hitting outfielder Nick Swisher with a pitch. He is 3-1 with a 4.66 ERA in nine career games against the Athletics, including a 1-1 record with a 7.11 ERA in six appearances in Oakland. Padilla is 2-1 with a 4.70 ERA in four starts on the road this year and 11-13 with a 5.55 ERA in 33 road starts since the beginning of the 2006 season.

home_pitcher_note: Gaudin, who was rushed off the disabled list in the wake of injuries to fellow starters Rich Harden and Justin Duchscherer, struggled in his first two starts of the season but has been lights-out as of late. In his most recent outing, Monday at Anaheim, he won his third consecutive start by holding the Halos to give hits and two walks while striking out four over six innings. Gaudin, whose velocity was down in his first two outings, is back to working in the 90-93 mph range, and his sinker is every bit as good as it was during the first half of 2007, when he went 8-3 with a 2.88 ERA before the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Murray was pulled after just one inning of his Wednesday start for Triple-A Oklahoma when it became apparent he would be summoned for this start. Murray was 2-0 with a 4.00 ERA and one complete game through his first five starts for the RedHawks this year. The left-hander made 14 appearances in the big leagues last year (including two starts), spanning 28 innings. He was 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA and held opposing hitters to a .238 average. He has pitched three times in relief against Oakland, going 1-1 with a 7.11 ERA. The Athletics put up five runs on eight hits (three home runs) in 6 1/3 innings against Murray.

home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday in Anaheim, Smith gave up two runs on three hits and three walks while striking out four over seven innings for his fourth quality start in five assignments this year. The A's offense was stifled by the Halos, pinning Smith with his first big league loss in his first complete game, but the rookie was again impressive, keeping the hosts off-balance with his high-80s fastball and an array of offspeed pitches. Smith has never faced the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman threw 69 pitches over four innings Tuesday against Kansas City in relief of the injured Jason Jennings. He will take over Jennings' spot in the rotation beginning with this game, which will mark his second Major League start. Feldman has made five career relief appearances against Oakland, posting a 0-0 record and 1.50 ERA. He has allowed the Athletics one run on two hits and nine walks over six career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Washburn struck out a season-high seven batters in his last start but surrendered six runs (five earned) in a loss to the Indians. The veteran left-hander continued to pile up the pitches, throwing 102 over 4 1/3 innings, the fifth time in six starts he reached the 100-pitch mark. He has logged six innings twice and seven innings once.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood, coming off a Wednesday start against Kansas City, will be facing the Mariners for the second time this year. He lost on March 31 at Safeco Field in the season opener by a 5-2 score after allowing two runs (none earned) on four hits over six innings. In 16 career starts against Seattle, the right-hander is 7-7 with a 4.02 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After one of his shortest outings of his career -- one-plus innings against the Athletics -- was cut short because of a slight leg injury, Batista bounced back in a big way in his next start, holding the Indians to four hits and one run over seven superb innings. But that one run prevented him from winning his third game of the season. The six strikeouts were his second-highest total of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Ponson was terrific in his last start against the Royals, holding them to one run on six hits and two walks in eight innings. He struck out five and the Rangers won, 2-1. This will be Ponson's third start for the Rangers. He allowed one earned run in 5 1/3 innings in his first start against the Twins, but four unearned runs cost him. He is 2-4 with a 4.84 ERA in 12 games, including 11 starts, his career against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander made a second consecutive solid start in his last outing, surrendering one earned run over seven innings against the Yankees in New York, but three of the four errors they committed led to two unearned runs and his first loss of the season. He retired the final 14 batters he faced and did not allow a hit after the second inning. His troublesome hip appears to be 100 percent and his pitches are crisp and sharp.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is making his second start against the Mariners and both have come at Safeco Field. He started there in the second game of the season and allowed one run on eight hits in six innings. He walked three and struck out four but was not involved in the decision as the Rangers rallied for a 5-4 victory in the ninth inning. Padilla is 2-5 with a 5.66 ERA in eight starts and two relief appearances in his career against the Mariners. He is 1-3 with a 5.77 ERA at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander is coming off the worst outing of the season and one of the worst of his young career, a 12-hit, six-earned-run debacle against the Yankees in New York. The 12 hits were the second-most Hernandez has surrendered in his 80-start MLB career. It was the first time this season that a Seattle starter showed signs of being frustrated because of the continuing lack of run support. Hernandez has not fared particularly well against the White Sox. He is 1-1 with a 5.01 ERA in four career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard has made four starts for the Rangers and is coming off the disabled list. He has been sidelined with a strained muscle in his lower back. He pitched four innings for Double-A Frisco on a medical rehabilitation assignment on Saturday and allowed one run on one hit and three walks in four innings. He struck out six. He has a 5.59 ERA in three career appearances against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: This is probably Feldman's start but it could go to A.J. Murray. Both pitched well against the Athletics in Oakland. Feldman lost 3-1 on Sunday despite taking a shutout into the seventh inning. The Athletics scored three runs off him, and Feldman is now 0-1 with a 4.38 ERA in two starts this season. Murray, making his first start for the Rangers, beat the Athletics, 6-3, on Saturday, allowing three runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander struck out a career-high 10 in his last start, while allowing only one run in a three-hit, six-inning effort against Texas. Since making his Major League debut on April 9, Smith has not allowed more than three runs in any of his six starts and has gone at least five innings in each.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood is 2-0 despite a 5.55 ERA in four starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington this season and is now 17-11 with a 5.10 ERA in 37 career starts. He is 3-3 with a 4.34 ERA in 10 career starts against Oakland. Frank Thomas has been particularly rough on him with 12 hits in 20 at-bats against him, including two home runs. That's a .600 average that is Thomas' highest against any pitcher with at least 20 at-bats.
away_pitcher_note: Following a rough outing in Anaheim, Eveland scattered three hits and four walks while pitching into the eighth without allowing a run in a 10-inning, 2-1 Oakland win over Baltimore in his seventh start of the year. The lefty threw 90 pitches while improving his home ERA to 0.92. He will look to conquer his struggles on the road, where he has a 4.98 ERA, against the Rangers. Eveland has never faced Texas in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson has won his last two starts for the Rangers, allowing just two runs on 13 hits in 15 innings. This will be his fourth start for the Rangers. He was signed midway through Spring Training and opened the season in Triple-A Oklahoma where he was 1-2 with a 3.47 ERA in five games. He is 3-3 with a 6.58 ERA in 13 games, including 10 starts, against the Athletics in his career.
away_pitcher_note: This will mark Harden's return to the Oakland rotation after spending the past month on the disabled list with a strain under his right shoulder blade. One of the game's most dominant pitchers when he's healthy, Harden, who throws a high-90s fastball and has a split-fingered pitch that occasionally knuckles, has been on the DL six times since the start of the 2005 season. In his final Minor League rehab start Tuesday, Harden struck out nine without a walk -- he hit three batters -- over six shutout innings of three-hit work for Class A Stockton against visiting Visalia. Harden is 5-2 with a 3.73 ERA in 11 career appearances against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla threw seven shutout innings in a 2-0 victory over the Mariners on Wednesday. He allowed two hits, walked two, hit a batter and struck out eight. He has allowed one run in 13 innings against the Mariners in two starts this year and is 3-5 with a 4.94 ERA in 11 games, including nine starts, in his career. Padilla, the Rangers' Pitcher of the Month for April, has won three straight starts and allowed just one run in his last 21 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander pitched another superb game in his start against the Rangers at Safeco Field, surrendering six hits and two runs over seventh innings. It was his third straight quality start, but he has only one win to show for it. The Mariners' offense has produced one run for Bedard in the last 14 innings he has pitched. Right-handed hitters are batting .157 (13-for-83) against him.

home_pitcher_note: Gabbard has not allowed a run in his last two starts. Problem is he has pitched just a total of 5 2/3 innings in his last two starts. Gabbard went 3 2/3 innings against the Mariners on Thursday before being forced out after an altercation with Richie Sexson. The Mariners' first baseman charged the mound after Gabbard threw a pitch that was eye level. After the altercation, Gabbard stayed in for two more batters but had to come out with sore knees. It was his first start after coming off the disabled list. He was sidelined with a strained muscle in his back, an injury that occured while pitching two scoreless innings against the Red Sox in April.
away_pitcher_note: Payback could be on the mind of the 22-year-old right-hander, who surrendered four runs in the first two innings against Texas in a game at Safeco Field. Hernandez went five innings, his shortest outing of the season, and needed 67 pitches to make it through the first two innings. He has not won since pitching a complete-game victory over the Athletics on April 16. Though he struck out five Rangers in his five-inning stint, Hernandez has been having a tough time putting hitters away after getting ahead in counts.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman, who has also made two relief appearances, has a 2.89 ERA in three straight quality starts. He pitched six scoreless innings on Friday against the Athletics in a 4-0 win. It was his first victory as a starter. The key to his success has been late life on his fastball, working both sides of the plate and throwing his sinker and cut fastball at the same speed. Feldman has pitched eight scoreless innings over nine career relief appearances against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Silva dropped his second consecutive decision despite a seven-inning effort against the White Sox in his last outing. The right-hander allowed four runs on eight hits in a 4-1 loss. After posting a 3-0 record with a 2.79 ERA in April, Silva has struggled in May. He's 0-2 with a 10.80 ERA in two starts this month, allowing 12 runs on 19 hits in 10 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson struggled in his last outing, Sunday against Oakland, allowing six runs (all earned) on seven hits with five walks and a strikeout over 5 1/3 innings. He gave up four runs in the first, but then settled down and was able to make it to the sixth inning. Ponson said he didn't have command of any of his pitches and relied mostly on mixing up pitches. In his career against the Astros, Ponson is 0-2 with a 2.08 ERA. In Interleague Play, Ponson has a lifetime record of 8-14 with a 4.47 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It's not exactly a record he's proud of, but it's a record nonetheless. Chacon has made eight starts this year and has yet to record a decision, the longest such streak in franchise history. He's also tied for the all-time MLB record for the most starts to begin a year without a decision. The right-hander has six quality starts, the most among all of Houston starters.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla hasn't pitched against the Astros since June 30, 2006, when he beat them, 4-1, at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington. He allowed just four hits and a walk in eight innings and struck out five. That was his first career victory against the Astros. Prior to that, he was 0-4 with a 5.68 ERA in 10 games, including five starts, against them. Lance Berkman is 8-for-16 with five doubles and a home run off Padilla.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt completed eight innings for the first time this year during his start on Monday against the Giants. He yielded three runs early but decided to stop pitching to contact and just be more aggressive. He struck out five in his final three frames to improve to 4-3. Oswalt lost his only start against the Rangers last year, allowing three runs over 6 1/3 innings. In his career, he's 4-3 with a 3.53 ERA in nine games versus Texas.

home_pitcher_note: Gabbard allowed two runs in 5 1/3 innings in his last start against the Mariners on Tuesday and was not involved in the decision when the Rangers won, 5-2. Gabbard has still never lost a home game in his short career. He has made 10 home starts for the Red Sox and Rangers and is 6-0 with a 2.70 ERA. He is 1-0 with a 4.30 in five starts for the Rangers at the Ballpark in Arlington. This will not only be Gabbard's first start against the Astros, but also his first start against any National League team.
away_pitcher_note: Backe lost his fifth game of the year in his last outing on May 13 in San Francisco, allowing four runs over six innings in a game the Astros were dominated by Giants pitching. Backe allowed three innings in the first, thanks in part to a mental error by Michael Bourn and a passed ball by J.R. Towles. Backe has faced the Rangers five times in his career, compiling an 0-2 record and a 9.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time in his last three starts, Bonser suffered through a disastrous first inning. This time Bonser gave up a grand slam to the Blue Jays DH, Matt Stairs, to put the Twins in a big hole. He would recover to allow just one more run over his final five innings. But the Twins seem to be getting frustrated with Bonser's inability to stop yanking the ball early in his starts. That tendency to overthrow has hurt Bonser and the feeling is that only he can correct the problem. He'll get his next chance when he faces the Rangers for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman is making just his second start on the road this season. He pitched six scoreless innings against the Athletics on May 4 in Oakland, but allowed three runs in the seventh and ended up losing, 3-1. He has made one relief appearance against the Twins, giving up three runs in two innings on April 26 at the Ballpark. He has a 5.79 ERA in six career relief appearances against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins pitched six strong innings in a 3-2, extra-inning loss to Toronto on Thursday and didn't figure into the decision. In the outing he gave up two runs on five hits, walked two and struck out a career-high six batters. Perkins has given the Twins a chance to win in each of his first two career starts this season since being called up from Triple-A Rochester. He will face the Texas Rangers in the second game of a three-game series at the Metrodome on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: After three relief appearances, Mathis is making his first Major League start. He earned it on May 12 with a scoreless inning of relief against the Mariners in a 13-12 victory. He was the first Rangers reliever to get his first Major League victory in his debut appearance. He was 5-0 with a 3.55 ERA in seven starts for Triple-A Oklahoma before being called to the Major Leagues.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander has started to show progress, after hitting a bit of a skid recently. Blackburn pitched seven innings against the Rockies, allowing just two runs on six hits. He didn't issue a single walk and struck out five. The Twins have been wanting Blackburn to slow down and not overthrow when he gets into trouble. Something he did in the one inning where the Rockies tagged him for runs. After giving up two straight hits, he settled down to get key outs and mixed in all of his pitches. Next up for Blackburn is a start against the Rangers. He received a no-decision in his only start against the club this season, allowing five runs over six innings to Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Ponson is facing one for his former teams. He pitched for the Twins in 2007 and made seven starts, going 2-5 with a 6.93 ERA before he was released. This is only his second start on the road this season. He beat the Mariners, 10-1, on May 6, holding them to one run in seven innings. He is 9-2 with a 2.56 ERA against the Twins in his career, his lowest ERA against any American League team.

home_pitcher_note: In his return to National League action, Hernandez looked very much at ease. He held the Rockies to just three runs on eight hits over 7 1/3 innings. All of that damage after Hernandez carried a perfect game into the sixth inning. The veteran pitcher continues to baffle hitters with his slow curveball around 60 mph and his fastball registering at 85 mph. Next up will be his second start of the season against the Rangers and the challenge will be to see if he can improve from that last outing vs. Texas. Hernandez gave up seven runs over 2 2/3 innings to the Rangers on April 27 in Arlington, in what was clearly his worst start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla has won four consecutive decisions after allowing two runs in seven innings against Houston on Saturday. Padilla has a 1.60 ERA for his last five starts. He has been automatic when he reaches 100 pitches. Padilla is 5-0 with a no-decision in his six starts where he has thrown more than 100 pitches. The win against the Astros matched his win total from last season. The Rangers are 8-2 when Padilla starts.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona was stellar again on Saturday, working 7 1/3 innings and allowing one run on four hits with four strikeouts and, perhaps most impressively, no walks in a 4-2 loss to the Reds. Prior to Saturday, he had issued 35 walks in 48 2/3 innings. Carmona said the game was the best he's felt all season, as all but three of Carmona's outs in the game came on the ground. In nine career games against the Rangers, Carmona is 4-1 with a 2.25 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard took his first loss of the season in a 5-4 loss to Houston on Sunday, allowing five runs in five innings. It was the first time he has allowed more than three earned runs in seven starts this season. The Rangers are 5-2 when Gabbard starts. He has induced 57 ground-ball outs, an average of eight per start. But he struggled with getting the ball up in the strike zone against the Astros. Gabbard is 0-1 with a 6.97 ERA in two games against Cleveland, both at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Lee pitched well early on, but struggled at times with his location as the game progressed in his last start -- a 6-4 loss at Cincinnati on Sunday. He posted season-worst marks in innings pitched (5 2/3), runs allowed (six total, five earned), hits allowed (10) and strikeouts (two) in earning his first loss of the season. Lee held a Major League-best 0.67 ERA heading into the game only to have it jump to 1.37. Brandon Phillips' RBI groundout in the first inning snapped Lee's 16 consecutive scoreless inning streak. Lee is 3-2 with a 6.52 ERA lifetime in five games against the Rangers. He faced them once last year when he went 6 2/3 innings and gave up seven earned runs in a losing effort.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman is 1-1 with a 3.45 ERA in five starts. He has pitched at least six innings in all five starts, and the first four were quality starts. That streak was broken when he gave up five runs in six innings in his last start against the Twins on Monday. He has made five career relief appearances against the Indians, and has a 1.42 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the White Sox on Tuesday, Sabathia was saddled with a loss he didn't deserve for the second time this season. In seven strong innings of work, Sabathia allowed just two runs on seven hits with eight strikeouts. The runs came on two solo homers. A lack of offensive support did Sabathia in. Still, he has continued to distance himself from those rough four starts to open the season. Sabathia is 2-2 with a 2.15 ERA in four May starts.
away_pitcher_note: Mathis pitched a scoreless inning each in three relief appearances before making his first Major League start on Tuesday against the Twins. He allowed nine runs, six earned, in 2 1/3 innings in an 11-4 loss. He is filling in for Kevin Millwood, who could be close to returning when this spot in the rotation comes around again. Mathis was 5-0 with a 3.55 ERA in seven games for Triple-A Oklahoma before being called up on May 11.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir's 16-inning scoreless streak came to an end on Tuesday in Oakland, but not his ability to pitch effectively. The left-hander hasn't lost a thing since coming off the disabled list. He allowed one run on four hits over seven innings against the A's. Kazmir is 1-0 with a 2.05 ERA in four games against the Rangers. He's allowed the Rangers two runs in 16 innings at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Ponson is coming off a complete-game victory over the Twins, allowing one run on six hits and a walk in a 10-1 victory over the Twins. It was the 29th complete game of his career, but his first since April. He is 8-8 with a 4.14 ERA in 24 career games against the Devil Rays. He is also 6-5 with a 3.96 ERA at Tropicana Field, his most victories in any Major League park except Camden Yards.

home_pitcher_note: All good things much eventually end, and it happened to Sonnanstine in his last start against the Oakland A's on Wednesday. He allowed seven runs on nine hits in six innings and lost for the first time since April 9, ending a personal five-game win streak. Throwing strikes was not the problem; it was keeping the ball in the ballpark. He gave up two homers and four doubles. After retiring the first seven batters, it all came crashing down. When he gave up seven runs in 3 1/3 innings to the New York Yankees in mid-April, he came back to throw a three-hit shutout in his next start.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is now 4-0 with a 2.09 ERA in his last six starts. He did not get a decision in the Rangers 8-7 victory over the Twins on Thursday when he allowed three runs in five innings. But the Rangers victory left them 9-2 in Padilla's 11 starts. He is 0-2 with a 10.13 ERA in his three career starts against the Rays, his highest ERA against any Major League team. He is 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA in two starts at Tropicana Field.

home_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his ninth start of the season and his second career start against the Rangers. Friday night against the O's, the 24-year-old right-hander pitched 7 1/3 scoreless innings to earn his third win of the season and his fifth win in six career starts against Baltimore. Garza has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup. He is 1-0 with a 1.42 ERA against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard has allowed 13 runs in 13 innings in his last three starts, inflating his ERA from 1.85 to 4.34. He allowed six runs on four hits and six walks in 2 2/3 innings in his last start against the Indians on Friday. He has made just one start against the Devil Rays, pitching 1 2/3 scoreless innings on Aug. 12 before leaving the game with forearm stiffness.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood was cleared to return off the disabled list after throwing 65 pitches in a simulated game at Progressive Field on Saturday. Millwood has been sidelined for two weeks with a strained right groin muscle. He is 1-1 with a 7.67 ERA in his last six starts. His last start was against the Athletics but had to come out in the first inning after injuring himself. He is 3-3 with a 4.29 ERA in 11 career starts against the Athletics.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer tossed the best game of his career in his last start against the Red Sox, carrying a no-hitter into the seventh inning before David Ortiz broke it up with a one-out single. That was the only hit allowed by Duchscherer, though, and the second of only two baserunners on the night in a 3-0 combined one-hit shutout with closer Huston Street. After throwing 101 pitches, Duchscherer left the game after a career-high eight innings. This will be his first career start against Texas, a team against which he has a career 3-1 record as a relief pitcher. Duchscherer was 0-1 versus the Rangers last year, allowing three runs on two hits through just 2/3 of an inning.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson got his first loss of the year after allowing a season-high 12 hits in a mere five innings in Tampa Bay on Monday night. The right-hander walked three batters after allowing only one walk in his previous two outings, and will look to bounce back at home on Saturday. The veteran hurler faced Oakland once already this season, surrendering four first-inning runs before settling down to leave the game with a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: In his Major League-tying 12th start of the season, Blanton picked up his first home victory in a 6-3 win over Boston while putting a stop to the longest home losing streak of his career at five. He walked a season-high-tying four batters but also struck out a season-high-tying seven in his three-run, six-hit, six-inning effort. This is the second time Blanton will face Texas this year. In his May 2 start at home against the Rangers, he allowed just two runs on seven hits through seven innings, but he took the tough-luck loss in a 4-3 game. Blanton is 6-2 with a 4.75 ERA in his career against Texas.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has pitched at least six innings in all six starts, but the Rangers are just 1-5 in those games. Feldman couldn't overcome one big hit, a three-run home run in his latest outing, a 5-2 loss to the Indians by Saturday. Prior to that start, the hurler also gave up five runs in six innings to the Twins, again with allowing a three-run homer. If Feldman can avoid the long ball vs. Oakland, the right-hander could finally pick up his second win of the season on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Smith snapped a four-game losing streak while pitching into the seventh inning and not allowing a run to the visiting Blue Jays in his last start. He gave up just six hits and one walk with three strikeouts as his teammates gave him three runs of support in a 3-1 A's win -- a far cry from the 0.57 runs of support per nine innings he had been averaging over his previous five starts. Smith has already faced Texas twice this season, going 0-1 with a 2.77 ERA. He went six innings both times, surrendering a combined five earned runs and nine hits with 14 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: In just two starts this season, Mathis has had a case of the Jekyll and Hydes. In his first start, on May 20 at Minnesota, he coughed up nine runs (six earned), which were his first runs allowed of the season, in just 2 1/3 innings, on eight hits and four walks. Mathis rebounded nicely though in his last start on May 25 at Cleveland, holding the Indians to just one run on seven hits and three walks in six innings. Mathis has depended on his defense so far this season, to say the least. In 11 1/3 innings pitched, he has only four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Last season, Fausto Carmona filled in when two Indians starter suffered injuries, and he ended up winning a permanent job and 19 games. This year, it's Laffey filling in more than admirably -- first for an injured Jake Westbrook and now for Carmona. Laffey is coming off a six-inning outing in which he gave up just two runs (one earned) on seven hits and a walk to get his third win. He has allowed just three earned runs over his last five starts. This will be his first career appearance against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Murray's only start of the season wasn't sparkling, but it was effective. On May 3 at Oakland, Murray lasted 5 1/3 and held the Athletics to three runs, two earned, en route to a victory. In that outing, he allowed only six hits and two walks while striking out two. In his career, Murray has pitched a grand total of one inning, spread out over two appearances, against the Indians. But he's flawless in that one inning with one strikeout.
away_pitcher_note: This was supposed to be Jake Westbrook's second start since his return from the disabled list and an intercostal strain. Instead, Westbrook is headed right back to the DL with right elbow inflammation. Mastny, a reliever in parts of three seasons with the Indians, gets his first Major League start. He is 7-3 with a 5.00 ERA in 68 big league relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson got back on track in his last start, earning his fourth victory of the season on May 31 by holding the Athletics to four runs in seven innings. Ponson gets the start in the series finale with Cleveland, which will be his first meeting with the Indians this season. Ponson is still in search of his first victory against the Tribe, as he's winless in 12 appearances -- 11 of which starts. In those 12 games, he's 0-7 with a 9.47 ERA, having allowed 83 hits and 35 walks to just 31 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Lee has given up 11 runs in his last three starts after giving up four in his first seven starts of the season. In his last outing, against the Royals, Lee picked up the win, but only lasted six innings, giving up four runs. It was his second-shortest outing of the season. Lee has struggled lately, but who could've expected him to continue pitching as brilliantly as he did in April and early May.

home_pitcher_note: In his return from the DL on Friday against the Athletics, Millwood was superb, holding the Athletics to one run in six innings on five hits while striking out five and walking none. Millwood earned the victory against Oakland, which was his first since April 30 against Kansas City. Millwood's groin, which landed him on the DL, gave him no problems as he located pitches with ease. He returns to the mound Wednesday against Cleveland, which will be the first time he's faced his old club this season. Millwood is 2-1 in three career starts against the Tribe, with a 4.12 ERA and 23 strikeouts to just six walks.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia lost the fifth of his career Saturday night against the Royals. Sabathia went eight innings, allowing four runs, three of which came in one inning. Again, he didn't get much run support, which contributed him to losing his seventh game. In his last three starts, Sabathia has gone a combined 22 innings and given up just seven runs. Yet he hasn't won any of those games.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla is scheduled to be back with the team Thursday and will return to the rotation Friday against Tampa Bay. He threw a bullpen session in Nicaragua yesterday, so he'll be ready to take the mound for the Rangers earlier than originally thought. Padilla is currently on the bereavement list, so the team will have to make a roster move when he returns. He is 1-2 in his career against Tampa Bay with 9.18 ERA. In 12 starts this season, Padilla leads the team in wins and has the lowest ERA among Texas starting pitchers.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir is coming off a record-breaking May, in which the ace set new marks for wins in a month (five), and notched the best ERA (1.22) in club history. The southpaw is coming off another solid performance on Saturday night, in which he shutout the White Sox, holding the squad to three hits over seven innings. The shutout was Kazmir's third in May, and he has allowed only six runs in six starts -- four of which came May 4, his first start off the disabled list. He is at his best when he is locating his fastball as it makes his slider even more devastating. He will be facing Texas for the second time this season, holding the Rangers to three-hits and one run in a win on May 26.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman had his fifth quality start this season in his last outing, Sunday against Oakland. He went six innings allowing four runs, three earned, on four hits in an 85-pitch effort. Feldman left the game with a 7-4 lead, but the bullpen gave up nine runs to spoil his outing as he got a no-decision. "It's always frustrating to lose," Feldman said. "I felt fine out there and tried to get the job done." In four lifetime appearances against Tampa Bay, Feldman is 1-1 with a 3.60 ERA after allowing two runs, both earned, on five hits over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: After back-to-back tough outings, the right-hander's most recent performance was much improved, as Sonnanstine held the White Sox to three runs through 5 2/3 innings. But, he did allow 10 hits and has yet to regain the early-season form that saw Sonnanstine win four straight decisions. He is a master of deception of the mound, throwing an array of pitches from all different angles, but is at his best when he leads with his fastball. Sonnanstine has lost both of his decisions against Texas, posting a 6.75 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Mathis is coming off another rough start. His last time out he struggled mightily with his command, getting lit up by Cleveland's Casey Blake for two home runs and seven RBIs on June 2. Mathis allowed eight runs in all in 3 2/3 innings as his ERA ballooned from 5.56 to 9.00. Manager Ron Washington noted that Mathis' first bad start -- six earned runs allowed in 2 1/3 innings against Minnesota on May 20 -- came on three day's rest and his most recent start came on seven day's rest, so a normal five day's rest may do him some good. Saturday will be Mathis' first career start against the Rays. Mathis has yet to face an American League East club.
away_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his 11th start of the season and is 2-0 with a 1.88 ERA in two career starts against the Rangers. Tuesday night against the Red Sox, the 24-year-old right-hander allowed five earned runs on six hits -- two were home runs -- and two walks while striking out three to take his second loss of the season. Garza has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup. Sundays start will be the first of his career at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Meche fizzled fast in his last outing, giving up four runs in the second inning to the White Sox en route to a 6-2 loss. While the offense isn't giving Meche (or anyone else) much run support, he blamed himself and the pitching staff for coughing up too many big innings and putting the team in the hole. He's already lost eight games and his ERA is pudgy compared to last year's svelte 3.67. Meche hasn't won since May 15. Against the Rangers, he's 4-8 in his career with a 6.68 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood was a gamer for the Rangers in his last start. Despite giving up four runs in the first inning to the Indians on June 5 -- and throwing 26 pitches in the process -- he lasted into the seventh and earned his fourth victory of the season. He didn't record an out in the seventh, but in six-plus innings, he struck out six and didn't walk a batter. Millwood has now put together back-to-back wins for the first time since July 3 and 8 of last season. Millwood will return to the mound Tuesday at Kansas City on regular rest. In nine career starts against the Royals, Millwood is 5-3 with a 4.96 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Call Davies the stopper. In his first start after being called up, he halted the Royals' 12-game losing streak. In his second start, on Friday night at New York, he halted the club's 11-game skid in road games in a 2-1 victory over the Yankees. He was much more efficient in his latest effort, using 104 pitches in 6 2/3 innings against the Yankees. He'd used 100 in just five innings against the Indians. Best of all, he's throwing strikes and keeping the ball down, inducing ground balls. He's made three career starts against the Rangers and lost all three.
away_pitcher_note: With Monday's off day, Padilla will be able to start on regular rest. This coming after a week in which Padilla's start was pushed back four days because he was in his native Nicaragua tending to a family issue. Padilla lost his last time out, which was his first loss in seven starts. During that seven-start span, he was 4-0 with a 2.82 ERA. Padilla faces the Royals Wednesday, a team he's 1-1 against in three career starts with a 4.30 ERA. He won his last start against Kansas City on Sept. 5, 2007, when he pitched six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister's sunshine success didn't spill over into Saturday afternoon's game at Yankee Stadium. He was hammered for five runs in 3 2/3 innings although he had no decision. Thus his daytime record remained 5-1 compared to 0-5 at night and this is a chance to re-assert his superiority in a daylight game. Bannister's season started with three wins in three starts, but he's 2-6 in his 10 starts since. He was drilled for seven runs in three innings by the Rangers in an April 30 loss at Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Hurley will be making his Major League debut. A 2004 first-round Draft pick, Hurley spent the beginning of this season at Triple-A Oklahoma. He compiled a 2-5 record with a 5.30 ERA, but had three quality starts in his last four outings. He was called up to replace Sidney Ponson, who was designated for assignment last week.

home_pitcher_note: Perez recovered from his woeful start against the Giants on Monday and threw well enough against the Padres on Saturday. He allowed one run -- on a home run -- in 5 1/3 innings, surrendering four hits and two walks and hitting two of his last three batters. Now he is to face the Rangers and their dangerous batting order. It could be ugly or he could bury them. But it's always that way with Perez.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman gave the Rangers a strong start his last time out, holding the Rays to two runs on five hits and two walks in seven innings while striking out five. It's the second time this season he's gone seven innings and held an opponent to fewer than three earned runs, yet neither effort was enough to get him or Texas a victory. So, Feldman heads into his start against the Royals still looking for his first victory since May 9. He's faced Kansas City once this season in a four-inning relief appearance. The Royals tagged him for two runs that game, but he has a 3.86 ERA in 14 career innings against K.C.

home_pitcher_note: Maine's five-inning start vs. the D-backs on Tuesday was lengthened by some early control problems, but he got through any jams during those 101 pitches (61 strikes) by fanning seven batters. By giving up three earned runs in that start, which eventually turned into a no-decision in a 9-5 loss, it was the ninth time in Maine's 12 starts this season that he gave up three runs or fewer. And Maine hasn't fared much worse vs. the American League -- he has a career 2-1 record with a 3.72 ERA in Interleague Play.
away_pitcher_note: Late hits from his team and mistakes from the Royals on Tuesday prevented Millwood from getting his 11th consecutive loss in road decisions. He'll probably have to pitch better on Sunday if he wants to get a win and end that streak. Against the Royals, Millwood gave up 11 hits and five runs in six innings. On the positive side, he struck out the side once and got out of a couple early jams. Millwood has given up nine runs in his last two starts after giving up just one in the start before those.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez was fortunate the Mets abandoned their 2-1 ways when he made his start in San Diego on Sunday. He provided neither a quality nor a quantity start. He reached four runs allowed before he reached five innings and was gone after five, having thrown 97 pitches. Ten produced hits, one hit a batter and another was preceded by a balk that led to two runs. He departed with a 5-4 lead and a sense of having escaped, but New York's bullpen couldn't hold it in a series-ending loss.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard replaces Doug Mathis, who has been moved to the bullpen. Gabbard started this season with the Rangers but was sent to Triple-A Oklahoma after going 1-2 with a 4.75 ERA in nine starts. He is the second young pitcher to join the rotation in the last week. Eric Hurley replaced Sidney Ponson and started on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla avoided a loss and got a no-decision in his last outing, when the Rangers scored 10 runs in the final three innings against the Royals. He went six innings and gave up five runs (four earned). Padilla has already surpassed his win total (six) of last year. In his his last three starts, Padilla is 2-1 but has given up 12 runs in 18 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson allowed one run on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings on Thursday against the Cubs, but the Braves' bullpen surrendered a ninth-inning homer to negate Hudson's strong effort. Hudson did exactly what an ace was supposed to do to halt a dismal road losing streak, but he received no help. The Braves went 0-for-9 with runners in scoring position to provide very little run support (two runs) for Hudson. He has pitched into at least the seventh inning in each of his past five starts, and he has not allowed more than three earned runs during that span. Hudson is 6-5 with a 4.01 ERA in 16 career starts against the Rangers. His last start against the Rangers came on July 13, 2005, when he gave up five runs on five hits in 2 2/3 innings and took the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Hurley made his Major League debut on Thursday against the Royals and allowed four runs in six innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out three in the Rangers' 6-5 loss. A first-round Draft pick from 2004, Hurley was 2-5 with a 5.30 ERA in 13 starts at Triple-A Oklahoma, including 1-2 with a 2.57 ERA in his last four starts before being called up.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes recorded his first win since May 18 after scattering five hits and two runs in eight innings on Friday against the Angels, snapping the Braves' five-game losing streak. He gave up a solo homer in the second inning but recovered and picked up his third win of the season. He hasn't pitched badly in his past three starts, he just hasn't been rewarded with a victory. He has allowed no more than four earned runs in each of those three starts, and has struck out at least five in three of his past four starts. Reyes has shown remarkable improvement from the beginning of the season, when he was erratic with his location and couldn't pitch deep in the games. The 23-year-old left-hander has since become a dependable mid-rotation starter.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 0-2 with a 5.35 ERA in his last six starts. The Rangers are 1-8 on the season in his nine starts, even though six of them have been classified as "quality." He is 1-0 with a 3.32 ERA in seven games, including five starts, at home, as opposed to 0-3 with a 7.33 ERA on the road. Opponents are hitting .302 off him with runners in scoring position and .206 off him through his first 60 pitches and .319 off him after that.
away_pitcher_note: Morton impressed during his Major League debut on Saturday, limiting the Angels to three earned runs over six innings. He was perfect in four of his innings and allowed each of the three runs with two outs. The lanky 24-year-old right-hander, who was a third-round selection in the 2002 First-Year Player Draft, has a live fastball and the ability to buckle hitters with a sharp curveball. He was 4-2 with a 2.05 ERA in 13 appearances (12 starts) for Triple-A Richmond.

home_pitcher_note: Redding was the pitching star for Washington last Sunday, lasting six innings and giving up two runs (one earned) on five hits against the Mariners. Redding will face the Rangers for the fifth time in his career. He has given up 17 earned runs in 8 2/3 innings against them.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood snapped a 10-game losing streak over his past 14 road starts with an 8-7 win over the Mets on Sunday. Millwood allowed two runs in six innings and is now 3-0 with a 4.50 ERA in four starts since coming off the disabled list on May 30. He missed 20 days with a strained right groin muscle. Millwood has never faced the Nationals since the move to Washington, but he is 15-5 with a 3.60 ERA against that franchise while they were in Montreal. That's his most victories against any Major League team.

home_pitcher_note: Nationals right-hander Garrett Mock is the leading candidate to replace left-hander Odalis Perez in the rotation against the Rangers. Mock has a 4-2 record and a 3.12 ERA with Triple-A Columbus. The last time Mock pitched in the big leagues was on June 8, against the Giants. It was his Major League debut, and it was an outing he would like to forget. He didn't get past the fifth inning, as the Nationals lost, 6-3, at Nationals Park.
away_pitcher_note: Gabbard is 0-3 with an 8.22 ERA in his past five Major League starts. That includes a 4-2 loss to the Mets on Sunday in which he gave up four runs on eight hits and three walks in 5 2/3 innings. That was his first start since returning from Triple-A Oklahoma. He was optioned to Oklahoma at the end of May to work on his command and was 0-1 with a 4.97 ERA in two starts for the RedHawks. This is his first appearance ever against the Nationals. Gabbard is 2-6 with a 5.44 ERA in 21 games, including 18 starts, on the road in his career.

home_pitcher_note: It looked like Lannan was going to have one of his best outings last Tuesday against the Twins, but he made one mistake. He didn't allow a hit until the fourth inning -- a double by Joe Mauer. Lannan was cruising, in fact, until the sixth inning. After getting two quick outs in that inning, Lannan's breaking balls betrayed him. On a 2-2 slider, he gave up a single to Mauer. The next hitter was Justin Morneau, who hit the first pitch he saw -- a curveball -- for a two-run homer. The ball landed in the right-field upper deck.
away_pitcher_note: After earning his ninth victory Tuesday against Atlanta, Padilla has won seven of his last 10 starts. He allowed just two runs, one earned, in six innings against the Braves, striking out four and lowering his ERA from 3.89 to 3.73. In addition to leading the Rangers in victories, Padilla leads the team with seven quality starts. In his 15 starts this season, he's held opponents to three earned runs or fewer 11 times, and seven times he's kept opponents to no more than one earned run. In 14 games, 10 of which starts, against the Washington franchise, Padilla is 3-4 with a 3.99 ERA. In his last two starts against Washington, which both came in 2005, Padilla is 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler pitched brilliantly in his last outing, holding the Orioles to one run over 6 1/3 innings, walking two and striking out four. Moehler has held opponents to three earned runs or fewer in seven of his eight starts this year. Against the Rangers, Moehler has a lifetime record of 5-4 with a 4.96 ERA over 11 games versus the Rangers, including nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hurley has two no-decisions in his first two Major League starts, but the Rangers have lost both games late. His last start was against the Braves on Wednesday and he allowed just two runs in five innings. He allowed four in five innings in his first start against the Royals. Hurley was 2-5 with a 5.30 ERA in 13 starts at Triple-A Oklahoma before being called up but had a 2.67 ERA in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt was his old self in his last start against the Rays, allowing two runs over 7 2/3 innings with two walks and five strikeouts. The right-hander was locating his fastball well and had all of his breaking pitches working. Oswalt last faced the Rangers on May 17, exiting early with a tweak in his groin area. He yielded six runs over six innings in that start.
away_pitcher_note: To get another victory, Feldman might just have to toss a shutout. Against Atlanta in his last start, Feldman allowed just two runs in seven innings on five hits and three walks while striking out four. He departed with a 4-2 lead, but the bullpen cost him the victory. Nevertheless, if Feldman continues to pitch like he did against the Braves, his next victory will follow. Feldman faced the minimum in four of his seven innings and he retired 12 of the last 13 batters he faced. Feldman will take the mound in Houston on Wednesday with an extra day of rest. In 5 1/3 career innings against the Astros, Feldman is 0-0 with a 6.75 ERA, having allowed four runs on six hits and two walks with four strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez was in good form during his last outing on June 21 in Tampa Bay, allowing two runs over 5 2/3 innings while taking a no-decision. The lefty didn't allow a hit until the fourth frame and struck out six during his 100-pitch outing. At Minute Maid Park this year, he's 1-2 with a 2.10 ERA over five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is 3-0 with a 4.22 ERA in five starts since coming off the disabled list on May 30. In 32 innings since then, he has walked 10 and struck out 25. He is 1-3 with a 4.40 ERA in seven starts on the road as opposed to 4-0 with a 4.86 ERA at home. Left-handed hitters are batting just .262 off him while right-handers are hitting .342. He is 6-3 with a 3.48 ERA in 10 starts in his career vs. the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Gabbard earned his second win of the season and first since April 4 with a 13-3 victory over the Nationals on Saturday. He is now 1-1 with a 5.73 ERA in two starts since returning from a two-start trip to Triple-A Oklahoma. In 11 innings, he has allowed 14 hits and five walks while striking out nine. He is 0-1 with a 5.63 ERA in three starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington this year. He has never faced the Phillies in his short career.
away_pitcher_note: A promising Saturday outing for Myers was damaged by the righty's propensity for surrendering home runs. Of the six hits Myers allowed in seven innings, three were home runs. Myers' total of 23 home runs allowed leads the Major Leagues. Myers has never faced the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla is facing the Phillies for the first time since they traded him to the Rangers after the 2005 season. Padilla pitched for the Phillies from 2000-05 and was 49-49 with a 3.98 ERA in 162 games, including 111 starts. He enters the game with a record of 8-1 with a 3.28 ERA in his last 11 games. He is 3-2 with a 3.00 ERA in six starts at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels had a quality start Sunday against the Angels that was spoiled by a lack of Phillies offense. In seven innings, Myers allowed three runs on six hits while striking out four in taking the loss. Still, the Phils are 10-6 this season when Hamels has taken the hill. His outing against the Rangers will be his third consecutive start against an American League team that he has never before faced.

home_pitcher_note: Hurley lost to the Astros, 4-3, on Tuesday despite allowing just two runs in six innings. In three Major League starts, opponents are hitting .258 off him with 17 hits in 17 innings. He has walked five, struck out nine and allowed three home runs. Opponents are just 1-for-14 off him leading off an inning. Left-handed hitters are batting .242 off him while right-handers are hitting .273 off him.
away_pitcher_note: One bad pitch ruined a brilliant start for Moyer against the A's. He entered the seventh inning having allowed one hit through the first six innings, and striking out nine. Two bloop singles and a three-run home run by Emil Brown handed him a loss. In 13 career starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, the lefty is 4-5 with a 5.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Mussina was cut short in his last start on Thursday in Pittsburgh, and he was not happy about it. The right-hander passed the point of no return with 46 pitches against the Pirates before a lengthy rain delay and lightning storm wiped out his start. Mussina will instead draw the Rangers, as he goes for his 11th victory of the season. Mussina is 4-1 with a 3.69 ERA in his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman lasted just four innings, his shortest outing as a starter, against the Astros on Wednesday at Minute Maid Park. He is 0-2 with a 4.88 ERA in his past eight starts. He is 0-3 with a 6.91 ERA in five starts on the road this year and 0-7 with a 6.72 ERA in his career away from Arlington. He has made just one relief appearance in his career against the Yankees, pitching one-third of an inning.

home_pitcher_note: In five starts, Chamberlain has a 1.80 ERA with 26 strikeouts in 25 innings. The Yankees' 10-0 win against Pittsburgh on Wednesday gave the 22-year-old righty his first victory as a starter. The 114 pitches he threw against the Pirates -- 76 for strikes -- over 6 2/3 innings were the most he's tossed since his days at the University of Nebraska.
away_pitcher_note: Hurley came off the disabled list on Sunday and lost to the Athletics, 6-5, at McAfee Coliseum. He allowed six runs in two innings, giving up two home runs. The velocity and location of his fastball was off. He is 1-0 with a 2.53 ERA in two starts at home. Opponents are hitting .212 after an 0-1 count and .308 after a 1-0 count. This is his sixth Major League start and first against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: How's this for symmetry? Ponson's next probable turn would come against the Rangers, the same club that unceremoniously released him after off-the-field incidents made the organization question his desire. The Yankees would have little reason to not keep Ponson in the rotation after the right-hander hurled six innings of scoreless, five-hit ball against the Mets on Friday at Shea Stadium. Ponson walked four and struck out four in the outing.
away_pitcher_note: Since returning from the disabled list on June 20, Mendoza has done everything asked of him out of the bullpen and then some. In his last three appearances, he's thrown eight innings of shutout baseball. He earned a save in his first outing and a victory in the second. His last time out, he retired three of the four Phillies batters he faced. Since coming off the DL, Mendoza has six strikeouts compared to four hits allowed and no walks. Wednesday will mark Mendoza's first start against the Yankees and the Rangers' final regular-season game at Yankee Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie has pitched much better this season than his 4-7 record would indicate, his last start being a perfect example of this. Guthrie gave up one run early to the Nationals on Sunday, but then settled down and kept Washington off the board for the rest of his outing. The Orioles offense, however, couldn't seem to get on the board themselves -- making Guthrie once again the victim of poor run support -- in an eventual 3-2 extra-innings loss to the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla's All-Star chances took a blow in his last outing, as he surrendered seven runs in six innings to the Phillies.
