He allowed seven hits in the game, including two home runs, while walking as many as he struck out -- three. All the while, his ERA jumped 39 points from 3.74. Padilla will start the series opener in Baltimore, which will be his first game against the Orioles this season. He's 2-3 in his career against Baltimore with a 5.70 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a recurring stomach illness that forced him to miss his scheduled start on June 25 at Wrigley Field, Burres rebounded nicely by pitching five innings against the Royals and giving up five hits and just one earned run. After two rough outings to begin the month of June, Burres has been pitching better of late, throwing at least five innings in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman beat the Yankees, 2-1, on Monday by holding them to one run on four hits in 52/3 innings for his first victory ever on the road. He is 1-3 with a 6.00 ERA in six road starts this year. He went 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA in six starts in June but has a 2.70 ERA in his last three starts. He has a 1.93 ERA in three career relief appearances against the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: Liz moved his record to 3-0 at the Major League level his last time out, a 7-5 win over the Royals. Liz threw 80 pitches, 55 for strikes, over six innings, getting his first quality start of the season and earning the praise of manager Dave Trembley, who said it was the best Liz had looked all season. Liz allowed just three earned runs in the starts, although two were solo home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood held the Yankees to one run in five innings in his last start on Tuesday but left the game with a bruised right shin. He was hit there by Robinson Cano's ground ball in the second inning. Millwood is 1-4 with a 4.92 ERA in nine starts on the road and opponents are hitting .341 off him. Left-handed hitters are hitting .349 off him this season while right-handers are batting .279. He is 3-1 with a 4.93 ERA in seven starts since coming off the disabled list with a strained groin muscle. He is 8-2 with a 3.29 ERA in 11 career starts against the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: Yankees executive VP Hank Steinbrenner inspired the offense at just the wrong time for Mendoza. After pitching a scoreless first inning in Texas' final regular-season game at Yankee Stadium, Mendoza gave up a run in the second. It was his only earned run allowed, but the first of many runs. Mendoza allowed a grand slam the next inning after a Texas error extended the inning and New York scratched another run off him in the fifth thanks in part to an error. In addition to those six runs, Mendoza allowed four hits and two walks and didn't record a strikeout in 4 2/3 innings. Mendoza will now face the Angels, whom he's made one start against in his career, lasting 4 2/3 innings that outing, as well.
away_pitcher_note: Santana delivered another solid effort -- seven innings, two earned runs, seven strikeouts -- against the A's on Tuesday night without a decision. He was in trouble early but controlled damage, then threw five scoreless innings to keep the Angels in a game they won. His 106 strikeouts against 30 walks reflect how superb his command has been all season, his mid-90s fastball complemented by an improving slider and changeup. He beat the Rangers in Texas on April 14, yielding three earned runs in seven innings. He's 6-1 on the road with a 3.36 ERA, erasing the stigma of his road problems last season.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old left-handed Harrison has made a quick rise through the Rangers' system, earning Tuesday's start against the Angels. Harrison, who came over in last year's Mark Teixiera trade with Altanta, has split time between Double-A Frisco and Triple-A Oklahoma this season, and is a combined 6-3 with a 3.43 ERA in 15 starts -- 84 innings -- this season. He allowed one earned run in six innings in his last outing on July 3. He had five strikeouts and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders didn't have his best stuff on Wednesday against the A's, but he got the job done as he allowed four runs, two earned, on six hits while striking out five and walking two. His 12 wins before the All-Star Game are the most by an Angel since Chuck Finley and Mark Langston each had 12 wins before the break in 1991. He is 2-2 with a 6.08 ERA against the Rangers in his career, but hasn't faced them this season.

home_pitcher_note: Rather than call up Michael Ballard from Double-A, the Rangers have chosen to go with an all-bullpen look for this game. Whether or not they simply pulled a name out of a hat, Madrigal will make the start and the club hopes to get a couple of innings out of him before turning to Josh Rupe and Jamey Wright. Since allowing six runs in one-third of an inning to the Yankees on July 2, Madrigal has had two scoreless relief appearances, covering a span of three innings. His last appearance was in the series opener with the Angels, in which he went two-thirds of an inning, walking one.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver had great stuff for his third straight outing as he pitched seven scoreless innings before allowing two runs in the eighth. Weaver allowed just six hits, two coming in the eighth inning, in 7 1/3 innings and struck out six. The right-hander has now allowed just three earned runs and 10 hits in his previous three starts. Weaver is 2-1 with a 2.36 ERA in seven career starts against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 2-0 with a 3.18 ERA in his last four starts, winning against both New York and Baltimore on the road. He is 1-0 with a 3.20 ERA in eight games, including six starts, at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, where he has held opponents to a .227 batting average. Opponents are hitting .240 off him with runners in scoring position, but just .188 in those situations when there are two out. He has a 2.89 ERA in nine relief appearances in his career against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is coming off his first subpar performance of the season, yielding six runs (five earned) in six innings against the Blue Jays on Saturday night. His stuff was alive (seven strikeouts) and his command (one walk) wasn't bad, but the Jays took advantage of breaking balls left up in the hitting zone in banging out seven hits, including a two-run homer by Vernon Wells. It was the first time Lackey has yielded more than three runs in 10 outings. He's 9-8 with a 5.21 ERA in 23 career outings against the Rangers and 4-5 with a 6.24 ERA at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Mendoza never got comfortable in Monday's 9-6 Rangers loss to the Angels, allowing eight runs in 1 1/3 innings. The rookie right-hander said he felt great in the bullpen, but when he got on the mound, his mechanics and location were off. He allowed three home runs and nine hits. Mendoza is 0-3 with a 6.60 ERA in five starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Entering the 2008 season, Floyd had a rather inauspicious 8-10 career record with a disastrous 6.30 ERA. Following Saturday's dominant effort against Oakland, Floyd improved to 10-4 and watched his ERA drop to 3.22 in 2008 alone. Yes, it has been a coming-of-age effort for the right-hander. Floyd pitched scoreless baseball for 7 1/3 innings against Oakland, giving up three hits and three walks, while fanning six. Floyd has one career no-decision against the Rangers, working six innings and allowing three runs on six hits, while striking out four and walking two. This start came at the Rangers' home ballpark, as will his final first-half trip to the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood wasn't at his best in Baltimore his last time out, but he was good enough to earn his second road victory of the season. In five innings he allowed five runs, three earned, on nine hits and struck out two. However, the offense and bullpen kept him in line for the victory. Millwood is now 4-1 in eight starts since coming off the disabled list. Millwood will face the White Sox for the first time this season. He's 1-2 against Chicago in seven career starts despite having a 2.15 ERA, 1.09 WHIP and .229 batting average against in 46 innings.
away_pitcher_note: If not for pitching through an amazing eight no-decisions in 18 starts this season, Danks probably would have been a 2008 All-Star. Danks was impressive once again during Sunday's effort against Oakland, allowing two runs on four hits over 6 1/3 innings. The left-hander no-hit the A's through five innings and struck out a career-high nine in the victory. The Texas native and one-time top pick of the Rangers has faced his former team on just one prior occasion. Danks suffered a loss last year in Texas, allowing five runs on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings, with just two of those runs being earned.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison's numbers weren't astounding in his Major League debut, but he gave the Rangers just what they needed. Called up from Triple-A Oklahoma to start in place of Eric Hurley, who was placed on the DL with a strained left hamstring, Harrison went seven innings and allowed just two runs on five hits and a walk while striking out one. He faced the minimum in five different innings. It was the longest outing for a Rangers pitcher in his Major League debut since August, 2000. Harrison will try to put together another solid start in his first meeting with the White Sox Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: A no-decision was no doubt fine with Contreras in his last outing, which came on Tuesday against Kansas City. He gave up five runs in six-plus innings and never seemed in control. By the third inning, he had thrown nearly 70 pitches. In two July starts, he has two no-decisions. It's been better than his June, when he went 2-3 with a 6.83 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins was one of the surprises for the Twins in the first half. The left-hander provided nine quality starts in his 13 tries before the All-Star break. His ability to pitch inside and challenge hitters has been a welcome addition, and the Twins will need to see more of that in the second half. He'll face Texas in his first post-break appearance. He gave up two earned runs over 6 1/3 innings in his lone start vs. Texas this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers need an improved second half from Millwood, who didn't get past the sixth inning in any of his last four starts. Millwood allowed 10 hits and five runs in Saturday's 9-7 loss to the Chicago White Sox. Millwood did a nice break after struggling with a groin injury the last few weeks. He has struggled against the Twins the last three years, going 0-4 with a 5.59 ERA. Millwood has pitched better against the Twins in the Metrodome, where he is 0-2 with a 2.81 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: It was a rough finish to the first half for the lone veteran of the Twins staff. The right-hander gave up six runs in 4 1/3 innings to the Red Sox at Fenway Park. A pleasant surprise early in the season, Hernandez is looking to rebound from some recent difficult starts. Most of that trouble has come on the road where Hernandez holds a 7.48 ERA on the season. Despite his woes, the Twins are 13-7 in Hernandez's starts. Next up is a start against Texas. He's 0-1 with a 13.50 ERA in two starts vs. the Rangers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison struggled with his command in his previous start against the White Sox, allowing five runs in 2 2/3 innings. He had trouble throwing his slider for strikes, and allowed Chicago to tee off on his fastball for seven hits and a home run. Harrison will be making his third Major League start.

home_pitcher_note: Baker continues to emerge as the true ace of the Twins staff. Although he gave up four runs over seven innings to the Tigers his last time out, it was the first time in nine starts that Baker had allowed more than three earned runs in an outing. Now that the right-hander is healthy, he's expected to have an even bigger impact on the club's rotation in the second half. The Twins were 9-5 in Baker's 14 starts in the first half. He'll now face Texas in his first start after the All-Star break. He picked up a no-decision after giving up five runs in 4 1/3 innings in his lone start vs. the Rangers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla has been on the disabled list with neck stiffness. No, it's not from the 15 earned runs he's allowed in his last two starts. The Rangers are hoping the Padilla that does comes back is the one for most of the first half that was one of the most consistent starters in the American League. Padilla had allowed three earned runs or less in six of his last eight starts before his recent hiccup.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez will endure the longest layoff between starts of Chicago's starters, going 12 days since his start on July 9 at Kansas City. That outing, Vazquez was tagged for six runs on 11 hits in 5 2/3 innings, but he avoided taking a loss. In addition to the nearly two weeks between starts for Vazquez, he hasn't earned a victory in over a month -- June 17 against Pittsburgh. He's allowed at least four runs in all but one start since June 6. He'll be thrown right back into the fire for his first start of the season against Texas' high-powered offense. Vazquez is 2-1 in four career starts against the Rangers, despite posting a 6.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Eric Hurley was scratched with a sore arm, so the Rangers tabbed Feldman to take his place. After compiling mostly solid numbers in May and June, Feldman had a rough start to July. He was scheduled to return as a member of the bullpen, but instead will step right into the starting rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle made one mistake in his start on Friday night against the Royals. His 1-0 offering to Billy Butler in the sixth inning traveled 431 feet over the left-field wall for a three-run homer. Fortunately for Buehrle, the White Sox still had a three-run lead. The left-hander allowed just four hits and four runs, three of which were earned, in seven innings of work. It was his first win in his past three starts, and one that moved him past Joel Horlen into seventh place on the White Sox all-time victories list. Buehrle has not faced the Rangers this season, but is 9-3 with a 2.97 ERA lifetime against them. He will be working on three days' rest, moving up one day because he will return to Missouri on Wednesday for his grandfather's funeral. The White Sox did not want Buehrle to miss his turn in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Mendoza will come right back and face the Chicago White Sox after allowing only a run in six innings in a 7-2 victory over the Sox on July 11. The Rangers want to see more of the pitcher that challenged hitters in that game. Mendoza had eight strikeouts after not recording any in his previous start against the Angels, a game in which he allowed eight runs in 1 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander, who once played quarterback for the University of Michigan, makes his Major League debut during Wednesday afternoon's series finale. Richard will be taking the spot of Jose Contreras, placed on the disabled list with right elbow tendinitis. Richard posted a 12-6 record with a 2.44 ERA between stops this season at Double-A Birmingham and Triple-A Charlotte. He won all six of his starts for the Knights, striking out 29 and walking just four over 38 innings, while producing a 2.47 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood continued his career-long difficulty against Minnesota on Friday, going 6 1/3 innings while allowing five earned runs on 11 hits in the 6-0 Rangers loss. Millwood is now 0-6 career against the Twins. Millwood will next take on the White Sox. He allowed 10 hits and five earned runs in 5 1/3 innings against Chicago on July 12, a 9-7 Rangers loss.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher is slated to make his 13th start of the season and his third with Oakland since being traded in a six-player deal with the Cubs on July 8. The right-hander garnered no decision in Saturday's 4-3, 12-inning loss in New York, allowing two runs in five innings off seven hits. He picked up his first win in an A's uniform on July 11, tossing seven innings of two-hit ball. This will be his first career start against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla returned from the disabled list on Sunday and pitched a gem after being shelved with neck stiffness. The veteran right-hander threw seven innings of shutout ball against the Twins, allowing only three hits. Padilla didn't allow a runner past first base. He was originally scheduled to pitch Saturday, but was switched to pitch the first game of the A's series. He was victorious against Oakland on May 2, going 5 2/3 innings, while giving up one earned run on five hits and four walks in a 4-3 Rangers victory.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer took a tough-luck loss against the Yankees on Sunday afternoon. The right-hander threw seven innings on a hot day despite feeling under the weather from a viral infection. He gave up six hits and two runs to a patient Yankees lineup, and the righty said he felt tired by the time he left the game. He has held opponents to two runs or fewer in 11 straight starts, pitching at least six innings in each outing. In his last start against Texas, on May 30, Duchscherer allowed two runs and six hits in a 3-1 Oakland loss.
away_pitcher_note: Since an impressive debut, Harrison has been hit hard in his last two starts. Against Chicago and Minnesota, the lefty allowed a total of 13 runs in 7 2/3 innings. On Saturday facing the Twins, he gave up eight earned runs in five innings en route to a 14-2 Rangers loss. Harrison will next make his fourth career Major League start, facing the A's on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: The left-handed Eveland fell to 7-7 after taking Monday night's series-opening loss against Tampa Bay. Eveland was twice victimized by the long ball, and the Rays turned two of their three stolen bases -- in three attempts -- into runs. Eveland has lost his only decision against Texas, and has a 4.50 ERA from that five-inning contest.
away_pitcher_note: If Hurley is feeling well enough to pitch, he'll start Sunday's finale against Oakland. Hurley was supposed to come off the 15-day disabled list to start for the Rangers on Monday against Chicago. He felt soreness in his throwing arm, so the Rangers decided to play it safe and have Scott Feldman start instead. Hurley said the left hamstring injury that landed him on the DL on July 8 has recovered and he will be ready for his next turn in the rotation. The rookie right-hander has not faced Oakland this season.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman will be making his second spot start of the month. Texas optioned Feldman to the Minors earlier in the month to keep his innings down, but he was called upon last Monday to fill in for Eric Hurley. Feldman came through in the start, going six innings and holding the White Sox to one run while earning the victory. This time around, he'll be replacing Kevin Millwood, who is out with a pulled groin. Monday will mark Feldman's second start of the season against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander had to work especially hard to keep the Mariners in their series finale against the Red Sox, finally departing after 108 pitches over six innings -- including 31 in the sixth, when he loaded the bases with none out and escaped with just one run being scored. Felix walked a season-high five, but the Red Sox are known to force opposing pitchers into high pitch counts. Hernandez is 0-1 in two starts against the Rangers this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Rangers haven't officially announced who will start Tuesday's game against Seattle, but Mendoza will have already been skipped in the rotation, so he will likely get the nod. If not, the Rangers could look to Scott Feldman. It all depends on how healthy Kevin Millwood is Monday. If he can't go, either Mendoza or Feldman could get the nod Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Silva was scratched from his last start against the Blue Jays because of tightness in his lower back. The right-hander informed manager Jim Riggleman he could have started on Monday, but the club opted to err on the side of caution and give Silva an extra day of rest. The tightness in his lower back is the same injury that forced Silva to leave after three innings against the Indians on July 20. Silva is 4-4 with a 4.11 ERA in his career against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla was without his best stuff in his last start against Oakland, but he got plenty of offensive support -- 14 runs on 17 hits to be exact -- to tally the victory. In six innings of work, he allowed five runs on seven hits while walking four and fanning nine A's batters. In three starts against Seattle this year, Padilla is 1-0 with a 2.00 ERA. He is just three victories shy of tying his career-high win count of 15 in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Batista surrendered a run in each of the first two innings during his last start against the Blue Jays but quickly settled down and finished with a strong performance. The early runs were the only ones Batista would surrender over 5 1/3 innings. He allowed five hits while walking two before being forced to depart after 82 pitches because of fatigue. He appeared set to win his fifth game of the season but Seattle's bullpen was unable to hold the lead and as a result he was forced to take the no decision. The 37-year-old is 4-4 with a 5.12 ERA in 13 career appearances against the Rangers. Texas shortstop Michael Young has caused him the most difficulty, hitting .400 (8-for-20) with four RBIs in his career against the veteran righty.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison beat the Athletics, 9-4, on Saturday, allowing three runs (one earned) in five innings. He beat Justin Duchscherer, who entered the game with the lowest ERA in the American League. His other victory came against Angels All-Star left-hander Joe Saunders. This is his fifth start for the Rangers since being promoted from Triple-A Oklahoma.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey will return to the Ballpark in Arlington to face the team which drafted him in the first round during the 1996 Draft. He was a conventional fastball/breaking-ball pitcher earlier in his career with Rangers but now uses a knuckleball as his main weapon. Dickey made his last start on just three days' rest against the Blue Jays. He allowed a run during every inning he pitched and finished his 5 1/3 innings of work with eight earned runs on 10 hits while issuing four walks. With the loss, Dickey's record as a starter fell to 1-6 with a 6.06 ERA and it was the fifth time he has allowed four or more runs in an outing this season. This will be the first time he has faced the Rangers during his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter, who is in his first full professional season and began the season at Class A Bakersfield, will be promoted from Triple-A Oklahoma to make a spot start for Eric Hurley. Hurley is being skipped this trip through the rotation with tendinitis in his right biceps and is expected to make his next scheduled start. In five starts at Oklahoma, Hunter is 2-2 with a 3.24 ERA over 33 1/3 innings. He recorded 17 strikeouts to four walks in Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum did not fare well against the Mariners in his last start. The Toronto right-hander allowed four runs on six hits over 5 2/3 innings. He struck out two and walked three, collecting the loss in his second start since returning from the disabled list with a strained right elbow. In five career appearances against the Rangers, he is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman went six innings for the 12th time in 16 starts this season his last time out, but they weren't his most memorable. After having allowed four total home runs in his previous seven outings, he served up three home runs to the Mariners. However, at one point he'd retired 14 of 16 batters faced and he had four strikeouts to one walk -- compared to his 14/13 K/BB rate entering the start. Feldman has yet to figure in a decision against the Blue Jays in three career games, including a six-inning start on April 13.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett dominated the Rays in his last start to earn his 12th victory of the season, which matches a career high. The hard-throwing right-hander allowed one unearned run on six hits over seven innings. He walked four batters while striking out 10, needing 110 pitches to get through the outing. Over his past four starts, Burnett has gone 3-1 with a 1.32 ERA. In his career against the Rangers, Burnett is 0-2 with a 4.40 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: On the bright side, Mendoza went at least five innings for the third time this season -- and the second time in his last three starts. However, he also allowed six runs for the fourth time in his last five starts. As a result, his ERA has spiked nearly three points from 4.64. Against the Mariners his last time out, Mendoza allowed six runs, five earned, on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings. Nevertheless, he said all of his pitches were working for him. Mendoza will next face the Jays, against whom he took a loss in his first start of the season. He allowed four runs, one earned, in five innings in that outing.
away_pitcher_note: Purcey beat the Mariners in his last start to earn his first Major League win. The left-hander allowed three runs on seven hits over six innings. He walked one and struck out four, needing 99 pitches to get through the outing. With starter Dustin McGowan gone for the season, the Jays have indicated that Purcey will see time in the Jays rotation for at least the foreseeable future. He has never faced Texas before and on Friday, the 26-year-old former first-round pick will be making his fourth career appearance in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla was nibbled on by the Mariners in his last start. In seven innings, he allowed 10 hits -- nine of which singles -- and three runs and earned a no-decision. The outing was Padilla's first without receiving a decision in nine starts, going back to May 22. Since coming off the disabled list on July 20, Padilla is 2-0 with a 3.60 ERA, pitching 20 innings over three starts. His start Monday will be his first this season against the Yankees. Padilla is 1-1 with a 5.23 ERA in only two career starts against New York.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first appearance since he bested the Red Sox in his finest starting performance to date, Chamberlain limited Baltimore to two runs (one earned) over six innings Wednesday to post his second victory in as many starts. The 22-year-old scattered five hits while walking none and striking out six; New York has now won eight of Chamberlain's 11 big league starts. His only start against Texas was rough, a four-inning outing July 1 in which he allowed two runs, five hits and four walks over 91 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison's starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington have been declining. After winning his Major League debut at home, allowing two runs in seven innings to the Angels, he's had more runs allowed than innings pitched in his last two home outings. In his most recent, he allowed six runs -- four earned -- to the Mariners in 4 2/3 innings and he walked five. "I try to concentrate on keeping the ball down here, but you don't want to put it in the dirt," he said. Harrison took the loss, giving him a 12.41 ERA in his two losses this season. Harrison will have the opportunity to improve his home numbers Tuesday in his first career start against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte completed his evening Thursday charged with nine runs on a season-high 11 hits over 5 1/3 innings. He walked three and struck out two, losing for just the third time in his last 14 starts. In 19 career starts against Texas, Pettitte is 9-7 with a 5.36 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter's Major League debut was one he should have no problem improving upon. At home against the Blue Jays, Hunter allowed six runs on eight hits and two walks and he struck out four. He found out the hard way just how easily balls can fly out of Rangers Ballpark, allowing a three-run home run to Scott Rolen in the second and a two-run home run to Lyle Overbay in the third. Now that Hunter knows what to expect from his home park and Major League hitters, he'll brave the hitter-friendly elements of Ranger Ballpark again in his next start against a Yankees lineup that doesn't figure to be pitcher-friendly.
away_pitcher_note: Though he earned a no-decision, Ponson stuck with the Angels' Ervin Santana on Friday and matched him zero for zero through seven innings. Making his sixth start this season since joining the Yankees, Ponson turned in his best performance, shutting the Angels' potent lineup out on two hits with four walks. In 16 career starts against Texas, Ponson is 8-2 with a 5.22 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman dropped back to .500 in his last start against Toronto as his ERA remained at 4.97. In 5 1/3 innings against the Blue Jays, Feldman allowed four runs, three earned, on five hits and three walks while striking out four. It was the second consecutive start he struck out more batters than he walked. In his three starts leading up to his last two, he registered 12 walks to a mere three strikeouts. Thursday will be Feldman's second meeting with the Yankees this season. The first time around, he earned the victory at Yankee Stadium, allowing just one run in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Mussina limited a red-hot Angels offense to two runs (one earned) and two hits on Saturday afternoon at Yankee Stadium. After his team fell to an early 2-0 deficit, the righty retired 16 batters in a row to keep the Halos off the bases and the scoreboard. He effectively mixed in his breaking ball to keep hitters off balance and struck out five with two walks. Mussina also pitched economically, throwing 89 pitches through seven innings. The righty picked up the tough-luck loss in his last start against Texas on June 30, giving up two runs on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie fired the first complete game of his career in his last start and has finally made it back to an even record. Baltimore's Opening Day starter ranks first in the American League in quality starts (16), second in innings pitched (156) and eighth in ERA (3.35). After starting 3-7, Guthrie has won five of his last six decisions.
away_pitcher_note:
Mendoza seems to be settling in better as a starter in the big leagues. 
He has pitched into the sixth inning for the third time in four starts. 
But what Mendoza did in Sunday's 8-4 victory over Toronto was make it through seven innings for the first time this season. He survived allowing three runs in the first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Cabrera leads the American League in walks, wild pitches and hit batsmen, and if he continues at his current pace, he'll likely lead the league in free passes for the third straight season. Cabrera struck out six in his last start, which was his highest total since mid-June. The right-hander has allowed runs in the first inning 13 times in 24 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is 2-0 with a 4.15 ERA in four starts since the All-Star break. He is working off consecutive no-decisions for the first time this season. He has pitched at least six innings in 17 of 22 starts. He had two balks in his last start against the Yankees, only the third Rangers pitcher in 20 seasons to have two balks in a game. He allowed eight runs in 2 2/3 innings in his previous start against the Orioles on July 4. He is 2-4 with a 7.86 ERA in his career against the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: Waters had one of the best Major League debuts in franchise history last week, when he one-hit the Angels over eight shutout innings. The last Oriole to have that kind of debut was Bob Milacki, who had the same statistical performance in 1988. Waters will get another look, and if he succeeds again, he may just stay in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Coming into his last start, Harrison had allowed 18 earned runs in his previous 17 1/3 innings. Against the Yankees, though, Harrison went 6 1/3 innings -- his second-longest outing of the season -- and allowed just two runs on five hits and three walks. Not once did he face more than four batters in an inning. His next start will be his first against Baltimore. In two road starts, Harrison is 1-1 with an 8.10 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The start was originally supposed to go to Tim Wakefield, but the veteran will instead go on the 15-day disabled list with a right shoulder injury. Fellow knuckleballer Charlie Zink, who is having a terrific season for Triple-A Pawtucket, will make the start on three days' rest.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman is 0-2 with a 4.91 ERA in his past three starts. This is his 19th start, and the Rangers went 6-12 in his first 18. Feldman is the only Rangers pitcher who has started at least one game and has allowed fewer hits than innings pitched. He has pitched 112 innings and allowed 109 hits. He has the second-most innings pitched on the team this year and is 3-3 with a 5.20 ERA in eight starts this season on the road. He has never started against the Red Sox but has a 1.35 ERA in four career relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Lester's unbeaten streak was halted at 11 games in his last outing, though the lefty still turned in a decent performance (seven innings, four runs) against the White Sox. At Fenway Park this season, Lester is 6-1 with a 2.87 ERA in 12 starts. Left-handers are hitting just .233 against Lester. This will be the first time Lester has faced the Rangers since April 19, when he allowed 10 hits and three runs over 6 1/3 innings. In that one, he got a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Mendoza is 1-2 with a 7.50 ERA in four starts since the All-Star break, and he is 1-3 with an 8.46 ERA on the road. Left-handed hitters are batting .352 off him, while right-handed hitters are batting .294. Opponents are hitting .381 with runners in scoring position, including .414 with two outs. He lost to the Red Sox, 11-3, on April 18 in Boston, then ended up on the disabled list with a sore shoulder.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has turned in strong performances in his past two starts, going 2-0 while allowing three earned runs over 14 innings. In Matsuzaka's last start ?- a 6-2 win over the White Sox ?- he worked a season-high eight innings. In 11 starts at Fenway Park this season, Matsuzaka is 7-2 with a 3.65 ERA. He picked up the win in his last start against the Rangers this season, on April 18, giving up five hits and three runs in 5 1/3 innings. Matsuzaka is holding opponents to a .206 average.
away_pitcher_note: Originally, Hunter was slated to have his spot in the rotation skipped this week, which would have kept him from starting against the Red Sox. Instead, a rotation reshuffling has Hunter in line to start Texas' series finale with Boston. In 9 1/3 innings, Hunter has allowed 11 earned runs. He'll be looking to improve that ratio against the same Boston lineup that posted 19 runs Tuesday night. Despite having allowed eight hits in each of his first two Major League starts, Hunter has gone right at hitters and has recorded eight strikeouts. He didn't walk a single batter in 4 1/3 innings against the Yankees his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood will be making his first start since being placed on the disabled list July 24 with a strained right groin. He made one rehab start with Double-A Frisco and allowed two runs, one earned, in four innings. He allowed five hits and two walks while striking out six. With his return to the rotation, Millwood will try to end a streak of three straight winless starts, having not earned a victory since July 6. Friday will be his first start of the season against Tampa Bay, against which he's 1-1 in three career starts, with a 6.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his 23 start of the season after earning a no-decision against the Mariners on Saturday night. Garza allowed five runs in the first two innings, but never gave in to finish his outing with 3 2/3 scoreless innings before getting lifted with the lead. Garza has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup. He is 2-1 with a 2.95 ERA in three career starts against the Rangers; he is 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA in one career start at Rangers Ballpark.

home_pitcher_note: How do you allow six runs and coast to victory? Get 12 runs of support. That's what happened to Harrison his last time out, when he allowed six runs on 10 hits and two walks in five innings against the Orioles. He also gave up two home runs, didn't record a single strikeout in the start, and saw his ERA rise from 6.46 to 7.07. Harrison will go for his third straight victory against the American League East on Friday, when the Rays come to Texas. It will be his first game against Tampa Bay.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson picked up his ninth win of the season Sunday in Seattle when he held the Mariners to one run on seven hits in seven innings worked. The 24-year-old right-hander has shown marked improvement from the 2007 season when he had a 3-11 mark on the same date as Sunday's win. If Jackson is locating his 97 mph fastball, his other pitches can work well, particularly his slider. Jackson is 1-1 with a 3.74 ERA in three career starts against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Nippert is the leading candidate to replace Luis Mendoza, who was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma on Friday. Another possibility is rookie Tommy Hunter. Nippert has pitched four innings in each of his past five outings and has a 3.98 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir took his sixth loss of the season Tuesday night when he allowed two runs in a five-inning stint against the A's. The 24-year-old left-hander has struggled with his mechanics lately and has worked all season with little luck to gain command of his slider, which has historically been his best pitch. Without his slider, Kazmir has relied primarily on a fastball-changeup combination. He is 2-0 with a 1.80 ERA in two starts against the Rangers this season, and is 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA in two career starts at Rangers Ballpark.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman -- 0-2 in his last four starts -- didn't lose his last time out in Boston, but it was his roughest start of the season. He allowed 12 runs, six earned, on 10 hits and three walks in just 2 2/3 innings as his ERA spiked from 4.82. Feldman will be looking to start Texas' series with Detroit out on the right foot. He hasn't faced the Tigers this season and has a 7.71 ERA against them in seven career innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers surrendered at least four runs for the fourth straight start his last time out, which a rain delay ended with one out in the seventh inning. He looked sharp in every inning but the fourth. A bad hop gave the Blue Jays the bases loaded with nobody out, and Vernon Wells knocked a grand slam to left. Overall, Rogers allowed four runs on seven hits and three walks in 6 1/3 innings. He has allowed a total of 19 runs in his last four starts. Against Texas, he faces the team that drafted him in the 39th round of the 1982 Draft. He pitched for the Rangers from 1989-95, 2000-02 and 2004-05.

home_pitcher_note: Originally slated to pitch on Thursday, Padilla was been pushed back to Tuesday to start against the Tigers. In his last start, Padilla allowed six runs to the Orioles in four innings as his ERA rose from 4.59. After winning five of seven starts from June 11 to July 25, he's winless in his last three.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga had one of his best outings of the season last time out against the Blue Jays. He went eight innings, allowing one run on five hits, while striking out six and walking two. He threw a season-high 121 pitches. He said after the game he couldn't remember the last time he threw that many pitches, but he added that he won't need any extra rest. Next he faces Texas, the team that traded him to the Tigers last offseason.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood came off the disabled list and allowed five runs on 10 hits and one walk in 4 2/3 innings in a 7-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays. He is 0-3 with a 9.00 ERA in his last four starts, and he is 4-2 with a 5.74 ERA in nine starts at home this season. The right-hander is 3-4 with a 4.23 ERA in nine career starts against the Tigers but will be facing them for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: Only Carlos Silva has a higher ERA among American League starters without enough innings to qualify, and Silva and Livan Hernandez are the lone AL hurlers to give up more hits. Those two stats have meant a long season for Robertson, who owns one win in his past 10 starts. The latest was a loss to the Orioles last Friday, when he gave up four earned runs on eight hits over 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: What was the most impressive stat from Harrison's last start? Take your pick. He had recorded just seven strikeouts in seven games entering the start and left after eight innings with eight strikeouts -- more than doubling his season total. Or there were the mere three baserunners he allowed -- all of which came on singles -- even though he entered the game with 19 walks against seven strikeouts. Finally, there were the 18 straight Rays he retired. Harrison is now 4-1 with a 4.03 ERA in his past five starts. Having allowed just two runs in his past two home starts, Harrison will try to continue his successful stretch at home in his first career start against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: In what has become a tough 2008 season for the young sinkerballer, there was, perhaps, something to build off in his most recent outing. Carmona went seven innings and allowed four runs (two earned) to the Angels on Saturday, but his command was better and he got back to keeping the ball on the ground, as he induced three ground-ball double plays. Carmona was the victim of some shaky defense, but he didn't do himself any favors either, uncorking two wild pitches and committing an error of his own in his fifth loss of the season. In his only outing of the season against the Rangers, Carmona lasted just two innings and gave up six runs before he was pulled with a strained hip, which would keep him on the disabled list for more than two months.

home_pitcher_note: At long last, McCarthy will join the Texas rotation. It will be his first start with the Rangers since Sept. 20 of last season, as severe right forearm inflammation has kept him on the shelf in 2008. Even after beginning a rehab assignment in July, McCarthy wasn't happy with his results. So, on Aug. 7, he made a trip to Rangers Ballpark in Arlington to meet with team president Nolan Ryan, pitching coach Andy Hawkins and bullpen coach Jim Colborn, who helped streamline McCarthy's mechanics. Since then, McCarthy has thrown 13 innings of shutout ball with 11 strikeouts and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers did his usual thing on Sunday against the Angels. He allowed two early runs to lift his first-inning ERA to 9.60 before settling down to finish with another non-flashy 6 2/3 innings of work. He allowed three runs and scattered eight hits, walking two and striking out two to collect just his second win of the season. Sowers has yet to face the Rangers in his three-year career.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching after a 10-day layoff, Padilla was solid through six innings in his last start; until the seventh, he'd allowed just one run, five hits and a walk. In the seventh, though, he allowed a walk, a single and back-to-back home runs before exiting. Padilla had been bothered by inflammation in the right side of his neck, but the righty said after the game that the pain wasn't an issue. In his past five starts, Padilla is 1-2 with a 7.14 ERA. He will look to end that trend on Sunday in his first start against Cleveland this season. It won't be easy, though. He's 2-2 in five career starts with a 7.09 ERA against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes allowed just two runs for the second consecutive outing Tuesday against the Royals, but he couldn't get past the fifth inning because of a high pitch count. His three walks contributed to that, but the long at-bats he faced in the first inning, when he threw 27 pitches, ultimately led to his early exit. He went five innings, never had a 1-2-3 inning, scattered six hits and struck out three to set himself up to be the winning pitcher. Since he was brought up from Triple-A Buffalo, Reyes has worked 17 1/3 innings and allowed five runs. Reyes has never faced the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up two early homers to the Indians last Wednesday night, Meche rebounded dramatically and retired the next 17 batters. He left after the seventh inning with a 5-3 lead but the bullpen blew the game. That ended a string of eight straight starts by Meche in which the Royals had emerged victorious. Against the Tribe, he piled up nine strikeouts and allowed only two hits (the homers) and one walk. Meche has faced the Rangers once this year, getting no decision as he went six innings and gave up just one run in what began a 6-5 loss on June 10. In his career, he's 4-8 in 15 games against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman faded at the end of his last start, but was encouraged, compared to his previous outing. Against the Red Sox on Aug. 12, he faced 22 batters and allowing 12 runs in 2 2/3 innings. Against the Tigers his last time out, though, he didn't face his 23rd batter until the seventh inning -- when he finally faltered. Through six, Feldman had held Detroit scoreless, allowing only six baserunners and striking out four batters. But he allowed the first three batters to reach in the seventh and all of whom scored as he earned a no-decision. He remains winless since July 21.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke lasted only five innings, running up 99 pitches, on Thursday at Cleveland. He insisted he made some bad pitches but he also was hurt by two errors. Those made four of the five runs charged against him unearned. In his last two games, in fact, just one of the seven runs he's given up was earned. Despite generally pitching well, he's posted just two victories in his last 10 starts. Greinke faced the Rangers on May 1 and gave up just two runs on four hits in seven innings but took the loss. Two of the hits were homers.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood said he didn't have his best stuff his last time out, but the numbers say it's the best stuff he's had in some time. Millwood threw a complete game against the Tigers, allowing just one run on six hits and a walk while he struck out four. It was his first nine-inning complete game in nearly two years, going back to late August 2006. Millwood said he was able to throw all of his pitches in the outing and locate them where he wanted, which was evident in his 80 of 113 pitches thrown for strikes. His ERA dropped 34 points in the outing. Tuesday will be Millwood's third start of the season against Kansas City. So far, he's 1-0 against the Royals and the Rangers won both times he started. However, Millwood's ERA against Kansas City this year is 7.30.

home_pitcher_note: After lasting just one-plus innings against the Yankees, Bannister rebounded to pitch eight innings on Friday night against the Tigers. But he gave up two bombs to Miguel Cabrera and wound up losing, 4-3. Despite the loss, it was a meaningful outing for Bannister, who had struggled mightily. He still hasn't won since June 23, nine starts ago. His next start will be a big test, because he's been hit hard twice by the Rangers this season, giving up 11 runs in 10 innings on 13 hits (five homers).
away_pitcher_note: Harrison's three-game winning streak had to end sometime and it did anticlimactically his last time out against Cleveland. In 3 2/3 innings, Harrison allowed five runs on seven hits and two walks as his ERA rose from 5.77. However, he did strike out more batters than he walked for the second straight game with three. Harrison also entered the start with a 1.26 ERA in his last two starts, both victories, at home. Harrison will look to get back on track on the road. He'll take his two-game road winning streak to Kansas City for his first career start against the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Garland was hurt by one bad inning against the Twins on Saturday, when he allowed four runs in the fifth . Before the fifth, he had allowed just one run on a solo homer by Alexi Casilla, but his start unraveled when he allowed three hits, a walk and a hit batter in the fifth. He lasted just 4 1/3 innings, allowing five runs on six hits while striking out one. Garland is 4-8 with a 5.87 ERA against the Rangers in 17 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy made his first start of the season on Saturday, allowing one run on three hits and four walks in four innings against the Indians. He missed most of the season with severe inflammation in his right forearm/elbow and was 1-1 with a 3.38 ERA in five starts at Triple-A Oklahoma. He is 0-1 with a 4.38 ERA in six career games against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Santana pitched well on Sunday against the Twins but was hurt by just one batter. Justin Morneau had three hits, including one home run, and drove in three runs against Santana. Santana still lasted seven innings, allowing three runs on nine hits while tying a season high by striking out 10. Santana is 6-4 with a 6.56 ERA against the Rangers in 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: With Vicente Padilla scratched due to inflammation in a muscle joint on the right side of his neck, Nippert is once again Johnny on the spot for the Rangers. Nippert's last appearance was a spot start against the Rays on Aug. 17 in which he allowed seven runs in four innings. The Rangers will be hoping instead for a similar outing to Nippert's seven-inning relief appearance on July 7 against the same Angels team he'll be facing Friday. In that outing, Nippert allowed just one run in seven innings to the Halos on four hits and a walk. However, Nippert's first appearance of the season was a brief appearance in which he allowed six runs in two-thirds of an inning to the Angels on April 4.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver turned in one of his best performances of the season on Monday against the A's but was saddled with the loss. The right-hander allowed just two runs on three hits over seven innings while striking out eight. He seemingly made just two mistakes all night, one coming on a home run he allowed to Daric Barton and another on a wild pitch that allowed a run to score from third. But the Angels could only muster one run against the A's and Weaver took the hard-luck loss. Weaver is 2-1 with a 2.26 ERA in eight career starts against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman, in the Rangers' 9-4 victory on Monday, held the Royals to three runs in seven innings to earn his first victory in over a month. He did not walk a batter. Feldman was 0-2 with a 6.33 ERA in his last five starts since beating the White Sox on July 21 and the Rangers had lost all five of those games. But his last two outings have been officially classified as "quality starts" and he leads the staff with 12 on the season. Feldman is 0-1 with a 7.62 ERA in 10 career appearances against the Angels, his highest ERA against any American League team.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey was just two outs away from a complete-game shutout against the A's on Tuesday but Jack Cust ruined his shutout bid with a solo home run in the ninth inning. It was the only blemish for Lackey, who didn't allow any other extra-base hits and outside of the homer he allowed just one runner to reach second base. The big right-hander has allowed just two earned runs over 17 innings in his previous two starts. Lackey is 9-8 with a 5.39 ERA against the Rangers in 24 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood has pitched two consecutive complete games in beating the Tigers and the Royals and is now 2-2 with a 4.50 ERA in five starts since the All-Star break. Left-handers are hitting .276 off him, while right-handers are hitting .360. He is 3-5 with a 4.92 ERA in 13 starts on the road. He is 0-1 with a 4.15 ERA in two starts against the Angels this year and 2-3 with a 3.72 ERA in nine starts against them in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison beat the Royals, 3-2, on Wednesday by holding them to two runs in 6 2/3 innings. He possesses good fastball command but must mix in his slider and changeup. He is 5-2 with a 4.35 ERA in his last seven starts but one of those losses was to the Mariners in Arlington on July 31, when he allowed six runs in 42/3 innings. He is 3-2 with a 5.01 ERA at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: On Monday, Silva will make his first start since he was put on the disabled list two weeks ago with right triceps tendinitis. Silva felt soreness in his elbow after his last start, which came on Aug. 15 against his former team, the Twins. The Mariners were feeling a little sore after the outing as well. The 29-year-old right-hander was rocked for nine hits and nine runs in 3 1/3 innings to take his 14th loss of the season. In the five starts before we went on the DL for the fourth time of his career, Silva racked up an 11.39 ERA and had struck out as many as he had walked. In three starts against the Rangers this season, Silva is 1-0 with a 5.17 ERA. Lifetime, he is 4-4 with a 4.76 ERA in 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has made two starts since being recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma. In his last start, against the Angels, he allowed two runs (one earned) in six innings, but the Rangers blew a 5-2 lead and he was left with no-decision. McCarthy is 3-4 with a 3.94 ERA in 14 career games, including 13 starts, at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington. He is 0-2 with a 9.28 ERA in four games, including two career starts, against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Feierabend looked solid against the Twins on Wednesday, when he went seven innings and gave up three earned runs while striking out four. He got stronger as the game went along and made a vast improvement upon his last time out against the Twins, on Aug. 17, when he gave up six earned runs in three innings. Two out of Feierabend's three starts since he came up for that first Twins game have been solid, and he's walked only three batters in 15 innings, while striking out 10.

home_pitcher_note: Nippert is filling in for Vicente Padilla, who is on the disabled list with a strained left hamstring. Nippert is 0-2 with a 9.64 ERA in two starts after losing to the Angels, 3-1, on Friday. He took a two-hit shutout into the sixth before growing tired and allowing three runs. Opponents are hitting .329 off him, including .357 with runners in scoring position. He allowed two runs in 4 1/3 innings in a relief appearance against the Mariners earlier this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez found trouble in nearly every inning against the Indians on Friday night. Though Hernandez never recored a 1-2-3 inning, he was still able to leave on top after six innings, allowing just two runs on six hits. Ground-ball double plays got him out of jams in the first two innings before the Indians cracked him for single runs in the third and fourth innings, respectively. Still, with the Tribe putting its first two runners on base in those particular innings, Hernandez showed enough poise to minimize the damage and keep the Mariners on top throughout his entire outing. In four starts against the Rangers this season, Hernandez is 0-2 with a 3.38 ERA. Lifetime, he is 4-6 with a 4.24 ERA in 14 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood has won three straight starts with a 1.46 ERA and has allowed one walk in his last 242/3 innings. He pitched two consecutive complete game victories against the Tigers and Royals, then beat the Angels on Sunday by allowing two runs in 6 2/3 innings. He is 5-2 with a 4.98 ERA in 10 starts at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: If everything goes according to manager Terry Francona's plans, Beckett will come off the 15-day disabled list and pitch Friday against the Rangers. Beckett's last appearance was on Aug. 17, a sub-par outing against the Blue Jays at Fenway Park in which he allowed eight runs on eight hits in just 2 1/3 innings. But after visiting esteemed orthopedist Dr. James Andrews on Friday, the Sox's ace seemed confident and more than ready to get back into the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison threw two flawless innings his last time out, which makes the other 3 2/3 that much more disappointing. In 5 2/3 innings, Harrison allowed five runs (four earned) on 10 hits, despite not walking a batter for the second time this season and striking out three. Harrison was handed a two-run lead going into the sixth, but turned around and allowed a run on three hits before getting pulled. He wasn't alone, as the Mariners tacked on 10 more hits and seven more runs off the bullpen. Harrison will try to lower his 5.26 home ERA Sunday against the Red Sox, whom he has yet to face.
away_pitcher_note: Wakefield did his part against the mighty White Sox lineup his last time out, holding Chicago to three runs on six hits in six innings of work on Sunday. After allowing two runs in the first, Wakefield blanked the South Siders over the next four innings -- giving Boston more than enough leeway to claim victory. Unfortunately for the veteran knuckleballer, the Sox were unable to get their bats going and he suffered the loss. Wakefield takes on Texas this time around, a team he defeated in a 6-5 win on April 20.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy earned his first Major League victory in more than a year on Tuesday. He allowed just two runs in six innings on four hits. He struck out four and walked none against a Mariners lineup that had scored 12 runs the night before. The victory was not only his first in three starts for the Rangers this season, but it was also his first since July 31 of last season. Sunday will mark McCarthy's first start against an American League East team this season. He's 1-2 in his career against Boston with a 5.21 ERA in six appearances, including three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd allowed three homers in his last outing against the Orioles, but all of them were solo shots. It was a night where balls were moving particularly smoothly through the Boston night at Fenway Park, and Byrd's offense provided enough fire power to earn the right-hander a 6-4 victory. Byrd is now 7-1 since July 21. He'll make his next start against the Rangers, a team he's yet to face in the 2008 campaign.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez gets another shot at the Rangers and his 10th victory of the season in the series opener against Texas. The right-hander surrendered a run in the first inning on Wednesday in Arlington, and it ended up being the only run of the game, as the ace lost his ninth game of the season. Hernandez has made 16 quality starts this season, but he lost two of them and settled for a no-decision in seven others. Only three other starting pitchers in the American League have received less run support than Hernandez this season, and one of them is teammate Jarrod Washburn. Pitching a shutout might be just the thing Hernandez must do to become Seattle's first double-digit winner in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is coming off the disabled list after being sidelined with both a strained left hamstring and inflammation in a muscle joint between his right shoulder and neck. The inflammation has been a problem for most of the second half and he is 0-2 with a 7.71 ERA in his last four starts. He is 9-3 with a 5.33 ERA on the road this year and 3-5 with a 4.86 ERA in 13 games, including 11 starts, against the Mariners in his career.

home_pitcher_note: After making 26 relief appearances this season, the rookie left-hander gets his first MLB start in the series finale. It's unlikely that he will pitch the necessary five innings to qualify for a win because the game plan is to make this a "Bullpen Day," with relievers needing the work getting to pitch one or two innings apiece. Jimenez has gone as far as four innings in relief, but that was more than a month ago and his arm is not stretched out enough to throw 60-some pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood had a three-game winning streak snapped when he lost to the Red Sox, 8-1, on Friday, allowing seven runs in six innings. He is now 3-3 with a 4.78 ERA in seven starts since the All-Star break while missing time because of a strained groin muscle. He is 4-5 with a 4.74 ERA on the road this year. Opponents are batting .312 off him, including .359 by right-handed hitters. He is 7-8 with a 4.51 ERA in his career against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Despite not feeling 100 percent in his last start, Braden turned in a performance that was good enough to result in his fifth win of the season. Braden was buoyed by 11 runs of support -- five of which came on bases-loaded walks surrendered by Orioles pitchers -- but he was able to get through five innings, allowing just one earned run on four hits and one walk. Braden tallied three strikeouts and said after the game that he felt good enough physically that he could have potentially gone deeper into the game. Braden is 1-0 this season against the Tigers. In his start against Detroit on Aug. 8, Braden held the Tigers to two runs on five hits and one walk over seven innings en route to a 4-2 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Nippert earned a spot in the Rangers' rotation for the month of September by pitching seven scoreless innings in a 1-0 victory over the Mariners on Wednesday. He allowed seven hits, did not walk a batter and struck out four. He is now 1-2 with a 5.51 ERA in three starts. He has a 9.55 ERA on the road. He made one relief appearance earlier this year against the Athletics at home and pitched four scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Smith provided what manager Bob Geren called his best performance in a long time -- seven innings of three-hit, five-walk, scoreless ball against the Orioles en route to a 5-1 victory. It was the left-hander's first win since Aug. 21 but just his second since June 30. Smith still had some problems with control, walking five, but he was able to keep the Orioles away from home plate. Moving to the middle of the rubber, from the first-base side, has helped the left-hander improve his control a bit, as has the more frequent incorporation of his breaking ball.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison beat the Red Sox, 15-8, on Sunday by allowing four runs in six innings, and he is now 5-1 with a 4.79 ERA in his past seven starts. He is 3-1 with a 6.65 ERA in four starts on the road. One of those victories came against the Athletics on July 26. Pitching against Justin Duchscherer, Harrison allowed three runs, one earned, in five innings, and the Rangers won, 9-4. Opponents are hitting .304 off him.

home_pitcher_note: Outman will make his first big league start. He has made two relief appearances since being called up from Triple-A Sacramento on Sept. 2.
away_pitcher_note: On Saturday, Feldman will make his first start since Aug. 30 and probably his final start of the season. He has thrown 133 2/3 innings for the Rangers this season and another 12 2/3 innings in the Minor Leagues. The Rangers would like to cut him off before he overdoes it in his first full season as a starter. He is 1-3 with a 5.63 ERA in his past seven starts. He is 4-4 with a 5.64 ERA in 11 starts on the road, and he is 1-1 with a 2.95 ERA in three starts against Oakland this year.

home_pitcher_note: In four starts since being recalled from Triple-A Sacramento, Eveland, who was sent down Aug. 3 to work on his mechanics and command, has shown dramatic improvement. His last time out, on Tuesday at Detroit, he held the powerful Tigers lineup to two runs on seven hits and two walks over six innings but didn't factor in the decision. Eveland, who needs to spot the ball to be effective despite a heavy, low- to mid-90s fastball, hasn't lost since returning to the A's, but he's 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA in two career starts against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla came off the disabled list on Tuesday and beat the Mariners, 7-3, holding them to one unearned run in 5 2/3 innings. He allowed six hits and a walk while striking out five. He is 3-2 with a 5.01 ERA in eight starts since the All-Star break while dealing with inflammation in his neck and a strained left hamstring. He is 3-4 with a 4.57 ERA in 11 starts at home. Padilla is 2-0 with a 4.63 ERA in two starts against the Athletics this season, and 5-1 with a 4.65 ERA in 11 games against them in his career.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy makes his fifth start for the Rangers after missing 4 1/2 months because of severe forearm/elbow inflammation. After two quality starts, he lost in his last outing against the Red Sox, allowing six runs in 5 1/3 innings in a 7-2 defeat. Opponents are hitting .250 off him, .300 by left-handed hitters and .200 by right-handed hitters. They are 3-for-17 (.176) off him with runners in scoring position. McCarthy is 1-2 with a 5.25 ERA in 10 games, including three starts, against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers will give Willis his shot at a start down the stretch after he spent most of the summer working on his command and delivery in a Minor League stint. He went from Class A Lakeland up through Triple-A Toledo and back to the big leagues, where a pair of simulated games earned him this test. How he fares could determine his course this offseason towards next year, the second season in the three-year contract he signed in December.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood is trying to break a two-game losing streak and is 3-3 with a 4.46 ERA in his last six starts since coming off the disabled list (strained left groin) on Aug. 15. He beat the Tigers, 9-1, on Aug. 20 with a six-hitter for the first of two straight complete games. He is now 4-4 with a 3.78 ERA in 10 starts against the Tigers in his career. He is 5-3 with a 4.37 ERA in 11 starts at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: After Miner's outings in July and August became a godsend to the Tigers rotation, Miner is struggling down the stretch. The latest example came Monday against the A's, who roughed him up for eight runs on 11 hits and forced him to use 110 pitches over 4 1/3 innings. That outing alone bumped up his ERA by more than half a run. He'll have a couple extra days of rest thanks to weekend postponements in Chicago before facing the Rangers, whom he beat in April with 3 1/3 hitless innings of relief.

home_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, Nippert has taken 163 points off his ERA as he's made his case to continue as a big league starter. His last time out in Oakland, he held the A's to one run on four hits and four walks in five-plus innings and he struck out seven. He shut the A's out over the first five innings, they finally scratched a run off him in the sixth when he couldn't record an out. Nippert will aim to extend his winning streak to three against the Tigers on Wednesday. It will be his first outing against Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia hasn't pitched in the Majors on June 8, 2007, when he was a Phillies starter trying to pitch through discomfort in his right shoulder. An unsuccessful summer of rest and rehab stints led to surgery to repair his labrum and rotator cuff just over a year, and he has spent most of this year working his way back into pitching shape. The Tigers signed him last month in what has essentially been a two-way tryout: Detroit gets to see where he's at in his rehab and gauge whether to try to re-sign him this winter, while Garcia has had the chance to work with the Tigers coaching staff on the finishing touches to his comeback and get an idea about the organization before free agency.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison will be hard pressed to best his last effort. At Oakland, Harrison tossed a shutout. He allowed just five hits and four walks and struck out five. It was the first shutout by a Rangers rookie in five years. It took Harrison seven Major League starts to strike out more batters than he walked in a game, but since Aug. 16, he has 27 strikeouts to nine walks. Harrison will face the Angels Friday. He earned his first career victory against the Angels in his debut, allowing only two runs on five hits and a walk in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garland worked around another poor first inning to throw a quality start Saturday against the Mariners, yielding just two first-inning runs on six hits in six innings. He has given up nine first-inning runs on 14 hits in his last four starts (20.25 ERA), but has not given up runs in any other innings of his last two outings (11 scoreless innings). Garland retired nine consecutive batters at one point on Saturday and did not give up a hit after the first until Ichiro Suzuki tripled in the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla's victory in his last start on Sept. 9 was his first since July 25. The former came against the Mariners and the latter came against the Athletics. Other than a victory on July 20 against the Twins, Padilla hasn't beaten a team over .500 since earning a victory against the Rays on May 27. He will have the opportunity to reverse that trend Saturday against the first-place Angels. Padilla did beat the Angels in his only start against them on April 6, allowing four runs -- three earned -- on nine hits while striking out four.
away_pitcher_note: Moseley is expected to get the call here as the Angels begin to set up their rotation for the postseason, giving Ervin Santana two extra days of R&R. Moseley salvaged what had been a disappointing season with an excellent performance against the Yankees in the Angels' Sept. 10 AL West title-clinching victory at Angel Stadium. Enduring a rocky first inning, he shut down the Bronx Bombers into the sixth inning, yielding two earned runs on three hits and three walks, while striking out six in five innings. Moseley is 0-1 in eight career appearances against the Rangers, with a 5.49 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Well, Feldman remained shut down for all of seven days between his start on Sept. 13 and his scheduled start on Sunday. Having thrown a career-high 138 1/3 innings this season, the Rangers had hoped his 4 2/3-inning start last Saturday would be his last of the season. However, a finger injury to Brandon McCarthy nixed those plans. But the change in plans will give Feldman to wash the sour taste from his mouth after his last start. Against the Athletics, he allowed six runs on seven hits and two walks in 4 2/3 innings. He'll face the Angels on Sunday. He's 0-1 in two starts against them this season with an 11.17 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rolling through 4 1/3 innings against the A's on Tuesday night having given up three hits, Lackey was rocked for a homer by Jack Hannahan and departed after yielding hits to five of the next eight men he faced. Lackey said he felt good, having gone nine days between starts, but had trouble putting his fastball where he wanted. Since going the distance to beat the Red Sox on July 29, Lackey is 2-2 in eight starts with a 4.22 ERA. Of his 102 pitches against the A's, only 58 were strikes -- reflective of subpar command. Lackey is 9-9 in 25 career starts against the Rangers with a 5.45 ERA, and he's 4-5 in 13 starts in his native Texas with a 6.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood didn't get the victory his last time out, but he definitely pitched worthy of one for 5 1/3 innings. That was the span he went without allowing a single baserunner. Six of the 16 straight batters he retired were by way of strikeouts. However, he allowed a run in the first inning and three more in his seventh and final inning to put a damper on his outing. It's now been three starts since Millwood earned his last victory on Aug. 31. He'll try again Monday against the Athletics, whom he is 1-0 against in two starts this season with a 1.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Smith entered his most recent start with the lowest run support in the Majors at 2.82 runs per nine innings. Despite seeing that number shrink, Smith was in line to beat the 2008 American League West champions until Mark Teixeira's two-run homer in the ninth inning gave the Angels a 2-1 lead that they lost in the bottom half of the frame. Less than a month after being tagged for 10 hits by the Angels in Anaheim, Smith held the Halos to four hits and a walk over six efficient innings Wednesday in Oakland. away_pitcher_note: What will Lee do for an encore, after a remarkable '08 season in which he became the Indians' second Cy Young Award winner in as many years and their second 20-game winner in 34 years? With former ace CC Sabathia long gone, the Indians are relying on Lee more than ever. They need him to set the tone for a rotation that enters the season with no shortage of question marks and concerns. Lee certainly has the mentality for the job, as his unshakable consistency, in terms of fastball command and aggressiveness, carried him to new heights in '08. He was one of just seven pitchers since 1920 to win 22 of his first 25 decisions, and his ERA was the lowest by an AL left-hander this decade. There will, however, be a worry that Lee's career-high workload (223 1/3 innings) could affect him in '09. Lee had a rough Spring Training camp, performance-wise, but he attributed most of his struggles to working on locating his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla went 0-2 with a 4.80 ERA in four Spring Training outings. He was 3-2 with a 3.79 ERA in six April starts in 2008, but is 13-19 with a 4.09 ERA in his career in April. away_pitcher_note: Two Carmonas exist -- the guy who used his sinking, 97-mph fastball to great effect in 2007, when he won 19 games and finished third in the Cy Young voting, and the guy who overthrew that sinker with disastrous consequences in his brief closing stint in '06 and his unremarkable '08. Carmona had a hip strain that held him out of action for two months last year, and that was no doubt part of his problem. But the Indians also believe he had trouble controlling his emotions. He showed much better control of himself and his pitches in spring camp, so the Tribe has high hopes for him going forward. They'll need a strong season from him in the No. 2 spot of the rotation if they're going to contend. Carmona was 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA in two starts against Texas last year.

away_pitcher_note: Pavano is the mystery man of the Indians' rotation. away_pitcher_note: Simon pitched three shutout innings in his season debut, but then he allowed a pair of home runs in the fourth that turned the game around. In this primetime game in Arlington, the southpaw faces the team that originally drafted him. Danks had a 1-0 record against the Rangers last year and is 1-1 lifetime against Texas.

away_pitcher_note: Millwood beat the Athletics, 5-4, on Tuesday while going eight innings. When it was over, Millwood was leading the American League in innings pitched and was fifth in the league in ERA. He is 2-6 with a 5.05 ERA at Safeco Field, his second most losses in any opposing AL city.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander has struck out 32 and walked only six in 31 innings over his first five starts of the season.  But he threw 92 pitches in five innings in his last start, settling for a no-decision in an eventual Mariners loss to the White Sox. away_pitcher_note: Padilla lost to the Athletics, 4-2, on Thursday and is now 0-2 with an 8.14 ERA in his last four starts. Padilla was 2-0 with a 2.05 ERA in five starts against the Mariners last year and is 4-5 with a 4.48 ERA in his career. He is 3-3 with a 4.21 ERA in nine career starts at Safeco Field.

away_pitcher_note: Feldman had it going early on against the Chicago White Sox, retiring the first 11 batters he faced, eight of them on ground balls. He wound up giving up three two-out hits in the game, and three runs. It earned Feldman another turn in the rotation with Kris Benson, the starter he replaced, out on a rehab assignment. Feldman seems to pitch better as a starter. He has allowed nine runs in 6 2/3 innings (three games) as a reliever. He has allowed four earned runs in 10 2/3 innings for two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Skipping a start and working on mechanics paid off for Cahill, who bounced back from his worst start of the season with six excellent innings against first-place Seattle. Cahill gave up one run on seven hits and settled into a groove in his later innings. After a leadoff home run by Russell Branyan and two more hits in the second, Cahill pitched shutout ball the rest of the way and retired the last seven hitters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy was strong in his start Saturday against the team that traded him, the Chicago White Sox, allowing three hits in five innings. He had three strikeouts and didn't walk a batter. He retired the last 12 batters he faced. McCarhty did a great job of attacking the strike zone, throwing 45 of 68 pitches for strikes. He has started a season 3-0 for the first time in his career, winning three consecutive decisions for the second time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: The White sox could have skipped Contreras' turn in the rotation after Wednesday's postponement, but Ozzie Guillen wanted to show another vote of confidence in the right-hander and simply moved all of his starters back one day. Contreras was shellacked by the Rangers on Saturday night, allowing seven runs on seven hits over 3 1/3 innings, striking out three and walking two. A three-run home run from Hank Blalock in the third seemed to change the complexion of the start and Contreras never recovered, falling to 1-7 in his last eight decisions dating back to last year.
