away_pitcher_note: This will be Harrison's second successive start against the White Sox. He pitched five scoreless innings, allowing six hits, in a 5-1 victory over them on Sunday. He did not walk a batter or strike one out. Harrison will be looking to win his third successive start. Harrison has made eight starts on the road in his Major League career and is 5-2 with a 5.51 ERA. This will be his first career start at U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: It was not exactly a triumphant return to Texas for the left-hander and Round Rock native, although Danks pitched better than the numbers indicated against the team who originally drafted him. Danks gave up four runs on 10 hits over 5 1/3 innings, the first time he has allowed double-digit hits in a game, but really only half of those hits were solidly stroked. Nonetheless, they all count in Danks' second straight loss after two straight wins, having now allowed 10 runs on 18 hits over his last 9 1/3 innings. Danks gets to face the Rangers again this weekend, looking to even his career ledger against Texas at 2-2. Danks has never faced the Rangers in Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood beat the Mariners, 6-5, on Monday despite allowing five runs in 7 2/3 innings and is now 2-0 with a 4.11 ERA in his last two starts. Left-handed hitters are batting .160 off him as opposed to .269 by right-handed hitters. Opponents are hitting .176 off him with runners in scoring position. He has pitched at least seven innings in six straight starts. He is 1-4 with a 3.23 ERA in nine career starts against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Colon looked as strong as he has in any of his four starts for the White Sox this season during a 2-1 victory over the Mariners in Game 1 of Tuesday's doubleheader. Colon struck out six and walked one, giving up four hits and one unearned run over seven innings. He also pitched out of a second-and-third, one-out jam in the seventh, nursing a one-run lead, while working up his pitch count to 95. Colon has not faced the Royals this season but has a 15-7 career mark with a 4.84 ERA in 25 starts. Colon holds a 6-4 record during his starts at Kauffman Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla pitched brilliantly on Tuesday against the Mariners, allowing one unearned run in eight innings and just one single. He didn't get the win but the Rangers won, 7-2, in 10 innings and are 4-2 in his six starts. He has a 3.05 ERA in his last three starts. Padilla is 1-2 with a 3.94 ERA in his five career starts against the White Sox. He did not pitch against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 2-0 with a 3.24 ERA in three starts and opponents are hitting .186 off him as a starter. They hit .355 off him as a reliever. He beat the Athletics, 4-2, on Wednesday night by holding them to two runs in six innings. He is now 8-8 with a 4.98 ERA in 28 career starts, going back to last season. Of those, 14 have been "official" quality starts and he is 6-2 with a 2.82 ERA in those games. He has a career 2.57 ERA against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: A start that originally was supposed to go to right-hander Carlos Silva goes instead to Vargas, who makes his first Major League start since 2007 when he was with the Mets. Silva is on the 15-day disabled list with inflammation in his right shoulder. Vargas has worked 3 2/3 scoreless innings of relief since being promoted from Triple-A Tacoma on May 2. He brought with him from Tacoma an 11 2/3-inning scoreless streak.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy had his shortest outing of the season on Thursday against the Athletics. He lasted just four innings and allowed seven runs in a 9-4 loss. McCarthy is 1-1 with a 7.71 ERA in his past three starts with opponents hitting .339 off him. McCarthy has made 19 starts in his career at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington and is 6-5 with a 4.30 ERA. He is 1-2 with a 7.02 ERA in his career against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn has been solid all season long, and he put up another great outing against the Royals in his last start. Unfortunately for Washburn, he took the loss despite allowing just one earned run in seven innings with five strikeouts. Washburn said his sinker was the key to his seven-inning performance against Kansas City. He threw it to lefties and righties and it kept hitters off balance all night. The 34-year-old left-hander has really surged this season, and he's one of the big reasons the Mariners are floating around the .500 mark.

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old lefty is learning to trust his stuff. Harrison has won three starts in a row and is working on a 19-inning scoreless streak. On Friday night, Harrison submitted a complete-game shutout against the White Sox, retiring 11 batters in a row at one point. He has chipped away at an ERA that rose to 9.20 after a no-decision at Toronto on April 22.
away_pitcher_note: As good as April was for the ace right-hander, May has been just the opposite. For the second time in two May starts, Hernandez had long-ball issues, surrendering two home runs during a four-inning outing against the Twins. After allowing just one home run in his first five starts and 37 innings, he has now given up four dingers in his last 10 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood has pitched at least seven innings in seven straight games to open the season. The right-hander pitched well but absorbed the loss on Saturday night against the White Sox, giving up three earned runs on seven hits. In 11 career starts against the Angels, Millwood is 3-4 with a 3.82 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Back in All-Star form, Saunders is coming off his first career shutout, a five-hit, 1-0 blanking of the Royals on Saturday night. Saunders unloaded 101 pitches and was throwing 91-93 mph gas in the ninth inning, striking out Mark Teahen and Jose Guillen, giving him six punch-outs for the night. Saunders' sinker and changeup resulted in a pair of groundball double plays to end innings as he outdueled Zack Greinke, handing the Royals' ace his first loss of the season. Saunders has had success against the Red Sox in his career, going 4-1 with a 3.25 ERA in seven outings. That one loss was his only defeat this season, a 5-4 setback on April 11, when he yielded four earned runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla made history during Sunday's 7-1 victory over the White Sox, becoming the first pitcher in Rangers history to allow one or zero hits in back-to-back starts. The right-hander walked four and threw a wild pitch that led to Chicago's only run, but otherwise, he has been on a remarkable run that has shaved his ERA down from 7.43 to 4.97.
away_pitcher_note: Missing the season's first six weeks for the second season in a row, this time with a right forearm strain suffered in late March, Lackey gets it fired up in his home state. Lackey, as the club's resident ace, will give a lift to the club -- even though starting pitching, amazingly enough, has been the least of the Angels' concerns. If he's back in 2007 form when he finished third in the Cy Young Award balloting, winning 19 games with a league-best ERA, the Angels will be thrilled. Lackey relies on fastball command and a big curveball. He had two Minor League rehab starts, going five innings on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 2-0 with a 2.74 ERA in four starts since coming out of the bullpen. He is 1-3 with a 6.39 ERA in 13 games against the Angels in his career. He is 1-2 with a 7.89 ERA in four starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver is off to a sensational start and is coming off a high-caliber effort against the Red Sox, in which he yielded only one run (on J.D. Drew's homer) across seven innings before the bullpen let a late lead get away. In the American League, only Zack Greinke has a better ERA than Weaver, who has averaged just under seven innings per outing in a reflection of his commitment to getting deeper in games with more early-count outs. Fastball command has been Weaver's secret, along with his cross-firing motion that provides deception. He's fourth in the AL in batting average against (.203) and has 35 strikeouts against only 10 walks in 47 2/3 innings. Weaver has excelled against the Rangers in his career (2-1, 2.54 ERA in nine starts) and at hitter-friendly Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, where he is 1-1 with a 1.80 ERA in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: The statistics from Willis' return to the big leagues weren't encouraging, with four runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings against the Twins last Wednesday at the Metrodome. The actual pitching was better than that, and it gave the Tigers a chance to win. He threw 53 of his 87 pitches for strikes, and both of his walks came on 3-2 counts with close calls. He not only changed speeds, but showed an ability to bust pitches inside on right-handed hitters with a fastball that consistently hit the low 90s. He picked up a no-decision last September at Texas, where he gave up three runs on two hits over five innings with five walks.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy is 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA in three starts in May. He went seven innings in his last start, his longest of the season, and the Rangers won, 6-5, in extra innings. He is 1-1 with an 8.40 ERA on the road with opponents hitting .355 off him. Overall, for the season, left-handed hitters are batting .315 off him while right-handed hitters are batting .219. He is 1-2 with a 5.11 ERA in 11 games, including four starts, in his career against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Not since Mickey Lolich in 1971 had a Tiger racked up double-digit strikeouts in three straight starts until Verlander followed up back-to-back 11-strikeout games with a career-high 13 strikeouts Thursday at Minnesota, most by a Tiger in one game since 2004. But that's just the surface of Verlander's success this stretch. He has given up three runs on 16 hits over 29 1/3 innings in his last four starts while racking up 44 strikeouts, and he's poised to do more of the same against a free-swinging Rangers squad. He's 4-1 with a 2.23 ERA in six career outings against Texas, striking out 33 batters in 36 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison has pitched two straight complete games and has won four straight starts with a 1.80 ERA. In those four games, he has pitched 30 innings while striking out 18 and walking two. He has allowed two earned runs in his last 28 innings, He made his first start of the season against the Tigers at Comerica Park and allowed four runs on nine hits and five walks over 52/3 innings in a 4-3 loss.

home_pitcher_note: In the wake of Justin Verlander's four-start tear, Edwin Jackson has been turning in some quality performances of his own. Jackson has now worked seven innings in consecutive starts, giving up only one run during the stretch. In his last start Friday, he stayed loose through a one hour, 13 minute rain delay after the fourth inning to complete a seven inning, one run performance. The start before that, at Cleveland on May 4, Jackson pitched seven innings of shutout ball, striking out seven. He's now made it through the seventh inning in half of his eight starts, and his 2.42 ERA is the lowest of all Tigers starters.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is 3-1 with a 3.81 ERA in his last four starts. He is 1-2 with a 3.81 ERA in four starts on the road. That includes a start in Detroit in the first weekend of the season when he threw seven scoreless innings against the Tigers before they rallied for six runs in the eighth inning against the bullpen. He is 4-4 with a 3.56 ERA in 12 career starts against the Tigers, including 2-1 with a 2.33 ERA in four starts at Comerican Park.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino didn't fare well in his first start since he was promoted to the rotation. In a May 12 outing at Coors Field, he allowed eight runs (seven earned) on seven hits over four innings. Prior to that outing, Paulino hadn't allowed more than four earned runs in any of his first three starts. He has never faced the Rangers.

Moehler allowed three runs over five innings while facing the Cubs in his last outing, earning his first win of the season. The veteran right-hander has allowed five runs over three starts since returning from the disabled list. Moehler made one start against the Rangers last year, earning the win after holding Texas to one run over 6 1/3 innings. In his career, he's 6-4 with a 4.63 ERA over 12 games versus Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman is 2-0 with a 2.17 ERA as a starter, with both victories coming on the road. He pitched six scoreless innings in the Rangers' 3-0 victory over the Angels on Sunday. As a hitter playing under National League rules, he is 1-for-3 with a single last year against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton had to leave his last start against the Brewers early with a small cut on his left thumb. Hampton received a no-decision after allowing two runs on three hits while walking three and striking out four before coming out after the fourth inning. Hampton will return to the mound at Minute Maid Park to face the Rangers still in search of his first win at home this season. Hampton is 0-1 with a 9.53 ERA in two career starts against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy went seven innings and allowed four runs for his second consecutive start. He surrendered single runs in each of the first three innings on a night when the high-octane Texas offense only managed one hit. The righty gave up just two hits in his final four innings. McCarthy has appeared three times against the Astros, making one start. He allowed two earned runs in those three outings. Catcher Ivan Rodriguez has gone 6-for-10 lifetime against him with two doubles and two RBIs.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison had a four-game win streak and two-game complete-game streak snapped in his last start. He allowed three home runs against the Tigers after yielding four home runs in his previous seven starts combined this season. He surrendered five runs on nine hits, which tied a season high, in five innings. Harrison will make his second career start against the Yankees. He allowed two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings in a Rangers win last season. Johnny Damon is the only current Yankee with a career hit off Harrison.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes allowed three runs in five innings in an 11-4 victory over the Orioles in his last start. But he is still 1-2 with a 9.77 ERA in his last four starts since throwing six scoreless innings in his first game on April 28, a 4-0 victory over the Tigers. Left-handed hitters are batting .372 off him while right-handers are hitting .283. He is also averaging 5.4 walks per nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Last time out against the Tigers, Millwood surrendered a home run for the first time in three starts. In fact, he gave up two. The righty allowed four runs on six hits in eight innings. Millwood has struggled in his career against the Yankees. In seven starts, he's 1-4 with a 4.46 ERA. He faced the Bombers once last season, allowing one earned run on five hits in five innings. Yankees outfielder Nick Swisher has hit .400 (10-for-25) off Millwood with three home runs and seven RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: Chamberlain left his last start against the Orioles in the first inning when Adam Jones hit a line drive off his right knee. He suffered a bruise, but is ready to go. He is 2-1 with a 3.23 ERA in his last six starts. He is 2-0 with a 2.22 ERA in four starts on the road. That's the fourth-lowest road ERA in the American League. He made two starts against the Rangers last year and allowed seven runs on 13 hits and six walks in 8 2/3 innings. His 7.27 ERA against the Rangers is his highest against any AL team.

home_pitcher_note: Holland, who was called up in April, opposed the Astros in his first Major League start and threw five scoreless innings before giving up a three-run home run to Lance Berkman in the sixth. The Rangers won the game in extra innings. Holland had a 4.85 ERA in seven relief appearances before being moved into the rotation. He has a 10.13 ERA in three appearances at the Ballpark.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett, like so many so far this season, was reminded how tough it is to pitch at the new Yankee Stadium in last start. He tied a career high by allowing three home runs to the Phillies on Friday, including one on the first pitch of the game to shortstop Jimmy Rollins. Burnett exited after six innings, having allowed five runs -- all on homers -- and took the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter is being called up to replace Matt Harrison, who is sidelined with a strained left shoulder. Hunter is 1-2 with a 4.82 ERA in four starts for Triple A Oklahoma. Hunter made three starts for the Rangers last year and was 0-2 with a 16.36 ERA. He was 13-8 with a 3.41 ERA in 25 starts in the Minors over three different levels.
away_pitcher_note: A 24-year-old rookie, Outman entered his most recent start, Sunday at home against the Diamondbacks, unbeaten with a 2.42 ERA and a .190 opponents batting average over four starts in May. He stayed hot with his most impressive outing yet, working a career-high 7 2/3 innings and rolling four double plays to offset five walks while allowing one earned run on four hits before leaving to a standing ovation with the bases empty and two out in the eighth. Acquired in the deal that sent Joe Blanton to the Phillies last summer, Outman made his big league debut last September and picked up a victory over the Rangers in his first start, holding Texas to a run on four hits and two walks over five innings. He faced the Rangers again later in the month and gave up three runs over six innings on the way to a no-decision. He hasn't faced Texas this season.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman, after a 6-3 victory over the Astros on Saturday, is now 3-0 with a 2.52 ERA in six starts. Opponents are hitting .222 off him for the season. They are hitting .200 off him the first time through the lineup., .188 the second time and .375 in the third turn through the order. All his victories have come on the road. He has not won in his last 13 starts at the Rangers' Ballpark in Arlington going back to last year. His last victory at home was on May 9, 2008, against the Athletics, and he is 2-2 with a 3.86 ERA in ten games, including five starts, against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Signed to a Minor League deal and intvited to Spring Training as a non-roster candidate for the starting rotation, Gonzalez, 26, opened the year at Triple-A Sacramento and was called up last week to make his Oakland debut Saturday. He worked five solid innings against the only other team for which he's played in the Majors. Expecting his former Diamondbacks teammates to be looking for a steady diet of breaking balls, Gonzalez kept them off balance by pounding the strike zone with fastballs and gave up a run on four hits before being pulled after issuing his only two walks of the game to open the sixth inning. Gonzalez, who pitched for Arizona from 2003-08, has only faced three current members of the Rangers in his career -- Omar Vizquel, Andruw Jones and Josh Hamilton -- and has allowed four hits in 26 at-bats (.154) against the trio. Hamilton is 1-for-4 with a home run.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy pitched his first career shutout in a 5-0 victory over the Astros on Sunday, allowing nine hits and one walk while striking out six. He has pitched at least seven innings and thrown at least 105 pitches in his last three starts and is 1-1 with a 2.74 ERA. He is 2-0 with a 4.30 ERA in four starts at home this season. He lost to the Athletics, 9-4, on May 7 by allowing seven runs in four innings and is 0-3 with an 11.57 ERA in his career against them. That's his highest ERA against any team.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson may have this winning thing worked out after recording his second Major League victory in as many starts. Monday's six-inning stint was easily his best of the season. He gave up a home run to Kenji Johjima, but it was the only solid hit off him all day. He allowed one run on six hits, walked two and struck out four. He pitched in Texas on April 28, taking a no-decision after giving up three runs (one earned) over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood threw a season-low 5 2/3 innings against the Yankees on Tuesday. He allowed three earned runs, but was throwing after a rain delay that lasted more than two hours. His ERA was 2.13 in five starts in April, but Millwood has pitched to a 4.50 mark in five starts in May. He is 5-3 with a 3.71 ERA in 14 career starts against the A's. Earlier this season, Millwood allowed two earned runs over eight innings in Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Braden, who entered his previous outing -- Tuesday at home against the Mariners -- with the lowest run support in the American League at 2.67 runs per nine innings, looked doomed to another tough loss when he walked to the dugout after the seventh inning. He was trailing 3-0 after having allowed three runs on nine hits and a walk while striking out one for his seventh quality start in 10 assignments this season. The A's offense came to life with a four-run rally to get him the win, though, ending Braden's personal three-game losing streak. A command pitcher with an excellent changeup and no fear when it comes to pitching inside, Braden beat the Rangers in his only start against them this season, scattering five hits and four walks while striking out a season-high six April 30 in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett won for the first time since April 14 in his last start, hurling six innings of scoreless three-hit ball against the Rangers in Arlington as part of a 9-2 victory. Burnett wasn't thrilled with his command -- he walked four -- but said it was progress. He last pitched against the Indians on April 19 in New York, taking a no-decision in the Yankees' 7-3 victory. Burnett is 1-4 with a 6.69 ERA in six career starts vs. Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is coming off the disabled list and making his first start since May 16. He has been sidelined with a strained right shoulder. Prior to that, he was 2-0 with a 1.57 ERA in his past three starts. He also has a 2.08 ERA in three starts on the road. Left-handed hitters are batting .325 off him, while right-handers are hitting .190. He is 1-1 with a 5.51 ERA in three career starts against the Yankees. That's his fewest appearances against any team that he's never played for in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte left his last start against the Indians with lower back tightness, but said he is certain he will make his next start against the Rangers on Wednesday in New York. Pettitte was a winner in that start, allowing one run on six hits in five-plus innings, but walked five and struck out one as he dealt with a soft mound at Progressive Field. Pettitte has won his past three decisions dating back to May 13 and has not faced Texas this year.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman improved to 4-0 with his victory over the Athletics Friday. Since joining the Rangers rotation, Feldman is 4-0 with a 2.59 ERA. This strong work has dropped his season ERA to 3.91 from 12.15. Feldman's previous victory at Rangers Ballpark also came against Oakland in a 4-0 Texas win on May 9, 2008. Prior to Friday's win, he had gone winless over 13 consecutive starts at home, a club record.

home_pitcher_note: Wang will make his first start since three dreadful ones at the beginning of the season, which resulted in a trip to the disabled list. But the Yankees insist that Wang has returned to the form that saw him win 46 games over two and a half seasons before a foot injury, pointing to his two most recent relief appearances as proof. At any rate, a game against the Rangers is a good place to start -- Wang shut them out over two innings of relief last week in Texas.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy is 2-1 with a 2.48 ERA in his past four starts after a 14-1 victory over the Athletics on Saturday. His five wins has already tied his career high for one season. He has gone at least six innings in his past four starts and has not allowed a home run in his past three starts. He is 2-2 with a 4.94 ERA in five starts on the road. McCarthy hasn't pitched against the Yankees in over two years. He beat them, 14-2, in his only career start back on May 10, 2007 in the Bronx.

home_pitcher_note: Despite giving up 10 hits over six innings in his last outing, Penny recorded his sixth quality start of the season. He gave up three runs, two of which were earned. Friday's start will be the third of Penny's career against the Rangers; he went 1-1 with a 2.70 ERA in the first two. At Fenway Park this season, Penny is 3-0, but with a 6.14 ERA. Opponents are hitting .310 against Penny this season.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is 2-2 with a 4.23 ERA in his past six starts after going 2-2 with a 2.10 ERA in his first two starts. He allowed runs in six innings in his last start against the Athletics on Sunday and was not involved in the decision. He is 1-3 with a 3.96 ERA in five starts on the road. He is 4-4 with a 4.46 ERA in 12 starts against the Red Sox in his career and is 3-1 with a 3.38 ERA in seven career starts at Fenway Park.

home_pitcher_note: In one of his best performances in what has been an inconsistent season, Lester struck out a career-high 12 batters over six innings in his last start, a win over the Blue Jays. He allowed just three hits and one run. Lifetime against the Rangers, Lester is 1-0 with a 4.50 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Holland last appeared on Sunday, when he pitched two innings in relief against the Athletics and allowed two runs. He is 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA in two starts. The Rangers brought him up to be a reliever but injuries to Vicente Padilla and Matt Harrison forced them to put the 23-year-old left-hander in the rotation. He has a 2.70 ERA in five appearances, including one start, on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Dice-K finally got in the win column in his last start, allowing one run over five innings against the Tigers. The righty walked three and struck out six. Matsuzaka hasn't pitched six innings in any of his five starts. This will be his third start of the season at Fenway. Matsuzaka has won all three of his career starts against the Rangers, posting a 4.15 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla made his first start since May 16 on Tuesday against the Yankees and showed signs of rust. He struggled with his command throughout the night and allowed seven earned runs in just 3 2/3 innings. Padilla surrendered seven hits, but was ultimately did in by four walks and two hit batters. He had won his final two starts before going on the disabled list with a strained right shoulder.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman's last outing wasn't particularly pretty, but it was effective. away_pitcher_note: Millwood lost for only the second time in his last eight starts when he was beaten by the Angels, 9-4, on Monday. He tied a career high by allowing nine runs in five innings. He is 8-9 with a 4.81 ERA in 19 career starts against the Mariners and is 3-6 with a 5.18 ERA in 11 starts at Safeco Field. He won there, 6-5, on May 4 to snap a four-game losing streak against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard showed good stuff in his first start back from the disabled list, retiring the last 10 batters he faced in four innings of work against Baltimore. He ran into trouble in the first inning, running up his pitch count early, causing his removal after the fourth inning. Two runs on two hits was all the Orioles managed, though, and the left-hander still managed to rack up eight strikeouts while throwing 72 pitches. Bedard is expected to be on a higher pitch count in this one. He's 4-2 lifetime against the Rangers with a 3.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Nippert made his return from the 60-day disabled list against the Angels on Tuesday, and he gets his second start of the season against the Mariners. He went 3 2/3 innings his last time out, allowing three runs on seven hits in an 8-5 Texas win. Nippert threw 72 pitches in that game, and manager Ron Washington said he doesn't have a set plan on how many innings he'll allow Nippert to throw against Seattle. home_pitcher_note: Padilla will be making his first start since July 8, marking just his second outing in 17 days. He went eight days in between his last two starts due to shoulder soreness. Padilla allowed one run on eight hits in six innings his last time out, but had to leave when he tried to barehand a one-hopper. The ball bruised his palm a little bit, but he's fine and should be good to go against the Twins. The right-hander is 3-2 lifetime against Minnesota with a 2.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: A high fever pushed Perkins' most recent start back three days and he came out looking a bit rusty after the extra time off. Perkins lasted just 4 1/3 on Saturday against the White Sox, giving up five runs on eight Chicago hits. The loss came after a pair of quality starts where Perkins went seven innings and notched wins against St. Louis and Kansas City on the road. Perkins is 2-0 with a 1.12 ERA lifetime against the Rangers.

In seven games (including one start), Feldman is 0-1 with a 6.46 ERA over 15 1/3 innings pitched against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Baker benefited from plenty of run support as he earned his seventh victory of the year Sunday against Chicago. This will be his first appearance against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Prior to earning the loss against New York, Liriano had seen improvement in his last two starts -- games in which he pitched seven innings each. As he has been prone to do, Liriano let one inning change the course of the game, as Minnesota couldn't dig out of a three-run deficit when New York scored three times in the second inning. home_pitcher_note: Millwood allowed four earned runs over six innings against the Mariners in his most recent start on July 11. away_pitcher_note: Smoltz closed out the first half by earning his first victory since April 17, 2008 -- a span of 450 days. In one career appearance at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, Smoltz recorded a three-out save.

Hunter is 1-2 over five starts with a 5.81 ERA over 26 1/3 innings pitched in his career at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington. This season, however, he's posted a 3.18 ERA over 17 innings there.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett earned his 100th career victory on July 12, firing a three-hit, complete-game shutout against Kansas City at Fenway Park. home_pitcher_note: Zack Greinke started off his second half with seven strong innings, but he still couldn't pick up a victory. away_pitcher_note: Feldman allowed three earned runs over six innings against the Twins on Saturday, earning his 11th quality start of the season. away_pitcher_note: Holland went four-plus innings against the Twins on Sunday, allowing three earned runs and four walks. Thirty-nine of his 90 pitches were balls. This was his first outing since a six-game rehab assignment with Triple-A Omaha in which he posted an impressive 2.18 ERA in 33 innings. He'd been out with a right elbow strain.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood earned the win after pitching six innings and allowing two earned runs to the Red Sox on Monday. He has now won six consecutive decisions at home. away_pitcher_note: Galarraga lowered his ERA by more than a quarter of a run in his last outing, thanks to 7 1/3 innings of one-hit, one-run ball. He has pitched at least 6 1/3 innings with one run allowed in three of his past four outings to revitalize his season, but the Tigers have won only one of those games. He would no doubt love to earn a victory against his old team in Texas, which he has beaten twice since the Rangers traded him to Detroit last year.

home_pitcher_note: Mathis will make Tuesday's start after Vicente Padilla was scratched for the second consecutive start after coming down with swine flu. away_pitcher_note: With the Tigers still looking for starting pitching on the market and the non-waiver trade deadline looming, this could be French's final start for a while. away_pitcher_note: Verlander has led the American League in strikeouts for much of the season, and it isn't really close. home_pitcher_note: Holland is 1-5 with a 6.42 ERA in nine starts this season after a 6-3 loss to the Royals on Saturday night. He is 1-2 with a 7.52 ERA in his last four starts. He is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA in three relief appearances against the Mariners this year.
away_pitcher_note: It's really anyone's guess as to who is going to start this game for Seattle, since it's Erik Bedard's turn and he just went on the disabled list. The left-hander has made three relief appearances against the Rangers, pitching an inning of scoreless ball in each of them.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla was scratched from last Wednesday's start due to swine flu and Tuesday's start because he didn't think his legs would last. away_pitcher_note: Since the Mariners could be short on starting pitching soon, depending on what happens with Jarrod Washburn at the non-waiver July 31 Trade Deadline, Vargas will probably make this start despite a rough outing last week. He got into a bit of a groove after the second inning but ran into trouble in the fifth and exited with the bases loaded and nobody out. The left-hander has faced Texas once this season, when he gave up one run in five innings in a 7-1 loss. He did not get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter pitched a career-high seven innings against the Tigers on Monday, allowing one earned run. He has now won in three consecutive decisions over his last four starts. In his past five starts since being called up from Triple-A, Hunter is 3-1 with a 1.47 ERA.  He has thrown four quality starts over that span. He has thrown at least six innings in four of his six starts this season. In one career start against the Mariners, Hunter received a no-decision, allowing no earned runs over six innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: The staff ace attempts to bounce back from an uncharacteristic outing, surrendering a season-high seven runs in a loss to the Blue Jays. He was not the same, as the Jays hit two home runs off him, the first time that had happened since May 9.

Feldman needed 38 pitches to escape the first inning and 18 more to record just one out in the third. In his career against the Athletics, he is 3-2 with a 3.73 ERA in 41 innings pitched. away_pitcher_note: Snell makes his Mariners debut after being acquired from the Pirates in a seven-player trade on Wednesday. home_pitcher_note: Anderson won for the second time in as many career starts at Fenway Park last Wednesday, firing six innings of three-run ball against the Red Sox. Anderson has a 7.00 ERA in two outings against the Rangers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Nippert receives another emergency start, this time in place of the injured Kevin Millwood. Nippert has earned a win in his last three appearances. He has not allowed a run in three career innings against the Rangers, all of which came last season.
away_pitcher_note: Holland allowed one earned run over 8 2/3 innings pitched against the Mariners on Thursday. He was perfect through 4 2/3 innings and retired 26 of 29 batters faced. away_pitcher_note: Padilla allowed three earned runs over six innings against the Mariners on Friday. It was his ninth quality start, which ranks third on the Rangers staff. away_pitcher_note: Hunter allowed five runs over five innings against the Mariners on Saturday. It was the most runs he allowed this season. He had allowed five runs in his previous five starts. away_pitcher_note: Feldman allowed two earned runs over seven innings against the Mariners on Sunday. It came on just three days' rest. home_pitcher_note: Weaver had his premium stuff working again on Sunday in Minnesota after going through a recent lull that he felt might have been the "dead-arm stage." He's 1-1 with a 5.75 ERA in three outings against the Rangers and 3-2 with a 3.39 ERA in 12 lifetime outings against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is expected to start on Saturday after having three consecutive starts scratched due a strained left gluteus muscle on July 26. In 14 starts in his career against the Angels, Millwood is 4-5 with a 4.62 ERA over 85 2/3 innings pitched. away_pitcher_note: Holland allowed four runs over 4 1/3 innings pitched against the Athletics on Tuesday, allowing four walks and striking out four and giving up four hits. In one game against the Angels in his career, Holland pitched two innings and gave up no runs, picking up a victory. Over his last three starts, Holland has a 4.15 ERA and a 1-1 record.

home_pitcher_note: After a shaky outing in his last start against the Angles, Laffey pitched one of the best games of his career Wednesday against the Twins. Laffey only gave up multiple hits in one inning and never let the Twins get much of anything going. He is feeling much more comfortable with his changeup, which is allowing him to throw all of his pitches for strikes. He is 0-0 with a 14.40 ERA in one career start against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Nippert is going into the rotation for good. He replaces Vicente Padilla, who was designated for assignment on Friday. away_pitcher_note: Hunter is coming off a 6-4 victory over the Athletics on Thursday and is 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA in two starts in August after going 3-0 with a 1.11 ERA in four starts in July. away_pitcher_note: Feldman is 6-2 with a 4.00 ERA in his last nine starts after being the Angels, 11-6, on Friday. He is 7-1 with a 3.70 ERA in 10 games, including nine starts, on the road this year. away_pitcher_note: The power lefty has been brilliant of late, despite not having the wins to show for it. away_pitcher_note: Penny registered just his second quality start in five appearances since the All-Star break on Monday, yielding three runs over six innings in a 93-pitch outing against the Tigers at Fenway Park. The bad news was that Masterson lasted just five innings and needed 92 pitches to get through them. That inefficiency forced the Indians to go to their bullpen in the sixth, and the one-run lead Masterson left behind was coughed up, leaving him with a no-decision. Masterson has made four career relief appearances against the Rangers but has never faced them as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis gets bumped up in the rotation to fill in for scheduled starter C.J. Wilson, who came down with a mild case of food poisoning. Lewis beat the Mariners, 6-2, on Friday at the Ballpark in Arlington in his first start for the Rangers after two years in Japan. He went seven innings and allowed one run on five hits. He was annoyed that he walked four, but the Mariners were 1-for-11 with runners on base and 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position. Lewis was 26-17 with a 2.82 ERA in 54 starts and one relief appearance for the Hiroshima Carp over the past two years, striking out 369 batters and walking 46 in 354 1/3 innings. Before he went to Japan, he made just two career appearances against the Indians. One was a start, one was a relief appearance and he has a 13.50 career ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Huff was the recipient of bad bounces on Friday in Detroit. The lefty took the loss despite just giving up one earned run in six innings. He worked his way out of a two-on, no-out jam in the sixth and generally had outstanding control and command throughout the game. That continued a strong trend from last September when Huff went 4-1 with a 2.18 ERA over his last five starts in 2009. "He was locked in all afternoon," Cleveland manager Manny Acta said of Huff in his first performance of the season. Huff did not face the Rangers in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison was supposed to pitch against the Yankees on Friday but was pushed up one day when C.J. Wilson came down with food poisoning. Harrison, the Rangers' fifth starter, made his first start of the season on Saturday against the Mariners. Harrison went six innings and allowed just one run on six hits, a walk and a hit batter. He struck out four. Harrison, who had shoulder surgery last summer and was making his first start since June 23, allowed eight of the first 18 Mariners batters to reach base, but then retired the last seven he faced on the afternoon. He left with a 3-1 lead, but the Mariners rallied in the ninth inning and kept him from getting a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia is on the hill to kick off a three-game weekend series with the Rangers, pitching on the one-year anniversary of the opening of Yankee Stadium -- also a game Sabathia hurled. The lefty was absolutely splendid in his last start on Saturday against the Rays at Tropicana Field, venturing 7 2/3 innings before Kelly Shoppach broke up his no-hitter bid with a single to left field. While Yankees manager Joe Girardi said that he would have pulled Sabathia no matter what due to his high pitch count (111), it makes for a fascinating argument to determine what might have happened. There will be a slightly longer leash on the workhorse Friday as he faces the Rangers, a team the ace has yet to face as a Yankee. Sabathia is 7-3 with a 4.50 ERA in 13 career starts vs. Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson was supposed to start Wednesday but was pushed back to this game because of a bout with food poisoning. He threw seven scoreless innings on Thursday against the Blue Jays and left with a 1-0 lead before Toronto rallied for a 3-1 victory. Wilson allowed five hits and two walks while striking out nine. The Blue Jays were 1-for-6 off him with runners in scoring position. He is only the second Rangers pitcher over the past three years to throw seven scoreless innings in a game and not get a victory for it. Wilson threw 98 pitches, the most he has ever thrown in a game. He has a 3.24 ERA in 17 career relief appearances against the Yankees.
summary: 2010-04-16 - Texas Rangers @ New York Yankees (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Burnett gave the Yankees plenty to like in his last start, overcoming a shaky first inning to hold the Rays to two runs on six hits over seven innings in a 7-3 win at Tropicana Field. Burnett did it by trusting the late life on his fastball and even mixing in a few changeups, believing catcher Jorge Posada when the backstop told him that his other pitches were good enough to win even though his curveball abandoned him. Burnett was 2-1 with a 2.84 ERA in three starts vs. Texas in 2009, striking out 27 and walking eight in 19 innings while scattering 13 hits. Burnett is 3-3 with a 4.05 ERA in nine career games (eight starts) vs. Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman put together a solid start his last time out, going seven innings and allowing two runs (one earned) on seven hits with four strikeouts in the Rangers' 9-2 victory over the Mariners on Sunday. Feldman, who won for the first time in 2010, ended up throwing the second-most pitches of his career, finishing the game with 117. After the sixth inning, Feldman had 105 but wanted to go seven innings. And Texas manager Ron Washington wasn't going to stop him, knowing Feldman had six days of rest between that start and his Opening Day start. He heads to New York on six days rest, too. In four lifetime games against the Yankees, including three starts, Feldman is 2-1 with a 3.72 ERA. In his lone start at Yankee Stadium last year, Feldman earned the victory after going 6 1/3 innings and allowing two runs (both earned) on five hits with five strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte will look to string another solid start to his ledger so far when he takes on the Rangers in Sunday's matinee at Yankee Stadium. Pettitte held the Angels to five hits over six scoreless innings on April 13, walking three and striking out six as the Yankees punched a 7-5 victory on the afternoon they received their 2009 World Series rings. Pettitte has scattered 11 hits in 12 innings this season but continues to find ways out of damage, allowing just one earned run so far. He was 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA in two starts vs. Texas last year and 10-9 with a 5.41 ERA in 22 career starts against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Harden held the Indians to two runs through six innings in the Rangers' 4-2 victory on Monday afternoon at Progressive Field. Harden, who didn't get the decision in a game decided in the 10th inning, allowed five hits and three walks while throwing 104 pitches. He struck out two. He wasn't particularly overpowering but the results were far better than his first start, when he lasted 3 2/3 innings. Harden said he still needs to do a better job of getting ahead of hitters right from the beginning. So far opponents are hitting .182 off him but he has walked eight in 9 2/3 innings. He is 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA in six starts and one relief appearance in his career against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer was terrific in his first start but labored in his last one. Over 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the Twins, Wakefield gave up 10 hits and six runs (five earned). He walked one and struck out two. In his two starts, Wakefield has walked two and struck out eight. This is Wakefield's first start of the season at Fenway. In his career, Wakefield is 91-69 at Fenway with a 4.30 ERA and a .258 opponents' batting average. The righty remains 11 wins shy of No. 200 in his career. He is 18 away from win No. 193 in a Boston uniform, which would surpass Cy Young and Roger Clemens as the club's all-time winningest pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis beat the Indians, 6-2, in his last start on Wednesday. He allowed two runs in 5 1/3 innings while allowing five hits and four walks. He also struck out 10, the sixth time in Rangers history that a pitcher has struck out 10 batters in a game while pitching no more than 5 1/3 innings. Opponents are hitting .186 off him in his first two starts, although he has walked eight batters in 12 1/3 innings. He walked just 19 in 176 1/3 innings in Japan last year. He has held opponents to 0-for-11 with runners in scoring position and 2-for-16 with runners on base. He has a career 1.93 ERA in four relief appearances and one start against the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: A solid performance in his last outing went for naught as the Red Sox offense could muster just three hits while Josh Beckett was in the game. Beckett went seven innings Friday against the Rays at Fenway Park, giving up one run (unearned) on four hits and a walk with eight strikeouts. He left with the score tied, 1-1.  Beckett has made three starts but has just one decision to show for it, a win April 10 in Kansas City.  In five career starts against the Rangers, Beckett is 2-2 with a 3.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison has made two starts and the Rangers have lost both despite his sparkling ERA. He took a 2-0 lead into the eighth inning in his last start against the Indians on Thursday in Cleveland before giving up a three-run home run to Shin-Soo Choo. Errors by third baseman Michael Young and Elvis Andrus set up the game-losing blast. Opponents are hitting .212 off Harrison and he has walked just two in 13 innings while striking out seven. His only start against the Red Sox came on Sept. 6, 2008, when he gave up four runs in six innings and was the winning pitcher in a 15-8 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Despite posting a low ERA, Buchholz hasn't been particularly pleased with his first two outings. In his last start, against the Rays, he pinned the Red Sox in a 4-0 hole after just one inning, but three of the runs were unearned. To his credit, he did settle down in that start and didn't give up a run for the rest of the five-inning performance. Buchholz took the loss in that one. In his first start of the season, Buchholz gave up seven hits and three runs (two earned) over five innings, picking up the win at Kansas City. Buchholz has pitched twice against the Rangers in his career, going 1-1 with a 2.70 ERA. He is 6-5 with a 3.70 ERA in his career at Fenway Park.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson had his last start pushed back two days because of a mild case of food poisoning. He started against the Yankees on Friday and threw 112 pitches over six innings in a 5-1 loss. Pitching in cold, wind and rain, he allowed five runs on seven hits, three walks and two hit batters. Two of the five runs were unearned. Wilson threw seven scoreless innings in his first start against the Blue Jays on April 8 but the Rangers lost that game in the ninth inning. Wilson, who spent the last four years as a reliever before moving into the rotation this season, has a career 2.53 ERA against the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Harden lasted just 3 2/3 innings in a 5-2 loss to the Yankees on Sunday. He faced 23 batters and 13 reached base on five hits, six walks and two hit batters. It was the first time in his career he hit two batters in a game. In three starts, he has struck out 15 and walked 14. Opponents are hitting .234 off him but with a .424 on-base percentage. Harden said he needs to do a better job of getting ahead of hitters right from the beginning. He is 3-2 with a 3.47 ERA in six career starts against the Tigers. In 23 career starts, Harden is 8-5 with a 3.35 ERA in 23 games in April.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer turned his fastball command into six quality innings against the Mariners on Sunday just when the Tigers needed it, helping them end a three-game losing streak and helping himself earn his first victory in a Detroit uniform. It was an encouraging sign for the Tigers, who are looking to Scherzer to fill a critical void in the rotation in his second full Major League season. He threw six innings of two-run ball with seven strikeouts against the Rangers in a start last year, numbers he would like to duplicate against an aggressive Texas offense.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman lasted just 2 1/3 innings in his last start, against the Yankees, allowing four runs on seven hits and two walks. It matched the shortest outing of his 59 Major League starts. In his first three starts, left-handed hitters are batting .414 off Feldman, while right-handers are hitting .189. He has given up eight of his nine runs in the first three innings. The last time Feldman went just 2 1/3 innings in a start was against the Tigers on July 29, 2009. He allowed six runs on 10 hits and two walks in a game the Rangers lost, 13-5, at the Ballpark in Arlington. Overall, he has an 8.82 career ERA against the Tigers, his highest against any American League team.
away_pitcher_note: Thomas gets the start in place of Dontrelle Willis, who was scratched from his scheduled start due to illness. In four appearances (no starts) this season entering Saturday, Thomas had a 7.04 ERA across 7 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis allowed three runs in five innings in his last start against the Red Sox on Tuesday. He left with a 6-2 lead, but the Red Sox rallied for a 7-6 victory. Lewis walked two, struck out five and threw 105 pitches. He has now walked 10 in 17 1/3 innings. He walked 19 in 176 1/3 innings in Japan last year. Opponents are hitting .206 off Lewis, including .222 by left-handed hitters and .185 by right-handed hitters. They are 1-for-15 against him with runners in scoring position. Lewis was with the Tigers organization in 2006, making 24 starts at Triple-A Toledo and two relief appearances for the Tigers at the Major League level. Lewis is 5-0 with a 3.75 ERA in his last seven starts and two relief appearances at the Ballpark in Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: Three starts into Porcello's second Major League season, success has been anything but easy, reminding many that even with a big league campaign under his belt, he's still a 21-year-old right-hander learning the game at this level. His sinker, the pitch that earned him a plethora of groundouts and efficient innings last year, has been less consistent so far this year, and it has cost him in the hit column, including 18 hits and nine earned runs over 10 1/3 innings in his last two starts. However, it's easy to forget that he owned a 6.23 ERA in four April starts last year. Porcello has never faced the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison lasted just four-plus innings in his last start against the Red Sox on Wednesday, allowing six runs on five hits and three walks. He was given a 4-0 lead and couldn't hold it, allowing three home runs. One of them was a grand slam by J.D. Drew. The Rangers are 0-3 in his three starts. He has now made 29 starts for the Rangers over the past three years and is 13-9 with a 5.60 ERA. He is 7-4 with a 5.52 ERA in 16 starts at the Ballpark in Arlington. He is 0-2 with a 7.59 ERA in two starts against the Tigers in his career. Both starts came last year.
away_pitcher_note: After searching for his old form in his first two outings of the year, his last start looked more like the Bonderman fans remember. After giving up three runs within five batters of his outing, Bonderman allowed a lone infield hit among his next 19 batters. He commanded his fastball and slider down in the strike zone much better than he had in his previous start, and he worked with catcher Alex Avila to induce some key outs with his new-found splitter. If he can continue that kind of pitching, he has a chance to be a workhorse kind of pitcher at the back end of Detroit's rotation. Bonderman is 2-1 with a 4.71 ERA in six career starts against the Rangers, but hasn't pitched in Texas since 2004.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson won his first career game as a starter on Thursday, throwing 6 2/3 scoreless innings to lead the Rangers to a 3-0 victory. It marked the first time a Texas starter has thrown at least 6 2/3 scoreless innings at Fenway Park since Kenny Rogers threw seven scoreless on July 16, 1995. Wilson has also started the season with three consecutive quality starts and will attempt to become the first Rangers starter with four in a row since 1993, when both Brown and Charlie Leibrandt did it. In 10 lifetime appearances against the White Sox, Wilson has a 3.65 ERA with 10 strikeouts. In three appearances against them last year, Wilson threw three scoreless innings and allowed only two hits with two strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: The final line for Buehrle during Wednesday's 12-0 loss to the Rays doesn't look very impressive. The southpaw gave up six runs on nine hits over 4 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking one. But of the nine hits Buehrle allowed, six were of the broken-bat or bloop variety. They all count the same, though, as Buehrle suffered the setback in his shortest outing of the season. Buehrle has a dominant 11-3 record with a 2.93 ERA against the Rangers, marking his most wins against a team outside of the American League Central. Buehrle also has a 4-1 record at Rangers Ballpark.

home_pitcher_note: Harden has struggled of late, as he has pitched five-plus innings only once in his first four starts this season. On Friday against Detroit, Harden lasted only 4 1/3 innings, allowing two runs (both earned) on six hits with five strikeouts and four walks. Harden has also issued 18 walks in 17 2/3 innings this season. Despite his early struggles, the Rangers intend to stick with Harden for the foreseeable future. "We've just got to figure out a way to get Rich to be more conservative with his pitches," Rangers manager Ron Washington said. "Rich is capable of winning at the Major League level." Harden will try to pick up his first win in a Rangers uniform against the White Sox, whom he is 3-3 with a 3.00 ERA in seven lifetime starts.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander took a walk on the wild side during Thursday's 10-2 loss to the Rays, issuing a career-worst seven walks over 4 1/3 innings, while throwing 108 pitches. Peavy gave up seven runs on seven hits, suffering his first defeat in seven starts with the White Sox. One bright spot, according to Peavy, was how changes made in his mechanics between his last start and this start resulted in a rise in velocity and the best stuff he has felt he possessed all season. He simply needs to harness that stuff within the zone. Peavy has never faced the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman struggled in his last start, lasting only 3 2/3 innings, allowing eight runs (four earned) on eight hits with four walks and a strikeout in a losing effort against Detroit on Saturday. It marked his second straight loss, as he went only 2 1/3, allowing four runs on seven hits against the Yankees on April 17. After Saturday's game, Feldman said he needed to work on keeping his pitch count low after throwing 93 pitches. In seven lifetime appearances, including two starts, against the White Sox, Feldman is 1-1 with a 4.11 ERA. In his one start against Chicago last year, Feldman went 5 2/3 innings and allowed three runs on three hits with three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander pitched far better than his last trip to the mound Sunday in Cleveland. But after giving up seven runs without retiring a batter in the second at Progressive Field, it couldn't have been much worse as Floyd stated. Floyd worked 6 1/3 innings against the Mariners on Friday in Chicago, allowing five runs on seven hits, while striking out four and walking three. Three of those runs scored when Jose Lopez hit a two-out grand slam off of reliever J.J. Putz in the seventh, erasing a chance for Floyd to pick up his first victory. Floyd has a 0-1 career record against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: The much-anticipated regular season debut of the 2008 American League Cy Young Award winner arrives as Lee takes on the Rangers at Safeco Field. A foot injury at the beginning of Spring Training, a strained lower abdominal muscle and a five-game suspension that was rescinded are all behind the veteran lefty, and it's full-speed ahead. Lee tuned up for Friday's start with six scoreless innings in a rehab start for Triple-A Tacoma last Sunday. He threw all of his pitches, commanded the strike zone and was basically pleased with the way he felt. He needed just 65 pitches to make it through six innings but should be able to reach the 100-pitch mark on Friday night without any problems.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis beat the Tigers on Sunday while allowing four runs in 6 1/3 innings. He allowed the four runs in the first two innings, but then retired 15 of 16 hitters to get the victory. He struck out 10 for the second time in four starts. He is only the third Rangers pitcher to strike out 10 or more batters in multiple April starts; Nolan Ryan did it in 1989, and Bobby Witt did it in 1986. Opponents are hitting .136 off Lewis with runners in scoring position through his first four starts. He has a 4.35 ERA in two starts on the road. Lewis made his first start of the season against the Mariners, allowing one run in seven innings in a 5-1 victory.

home_pitcher_note: A personal nine-decision winning streak, dating to last August 28, came to an end for the ace right-hander in his last start, although he extended his streak of quality starts to 18. He said the lack of run support has not affected the way he has gone about his work, but it's difficult to pitch when you know one or two runs could be enough to lose the game. He has pitched into the seventh inning in each of his five starts, but there simply is no room for mistakes with every outing being so closely contested, making every pitch critical to the outcome. This will be Felix's second start against the Rangers this season. He settled for a no-decision against them on April 10 in Arlington, allowing three runs (two earned) over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison allowed six runs in six innings in Monday's start against the Tigers and has allowed 12 runs in 10 innings over his last two starts. He allowed just two earned runs in 13 innings in his first two starts. The Rangers lost, 8-6, on Monday and have now lost all four games that Harrison has started. His first start of the season was against the Mariners on April 10 at the Ballpark and he allowed one run in six innings. He left with a 3-1 lead but the Mariners scored three in the ninth to steal his victory. Harrison has made four starts against the Mariners, his most against any American League opponent, and is 1-1 with a 3.91 ERA against them. But this will be his first start at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Fister did a nice job of holding Cliff Lee's place in the rotation through his first four starts, posting a 1.67 ERA (best among the team's starters) and a 2-1 record. With Lee back in the fold, Fister could give the Mariners an elite one-two-three punch if he stays hot. He lasted just four innings, threw 96 pitches and took the loss in his first outing of the season against Oakland, but since then, Fister has notched three quality starts in a row. He allowed just six hits and one walk during his next two appearances -- both wins -- and gave up two runs in eight innings against the White Sox last week, a game Seattle lost after closer David Aardsma was tagged for two homers in the ninth. Fister doesn't have a high strikeout rate (4.33 per nine innings), but his pitch-to-contact style works well at Safeco Field. As long as he doesn't put himself in harm's way by issuing free passes, he could thrive with the Mariners' solid defense behind him.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson beat the White Sox, 4-2, in his last start on Tuesday by allowing two runs in six innings. It was his fourth straight quality start to begin the year, the first member of the Rangers' Opening Day rotation to post four quality starts to begin a season since both Kevin Brown (six) and Charlie Leibrandt (four) accomplished the feat in 1993. The last Texas pitcher with an ERA of 1.75 or lower in four starts or more in April was Brown, who had a 1.14 ERA in his first four starts in 1993. Wilson is 1-1 with a 2.13 ERA in his first two starts on the road. He is 5-2 with a 5.77 ERA in 38 career appearances against the Mariners. That's his most appearances and most wins against any team in his career. He has a 6.28 ERA against the Mariners at Safeco.

home_pitcher_note: Braden was roughed up in his first loss of the year in his last start against the Rays, getting tagged for six earned runs on eight hits and three walks while striking out just one over four innings. The hiccup came after a string of four consecutive quality outings from the left-hander, who upped his ERA from 2.77 to 4.20. Considering the loss came against the team with the best record in baseball, Braden followers shouldn't fret just yet. However, he did admit after the outing that his seemingly permanent numb left foot did affect his game. Either way, Braden will look to bounce back vs. a Rangers team against which he owns a 1-2 record and 3.86 ERA in eight career games (five starts).
away_pitcher_note: Harden earned his first victory with the Rangers in his last start against the White Sox on Wednesday, allowing three runs in six innings. The Rangers won, 6-5, while Harden allowed four hits, walked five and struck out two. He has now made five starts and walked 23 in 23 2/3 innings while striking out 22. He is 0-1 with a 5.59 ERA in two starts on the road. This will be his first start ever against the Athletics. Harden was 36-19 with a 3.42 ERA in 89 starts and eight relief appearances with the Athletics from 2003-08. He is 18-9 with a 2.98 ERA in 47 starts and two relief appearances in his career at the Oakland Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro will make his 2010 big league debut after making 17 starts for Oakland last season. Mazzaro will make the start in place of injured right-hander Justin Duchscherer. Mazzaro started with Triple-A Sacramento this season and has a 1-1 record with a 2.59 ERA in five appearances (four starts). In 24 1/3 innings this year, Mazzaro has struck out 27 while walking 12. Mazzaro went 4-9 with a 5.32 ERA for Oakland last season, going 1-4 with a 5.46 ERA at home. Mazzaro has never faced the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman allowed three runs (one earned) in six innings in his last start against the White Sox on Thursday. The Rangers ended up losing, 7-5, and Feldman is now 0-2 with a 6.75 ERA in his past three starts. This is only his second start on the road. Last year, he set a Rangers record with 12 wins on the road. Left-handed hitters are batting .333 against him. He is 3-4 with a 5.33 ERA in eight starts and five relief appearances in his career against the Athletics. He has made four starts and one relief appearances at the Coliseum and is 1-3 with a 7.48 ERA there.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill was roughed up for six earned runs on seven hits over five innings in his season debut against the host Blue Jays. The A's right-hander walked one and struck out three in a loss during which he said he couldn't find his sinker. Cahill, who surrendered an Oakland rookie-record 27 home runs last season, offered up three to Toronto. The 22-year-old righty began the season on the DL with a left scapula stress reaction and was activated April 20 only to be immediately optioned to Triple-A Sacramento, where he made two starts and went 1-0 with a 1.04 ERA. Cahill earned the starting nod in Toronto due to Brett Anderson's trip to the DL, and he'll look to bounce back vs. a Texas team against which he owns a career 3-1 mark and 2.45 ERA in four starts. The ERA marks Cahill's lowest against any American League team.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis threw nine scoreless innings against the Mariners in his last start on Friday. He allowed three hits, walked one and struck out ten in a game the Rangers won in 12 innings. He retired the last 21 batters that he faced and the nine innings marked the longest outing of his Major League career. Lewis has struck out ten batters in three of his first five starts and his 38 strikeouts were the second most ever by a Rangers pitcher in the month of April. He now has a 2.33 ERA in three starts on the road. Opponents are hitting .195 off him, including .209 by left-handed hitters and .176 by right-handed hitters. Opponents are just 3-for-26 off him with runners in scoring position.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison beat the Mariners, 6-3, on Saturday for his first victory since May 14, 2009. Harrison needed 127 pitches just to get through six innings while allowing three runs, two earned, on seven hits and three walks. He struck out three. It was the most pitches thrown by a Rangers pitcher in six years. He still has a 7.88 ERA in his last three starts. Harrison will be pitching at the Ballpark in Arlington, where he has made 17 starts in his career and is 7-4 with a 5.74 ERA. Harrison is 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA in two career starts against the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Davies has produced back-to-back gems, following six shutout innings against Seattle with six innings of two-run work against Tampa Bay. He didn't get the victory in the latter game, but the Royals prevailed in extra innings so they've won in four of his five starts. His control continues to be something of an issue -- he walked five Rays and two of them scored -- but he gained command in his last three innings. Davies also notched a season-high six strikeouts. He's 0-3 with a 4.50 ERA in his career against the Rangers and all three losses have come at Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson has started the season with five straight quality starts, the longest such streak by a Rangers pitcher since Kevin Brown began the 1993 season with six straight. Charlie Hough also had six straight in 1988. Wilson faced the Mariners in his last start in Seattle and allowed one run on five hits with three walks and four strikeouts. The Rangers won in 11 innings. Wilson has held left-handed hitters to a .103 average while right-handers are hitting .256. He is 1-0 with a 1.38 ERA in two starts at home. He has made 10 relief appearances in his career against the Royals and has a 3.27 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke hardly could have pitched any better than he did last Sunday in Tampa Bay, where he worked a complete game, gave up four hits and no walks, struck out six and used just 87 pitches in his eight innings. Yes, eight innings because the Rays won, 1-0, on Greinke's only blip -- a slider that came in just a bit too high in the middle of the plate, which Evan Longoria hit it over the left-field wall. Again this year, Greinke isn't getting much run support, but this time around he's winless after six starts. In 2009, he was 6-0 at this point. Against Texas, he's 3-4 in his career but has a 2.68 ERA in 11 games. Last year, Greinke beat the Rangers once and lost to them once, both by 2-0 scores.

home_pitcher_note: Harden pitched seven scoreless innings in a 4-2 victory over the Athletics on Monday. He allowed just two hits, struck out nine and did not walk a batter. It's the ninth time in 133 career Major League starts that he did not walk a batter. Going into the game he was leading the league in most walks allowed. He is 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA in his past two starts, and 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA in three starts at home this season. Right-handed hitters are batting .191 off him while left-handed hitters are batting .230. He has struck out 31 batters in 30 2/3 innings. He is 2-0 with a 1.42 ERA in four career starts against the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Meche still hasn't got it working although he seemed to take a step in the right direction in his last start. He had a tough time against the White Sox, a team he usually handles well, although he was victimized by some well-placed ground balls. Meche gave up five runs in five innings, yielding nine hits and three walks while making 96 pitches. High pitch counts are indicative of his continuing struggle to get ahead in the count. His fastball was reaching the mid-90s, so there's no apparent problems with his shoulder or back, two trouble spots of the past. His history against Texas is spotty -- 5-9 with a 5.97 ERA overall against the Rangers and 3-6 with a 6.96 mark at The Ballpark.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman went seven innings in his last start against the Athletics on Tuesday and allowed seven runs on 10 hits, three walks and four strikeouts. He was the first Rangers pitcher since 2001 to pitch at least seven innings and allow at least seven runs. He allowed 13 of the first 22 batters he faced reach base before retiring the last 12. He is 0-3 with a 7.58 ERA in his past four starts. That matches his longest winless streak of the 2009 season when he won 17 games. He is 2-0 with a 2.48 ERA in two starts and seven relief appearances against the Royals in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Hochevar bounced back from a drubbing at Tampa Bay with six sharp innings in Chicago, holding the White Sox to one run on three hits last Tuesday night. That was big for Hochevar, who in the second half of last season got in a dreadful rut and had a tough time snapping out of it. In fact, it took him nine games before he could end his skid. This time, just one game. Hochevar is getting a lot of ground balls, indicating his sinker is working, and has given up just one home run. He's faced Texas just once in his career, beating them, 6-3, last year with seven strong innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis suffered his first loss of the season on Wednesday, allowing three runs in six innings in a 4-1 loss to the Athletics. He walked three and struck out six. He is 2-0 with a 3.38 ERA in two starts at home this season. Opponents are hitting .199 off him including .207 by left-handers and .186 by right-handers. They are 3-for-32 off him with runners in scoring position. He is 2-1 with a 3.60 ERA in five career starts and two relief appearances against the Athletics in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill allowed just one unearned run over five innings during Wednesday's win over the Rangers in Oakland. With the victory, Cahill moved to 4-1 with a 2.05 ERA in five career starts against the Rangers. His 2.05 ERA against Texas since the start of 2009 is the second-lowest figure in the Majors behind Scott Kazmir's ERA of 1.96. Felix Hernandez is the only other pitcher to have recorded four wins against Texas since the start of 2009. Cahill has only pitched in the Ballpark in Arlington once. He threw seven shutout innings, allowing one hit and two walks while striking out seven on Sept. 16, 2009, to earn the victory.

home_pitcher_note: Holland will be called up before the game to replace Matt Harrison, who is going on the disabled list with tendinitis in his left biceps. Holland was 4-1 with a 0.93 ERA in six starts at Triple-A Oklahoma City.  In 38 2/3 innings, he has allowed 32 hits, walked seven and struck out 37. He last pitched on May 4. Holland was 6-12 with a 6.23 ERA in 21 starts and 2-1 with a 5.48 ERA in 12 relief outings for the Rangers last year. He was 1-6 with a 10.19 ERA in his last nine starts. He was 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA in one start and two relief appearances against the Athletics last year.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez completed seven innings of work for the second time in three games in his last start, a 4-1 loss to Tampa Bay. He allowed three earned runs on three hits, striking out seven and walking five, but was outdueled by Rays lefty David Price. Citing a new slowed-down pitching motion, Gonzalez has been able to throw deeper into games recently. In three career appearances (one start) against the Rangers, Gonzalez is 1-0 with a 0.00 ERA over 9 2/3 innings. He has yet to face Texas this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson beat the Royals, 4-1, with a complete-game performance on Friday night. He allowed five hits, all singles and it was his sixth straight "quality start." He joins Kevin Brown (1993) and Charlie Hough (1988) as the only three Rangers starting pitchers to begin a season with six such starts. Nobody has done it seven times. Wilson has allowed one or fewer runs in four of his six starts. He allowed two runs over six innings in a 4-2 victory over the White Sox on April 27 and five runs -- three earned -- in his rain-shortened, six-inning complete game against the Yankees on April 16. Since that night he is 3-0 with a 1.21 ERA in four starts and the Rangers have won all four games.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets turned in his finest performance as an Athletic on Saturday, in Oakland's 4-2 win over Tampa Bay. He went 6 1/3 innings, his longest outing in the green and gold, allowing two earned runs on four hits while striking out eight and walking three. Sheets called it the most relaxed he had felt with his new team, since he signed a one-year, $10 million deal in the offseason. Sheets' breaking ball looked like it did during his days in Milwaukee, while his command looked better than it did in his previous two starts, when he gave up a combined 17 earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: While Cecil wasn't as dominant as his eight-inning, 10-strikeout performance against the Indians two starts ago, he pitched serviceably against the White Sox on Saturday in a 7-3 Blue Jays loss. Cecil went 5 1/3, allowing three runs on seven hits, chipping in three strikeouts. The bulk of the damage came in the first inning courtesy a two-out, two-run blast by White Sox slugger Paul Konerko. After a bases-loaded walk to Gordon Beckham in the second inning, Cecil settled down and cruised through his final 3 1/3 frames until being removed in the sixth because of a high pitch count (105). Credit the White Sox for battling as they forced Cecil to throw 61 of his pitches over the first two innings, contributing to his early exit. Over four starts Cecil's ERA sits at 3.12 with an impressive 24:7 strikeout-to-walk ratio. Cecil will pitch at home for only the second time this season, welcoming the Rangers, against whom he is 1-0 lifetime with a 12.60 ERA over one start -- an 18-10 Blue Jays victory.
away_pitcher_note: Harden allowed two runs in five innings in his last start against the Royals on Saturday. He didn't get the victory, but the Rangers ended up winning, 3-2. He is 2-0 with a 2.82 ERA in his last four games and the Rangers have won all four. He has struck out 34 and walked 25 in 35 2/3 innings, while opponents are hitting .225 off him. They are hitting .206 off him with runners in scoring position. He is 1-1 with a 3.24 ERA in three starts on the road. Harden, who is from Canada, is 0-3 with a 4.54 ERA in seven starts against the Blue Jays and 0-2 with a 10.61 ERA in two starts in Toronto.

home_pitcher_note: Romero was not his usual self against the White Sox on Sunday, lasting only 5 1/3 while surrendering four runs on eight hits with five walks. Although the Jays went on to win the game, 9-7, the five walks by Romero marked a season high. His lack of control was also evidenced by two wild pitches, bringing his season total to 12 -- he threw six all of last year. On the positive side, Romero has not been tagged for a home run since Tampa Bay's Jason Bartlett took him deep 20 1/3 innings ago. Romero also managed to fan seven White Sox, bringing his strikeout total to 22 over his past three starts. Look for a rebound at home against the Rangers. The young left-hander has dominated Texas in the past with a 1.35 ERA over 13 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman has gone five starts without getting a win. He managed to make it through just four innings on Sunday afternoon, allowing four runs on six hits and two walks in the Rangers' 6-4 victory over the Royals and was pulled after throwing 100 pitches. Feldman is 0-3 with a 7.83 ERA in his last five starts since going seven innings in a 9-2 victory over the Mariners on April 11. He is 0-2 with a 10.61 ERA in two road starts after winning a club-record 12 games on the road last year. Left-handed hitters are batting .319 off him. He is 0-2 with a 5.90 ERA in four starts and three relief appearances against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Morrow was dominant over his past four starts -- 2.96 ERA with 34 strikeouts -- heading into Monday's contest against the Red Sox, but was nothing short of awful at Fenway Park, going only 1 2/3 innings as Boston torched him for six runs, resulting in a 7-6 Blue Jays loss. Morrow set a Toronto record for most walks issued in an inning, with five, leading to a four-run second inning and the early hook from manager Cito Gaston. Blue Jays fans can only hope that this start was an anomaly, but Morrow certainly looked like the same pitcher who started the season with significant control problems and an ERA of 12.00 through his first two starts. Morrow has been lackluster in his career vs. Texas, going 2-4 with a 4.94 ERA over 23 2/3 frames.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis is 0-1 with a 2.45 ERA in his last three starts. He allowed three runs in seven innings in his last start against the Athletics on Tuesday and was not involved in the decision. The Rangers ended up losing in 13 innings. He is 1-1 with a 2.84 ERA in four starts on the road. Opponents are hitting .202 off him, including .176 by right-handed batters. They are 3-for-35 off him with runners in scoring position. In 45 2/3 innings he has struck out 49 and walked 17. He is 1-2 with a 12.08 ERA in his career against the Blue Jays. That's his highest ERA against any American League team.

home_pitcher_note: Holland was 4-1 with a 0.93 ERA in six starts at Triple-A Oklahoma City before being called up to replace Matt Harrison in the rotation. He made his first start on Wednesday against Oakland, pitching six scoreless innings in a 10-1 victory. He allowed five hits, walked one and struck out seven. He is now 7-12 with a 5.93 ERA in 22 career starts. He pitched a three-hit shutout against the Angels on Aug, 9, 2009 but lost two September starts against them, leaving him 1-2 with a 4.29 ERA against them in his career.
away_pitcher_note:
Kazmir admitted it was a "little strange" facing his former Rays teammates for the first time on Monday at Angel Stadium but didn't want to use it as an excuse for his command problems after he lasted just five innings and allowed three runs against his former club in a 7-2 loss. He walked three batters, one of which came home to score, and need 107 pitches to get through five innings.
