It marked his 12th straight start without pitching past the sixth inning. Kazmir is 6-1 with a 2.05 ERA against the Rangers in 10 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson allowed one run in seven innings in his last start against the Athletics, but left in a 1-1 game and did not get the win. He is still 3-0 with a 1.26 ERA in his last five starts. He has opened the season with seven consecutive quality starts, the first time in club history that's been done. He has an 0.93 ERA in four starts at the Ballpark. Wilson has also not allowed a home run in his last 69 1/3 innings at the Ballpark, which is also a club record. He has a 4.48 ERA in his career against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Three unearned runs, two on passed balls, were Weaver's undoing in a superlative effort against the Rays on Wednesday. The big right-hander had a career-high 12 strikeouts against two walks in seven innings, yielding six hits and two walks while giving up one earned run. Of the 120 pitches he delivered, 80 were in the strike zone. He had great command of his fastball and changeup. It was Weaver's seventh quality start in eight outings. Weaver is 4-3 with a 3.39 ERA in 14 career outings against the Rangers and is 1-3, 3.65 in seven starts in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Harden allowed seven runs in 2 2/3 innings in his last start, against the Blue Jays on Friday in Toronto. He walked six, giving him 31 walks in 38 1/3 innings. Harden was 2-0 with a 2.82 ERA in his previous four starts. He is 1-0 with a 3.79 ERA in four starts at home this season. Right-handers are hitting .203 off him, while left-handers are hitting .256. He has made two starts in his career against the Orioles and has a 0.69 ERA without a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie was dominant in a win against his former team on Friday night. He allowed a two-out, first-inning hit -- a bloop RBI single to Jhonny Peralta -- and then proceeded to dissect the Indians lineup with surgical precision. Guthrie retired 16 straight at one point and exited after tossing eight innings of one-run baseball in his best start this season. After an 0-4 start, Guthrie has won his past two outings and will look to keep that momentum going against the Rangers. He is 3-0 in seven games (five starts) against Texas, sporting a 3.48 ERA over 33 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 0-4 with a 7.42 ERA in his past six starts. He pitched on Saturday against the Blue Jays in Toronto and allowed five runs in 7 1/3 innings in a 6-0 loss. He is 1-1 with a 4.23 ERA in five starts at home. Left-handed hitters are batting .310 off him. They hit just .226 off him in 2009. Opponents are hitting .269 with runners in scoring position but .346 with two outs in those situations. Feldman is 3-0 with a 3.24 ERA in four relief appearances and three starts against the Orioles in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Matusz spent the better part of Saturday's game locked in a pitchers' duel with fellow rookie Mitch Talbot, who went eight innings and stole the win. While not at his best, Matusz rebounded from his worst start of the season to scatter seven hits -- all singles -- over seven shutout innings, walking four and striking out six. Saturday's no-decision was his first scoreless outing of the year and his longest outing since he went 7 1/3 innings in a no-decision on April 13. "[Matusz is] going to give you what he's got all the time," Orioles manager Dave Trembley said. "What he does have is a very good knack for coming up with the big pitch when he has to. He doesn't give in. He does not give in, which is commendable." Just 23, Matusz has an impressive four-pitch arsenal and will head into Thursday's finale at Texas looking to even his record. He has faced the Rangers just once, having allowed four earned runs over seven innings and collected the "W" in a start last season.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis went 3-0 with a 3.80 ERA in his first four starts but is 0-2 with a 3.58 ERA in his past four starts. He lost, 5-2, against the Blue Jays on Sunday, allowing five runs in 5 2/3 innings. He gave up three hits and walked four. He has walked 21 batters in 51 innings. He walked 19 in 176 innings in Japan last year. Opponents are hitting .132 off him with runners in scoring position. Lewis has never faced the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a win in his last game, which was his 100th start for the Cubs, but he did notch another quality start. The lefty gave up three runs on six hits over seven innings against the Pirates. He's now gone at least seven innings in back to back starts for the first time since last Sept. 18-30. He's made 12 starts against the Rangers in his career and is 4-4 with a 3.63 ERA. The last time was June 21, 2007, when he did not get a decision in a 6-5 loss in Texas. In that game, Lilly gave up five runs on six hits, including two homers, over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Holland went 5 1/3 innings, giving up just three runs on five hits with two walks and three strikeouts in a 4-3 victory over the Angels on Monday. Since being recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City, Holland has won both of his starts. He didn't give up a run until the fifth inning against the Halos, running his season-opening scoreless innings streak to 10. He pitched six innings and struck out seven in his first start of the season, a 10-1 victory over Oakland. This will be his first career start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wells did not get a decision in his last start but should've gotten a "W." He gave up one run on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings against the Rockies. It was his fifth quality start. He now has given up one or no runs in three of his eight games. He did throw 116 pitches, which was a career high. It'll be interesting to see if that has an effect on him. Wells is 2-0 with a 2.75 ERA in three starts against the NL West. This will be his first start against an AL West team.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson pitched just 4 1/3 innings against the Angels on Tuesday, giving up seven runs on seven hits with five strikeouts. In his shortest outing of the season, Wilson saw his homerless innings streak stop at 87 2/3 as Torii Hunter's two-run home run to left field was the first he had given up since July 9, 2009, to Franklin Gutierrez of Seattle. Despite that, the Rangers still won for the sixth straight game started by Wilson. This will be Wilson's first career start against the Cubs. He's 0-0 with a 0.00 ERA and three strikeouts against Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is the first Cubs pitcher to start 5-0 since Greg Maddux did so in 2006. This is the third time he's opened 5-0 (he also did so in 2004 with the Twins and 2002 with the Phillies, although the latter was as a reliever). He's never gone 6-0. The right-hander gives his family credit for their positive support. His wife, Maria, makes sure to text him before every game. But he's also benefited by pitching at Wrigley Field with the wind blowing in. That won't be the case in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Meche is still in search of his first win of the season as he opens a two-game series against the Texas Rangers. The Royals won Meche's last start, 8-5, thanks to a five-run ninth inning off of Indians closer Kerry Wood, but Meche didn't factor in the decision. The righty went just five innings, giving up five hits and two earned runs, but didn't have his sharpest stuff. In 17 starts against the Rangers, Meche is 5-10 with a 5.56 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Harden pitched 5 1/3 innings while giving up two earned runs in a 4-3 win over Baltimore on Wednesday night but did not factor into the decision. He struck out six Orioles while walking only one, the third time he's walked two batters or fewer in his last four starts. In his last start against the Royals on May 8, a 3-2 Rangers win, Harden pitched five innings while giving up two runs on six hits with three strikeouts in a no-decision. In four starts on the road this year, Harden is 1-1 with a 6.05 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After picking up his fourth win of the season in a complete game against the Cleveland Indians last Thursday, giving up just four hits and three earned runs with two walks and seven strikeouts, Hochevar will close out a two-game series against the Rangers. In his last start against Texas on May 9, Hochevar departed after just 2 2/3 innings, surrendering three hits and four earned runs, while walking four of the 15 batters he faced. Hochevar will look to become the Royals' first five-game winner.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Orioles, Feldman pitched six innings, giving up four runs on 12 hits with five strikeouts in a 13-7 win. It was his first win since April 11 against the Mariners. In his last start against the Royals, Feldman pitched just four innings, giving up four runs on six hits with four strikeouts in a 6-4 win. In two career starts at Kansas City, Feldman is 2-0 with a 1.61 ERA and nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Brewers, Slowey lasted 5 2/3 innings and gave up only two runs. He made it through four complete innings before allowing a runner to cross the plate. His other run came off a solo home run by Corey Hart in the sixth inning; he was pulled after that hit. Slowey gave up six hits and had five strikeouts in that outing. Slowey has lost only two of his 12 Interleague starts since the start of his career. The right-hander has had difficulty lasting deep into the game this season. He has lasted past the sixth inning only once this season, when he pitched eight innings against Cleveland on April 20. Slowey is on a two-game winning streak and has 43 strikeouts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis pitched six innings while giving up one run on five hits with four strikeouts in a 2-1 win over the Chicago Cubs last Friday. It was his first win since April 25, an 8-4 win over Detroit. In one career start and four relief appearances against the Twins, Lewis is 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA. In five starts on the road this year, Lewis is 1-2 with a 3.77 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano pitched well in his last outing against the Brewers, pitching eight innings and striking out five batters. Pavano allowed four runs in the game, three coming off home runs. The right-hander was given the loss due to lack of run support by the Twins, who left 14 men on base in that game. That has been a tough spot in Pavano's starts this season. The pitcher has the lowest ERA of the Twins starters, but has the least amount of run support with Minnesota scoring only 23 runs in his nine appearances. Pavano has lost four of his last five starts and is currently on a two-game losing streak. Despite his losing record, Pavano has pitched at least six innings in seven of his nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Cubs, Wilson suffered through a four-run first inning and finished the game with five runs allowed in 6 1/3 innings. Over his last two starts, Wilson's ERA is 10.80. Wilson has given up three home runs in his last two games after putting together 87 2/3 homerless innings dating back to last season. In 17 games against the Twins, Wilson is 0-1 with a 2.35 ERA and three saves. This will be his first career start against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Baker pitched a solid five innings in his last start against the Yankees on Tuesday. Although the game was suspended after the fifth inning, Baker was strong throughout. He allowed only three hits and faced more than three batters only once in the game. The right-hander pitched down in the zone and struck out two batters in the outing. Baker continues to prove his strength at home, where he has a record of 3-1 and allowing only 12 of his total 18 earned runs this season. Baker walked only one batter against the Yankees, and has given up one or fewer walks in his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Cubs, Holland pitched six innings while giving up three runs on four hits with five strikeouts. All three runs came on home runs. In two career starts against the Twins, Holland is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA and seven strikeouts. But for his career, he is 2-6 with a 4.98 ERA in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wednesday's afternoon of work was so abbreviated for Buehrle that he volunteered to pitch out of the bullpen on Friday night in St. Petersburg, which would have been his side day to throw. But Buehrle was not needed, so he comes into the homestand opener on the strength of 2 1/3 innings worked against Cleveland and only 36 pitches thrown. At that point, Buehrle was ejected by first-base umpire Joe West for dropping his glove following a second balk call against the southpaw made in consecutive innings. Buehrle enters the contest with Texas carrying a 4.38 ERA overall in 10 starts. He has an 0-1 mark against Texas this year, but has an 11-4 lifetime ledger, including a no-hitter thrown against the Rangers at U.S. Cellular Field in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Harden allowed six runs, five earned, in 51/3 innings against the Royals on Tuesday. He walked two, struck out five and did not get a decision in the Rangers 8-7 victory. The Rangers have won three of his last four starts although he did not get a decision. He has a 7.85 ERA and opponents are hitting .313 off him in those four starts. Because of the off-days, Harden will be pitching on six days' rest. He is 10-5 with a 2.66 ERA in 28 career starts when starting on six or more days of rest. He is 4-3 with a 3.19 ERA in eight starts against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: The months of April and May mercifully have come to an end for Floyd, who bounced back from a similar slow start in 2009 to post a 3-0 record and 1.28 ERA in June. Floyd posted a 6.49 ERA in April this season and followed up that lofty number with a 5.63 ERA in May. Floyd is coming off a loss to the Rays during which he gave up three runs on four hits over seven innings, striking out five and walking one, in making his second straight quality start. One of Floyd's two wins this year has come against Texas, while he has a lifetime mark of 1-1 against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman, after losing 5-2 to the Royals on Wednesday, is now 1-3 with a 6.97 ERA in his last five starts. He is 0-4 with a 7.71 ERA in four starts on the road after winning a club record 12 games on the road last season. Left-handers are hitting .319 off him while right-handers are batting .294. He made one start against the White Sox earlier this year and allowed three runs, one earned, in six innings. He allowed just two hits and walked four. He is 1-1 with a 3.83 ERA in three starts and five relief appearances against the White Sox in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia showed the importance of a veteran presence on the mound during the White Sox 4-2 victory over the Rays on Friday night. After getting crushed by the Marlins during his last start at home on Sunday, Garcia came back to absolutely shut down the best team in baseball by record. The right-hander gave up just two runs on four hits over seven innings, setting a season high with seven strikeouts and walking two. Garcia needed a mere 89 pitches to get through the seven frames at Tropicana Field. Garcia has not faced Texas this season, but has a 6-5 career mark against the Rangers. Garcia also has a 3-1 record on the road in 2010 but just a 1-2 mark at home, with a slightly lower 5.24 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis was 1-3 with a 4.11 ERA in May. He lost to the Twins, 2-1, on Friday by allowing two runs in six innings. He struck out just one and walked four. It's the fourth time this season he has walked four or more in a game. He is 1-3 with a 3.65 ERA in six starts on the road. Opponents are hitting .204 off him, but he has walked 28 while striking out 59 in 63 1/3 innings. He struck out a season-low one against the Twins on Friday. Opponents are hitting .154 off him with runners in scoring position.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson lost to the Twins on Saturday at Target Field. He retired 17 of the first 18 hitters he faced, but then allowed two runs in the fifth and three in the sixth. He is now 0-2 with a 9.56 ERA in his past three starts. Opponents are hitting .222 off him, including .102 by left-handers and .261 by right-handers. He is 2-1 with a 3.69 ERA in six starts at the Ballpark in Arlington. He is 1-0 with a 1.35 ERA in 13 career relief appearances against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Davis bounced back from a shaky outing against the Red Sox earlier in the week with a much-improved performance against the White Sox on Saturday night. The right-hander went 6 1/3 innings and gave up three runs on six hits and two walks. He had plenty of run support, as the Rays put up eight against Chicago, but Davis' fastball command was back where he wanted it to be. He gave up two home runs -- a two-run shot in the fifth and a solo shot long after the game was out of reach in the seventh -- and only struck out two, but he displayed his excellent command by throwing 72 of his 110 pitches for strikes. Davis will make his 11th start of the season and his first of the year against the Rangers. The rookie right-hander has never faced Texas in his short career.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter was 9-6 with a 4.10 ERA in 15 starts for the Rangers last year and was supposed to be in their rotation to start the season. But he came down with a strained muscle in his left ribcage in Spring Training and started the season on the disabled list. He is 1-2 with a 4.05 ERA in six starts at Triple A Oklahoma City. In 26 2/3 innings he has allowed 28 hits while walking 11 and striking out 14. He allowed five runs on 10 hits in five innings in a loss to New Orleans in his last start on Memorial Day. He is 1-0 with a 3.48 ERA in two career starts against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note:
After a quality eight-inning start against the Red Sox, Shields got back on the mound and had his worst outing of the season -- an 11-hit, seven-run loss to the White Sox in 5 1/3 innings of work -- that he deemed "absolutely unacceptable." Chicago got to Shields early, racking up three hits and a run before he got the first out of the game, and the biggest blow came in the form of a grand slam in the sixth inning. Shields doesn't walk a lot of batters, which makes him more susceptible to give up home runs. He has allowed nine roundtrippers this season, tied for the third most in the American League.
Shields will make his 12th start of the season and his first of the season against Texas. The right-hander is 2-1 with a 4.82 ERA in four career starts against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Harden beat the White Sox on Tuesday while allowing four runs in five innings but is still 1-0 with an 8.84 ERA in his past four starts. He leads the American League with 37 walks. He is 1-0 with a 3.70 ERA in five starts at the Ballpark in Arlington this season. Left-handed hitters are batting .274 off him while right-handers are hitting .250. He has pitched 54 innings over 11 starts, which is fewer than five innings per outing. He is 3-1 with a 4.94 ERA in five career outings against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Garza did not have his best stuff Monday in Toronto, but he still managed to give the Rays a chance to win. The 26-year-old right-hander struggled early, allowing two runs in the first inning and three runs total over the course of his 6 1/3-inning stint. In the end, he took his fourth loss of the season. Garza has the best stuff on the staff, which he can put on display in any given start and he seems to be maturing on the mound, which has led to his no longer allowing his emotions get the best of him. Garza is 3-3 with a 4.30 ERA in seven career starts against the Rangers; he is 1-3 with a 5.96 ERA in four career starts in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the White Sox, Feldman went eight innings, giving up five runs on eight hits in a 9-5 win. In his only start against the Mariners this season, Feldman went seven innings while giving up just two runs on seven hits with four strikeouts in a 9-2 win on April 11. In seven career starts against the Mariners, Feldman is 3-1 with a 2.67 ERA and 25 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last two starts, both eight-inning outings, Lee notched twice as many strikeouts (18) as hits allowed and gave up a total of four runs. That was a nice way to bounce back from his worst outing since 2007, an eight-run, 11-hit start against the Padres on May 21. He showed remarkable command Wednesday against the Twins, throwing 80 of his 112 pitches for strikes and walking just one. He was tagged for a solo home run by Michael Cuddyer, the first dinger he'd allowed in 50 2/3 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the White Sox, Lewis suffered the loss after giving up four runs on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings of work. Lewis has already started against the Mariners twice this season, going 1-0 with a 0.56 ERA. He's given up only one run to Seattle in 16 innings of work along with 13 strikeouts. For his career, Lewis is 3-2 with a 3.95 ERA in eight starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez was on fire Thursday against the Twins, as he struck out nine and allowed just one run on five hits in eight innings to earn his first win since April 21. Catcher Rob Johnson called it Hernandez's best outing of the season, and he put the finishing touches on in historic style by striking out four in his final frame. That was made possible after a wild pitch/strikeout combo landed Joe Mauer at first, and Hernandez responded by fanning Justin Morneau to end his night. The King was fired up after the fourth K, and rightly so. It was the first time a Seattle pitcher accomplished the feat since Kazuhiro Sasaki in 2003.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson matched starter Colby Lewis for the most wins on the staff with a 9-6 win over the Rays on Friday. Wilson pitched five-plus innings, giving up five runs on six hits with five strikeouts. It was his first win since May 7 against the Royals. Still, Wilson has left with the bases loaded in each of his last two starts, with four of those runners eventually scoring. In his only start this season against the Mariners, Wilson earned a no-decision in a 3-1 Rangers win in 11 innings. He went seven innings, giving up one run on five hits with four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Snell is coming off a complete game if you had his last two starts together. He lasted just 5 1/3 against the Angels on Friday while throwing 98 pitches (60 strikes), walking four and surrendering three hits and four runs. In his three starts since returning to the rotation from bullpen duty, Snell has yet to make it through the sixth inning. His main issue has been aggressiveness, as his inability to attack the strike zone has led to walks (nine compared to four strikeouts) and a rising pitch count that doesn't give him a chance to go deep into games.

home_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start of the season, Hunter picked up a complete-game win against the Rays, giving up just one run on five hits with four strikeouts. He had excellent control of his fastball, issuing no walks and inducing 13 ground-ball outs. Of the 117 pitches he threw, 76 were for strikes. Hunter made four starts against the Mariners last season, going 1-2 with a 2.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith is a placeholder in the rotation for Doug Fister, who's on the disabled list until at least June 16 with shoulder fatigue. Rowland-Smith's first spot start went well, as he allowed only one run on four hits to drop his ERA below seven for the first time since before being demoted to the bullpen following his May 17 start. Thanks to lots of foul balls and some long at-bats, his pitch count rose quickly and he was bounced after throwing 86 pitches in five innings. But he finished strong by staying down in the strike zone -- his problem in his first eight, mostly poor, starts -- and won back some faith from manager Don Wakamatsu. He'll be on a longer leash this time around with a chance to impress, even though it's unlikely to keep him in the rotation barring a setback from Ian Snell.

home_pitcher_note: If you take away his first inning on Saturday in St. Louis, Narveson pitched pretty well. But the Cardinals' four-run rally, which included a two-run home run by Albert Pujols on an 0-and-2 pitch, hurt, and the Brewers lost the game in 11 innings, 5-4. Narveson has surrendered at least four earned runs in four of his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Rays, Harden took his second loss of the season, giving up four runs on five hits in five innings. The Rangers offense gave Harden four runs but failed to get a win, as Harden fell to 41-1 in his career when receiving at least four runs of support. Opponents hitting in the No. 9 hole are hitting .476 (10-for-21) against Harden this season. In five career starts against the Brewers, Harden is 1-2 with a 4.70 ERA. However, two of those starts came at Miller Park, where Harden is 1-0 with a 1.30 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Parra made some strikeout history in his last start against the Cardinals but needed a bailout from the bullpen. First, the good: Parra became the 50th pitcher in Major League history to strike out four batters in an inning after Cards catcher Yadier Molina reached base on a wild pitch in the fourth. Parra also struck out the side in the third inning, making him the first pitcher since 2003 to whiff seven batters in the span of two innings. The bad: After Albert Pujols led off the sixth inning with a homer, Parra recorded an out but then walked three straight batters. He needed relief help to escape with the lead.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mariners, Feldman gave up four runs on nine hits with four strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings. Feldman has now surrendered four home runs over his last three starts. In his last seven outings, Feldman has a 2-4 record with a 6.45 ERA. This will be his first career start against the Brewers. In seven starts in Interleague Play, Feldman is 1-4 with a 5.71 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo settled for a no-decision against the Cubs on Tuesday after a valiant effort. He worked seven shutout innings, allowing four Cubs hits with two walks and seven strikeouts, and has now allowed two or fewer earned runs in 11 consecutive starts. Since beginning the season 0-2 with a 6.75 ERA in his first two starts, Gallardo is 6-0 with a 1.67 ERA in his last 11.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis pitched seven innings while giving up one run on four hits with five strikeouts in a 7-1 win over the Mariners on Tuesday. It was his third quality start in his past four outings and game him seven for the season, tying him for the team lead with C.J. Wilson. Opponents are batting .154 off him with runners in scoring position. Lewis is 1-4 with a 3.95 ERA in seven starts on the road. This will be his first career start against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Beating the guy who has already been perfect this season has risen Johnson to another level. In his last start, Johnson tossed eight shutout innings, retiring the final 17 he faced at Philadelphia, in a victory over Roy Halladay. In his last six starts, the ace is 4-1 with a 0.43 ERA (two earned runs in 42 innings). His lone loss was to Halladay. He gave up an unearned run in seven innings on the night Doc tossed a perfect game. Johnson threw 113 pitches at Philly.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mariners, Wilson pitched seven innings, giving up only two runs on four hits with four strikeouts. It allowed Wilson to retake the team lead in quality starts with eight. He's only pitched two-thirds of an inning in his career against the Marlins, giving up a hit while registering a strikeout. He only carries a 1-4 record in Interleague Play with a 5.26 ERA in 32 games.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez was effective in his last start, going seven innings and giving up four runs on four hits and three walks while striking out four. He didn't need to be, though, as the Marlins lineup put up a season-high 14 runs against the Rays. Still, the right-hander's solid outing put Florida in good enough position to withstand a Tampa Bay rally that brought the final score to 14-9. He was not as sharp as he could have been, throwing 61 of his 103 pitches for strikes while his ERA climbed to 3.36, but he got his sixth win of the year. This will be Sanchez's 13th start of the year and his second Interleague outing. He has never faced the Rangers in his five-year career.
away_pitcher_note: Hunter is making his third start since being recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. He beat the Mariners, 12-3, in his last start, allowing three runs in six innings. Opponents are hitting .185 off him in two games and right-handed hitters are 2-for-20. Opponents are also 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position. He is 11-8 with a 4.83 ERA in 24 Major League starts over the past three seasons. Hunter began this season on the disabled list with a strained muscle in his left rib cage. He was 1-2 with a 4.06 ERA at Oklahoma City before replacing Derek Holland in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Victimized by three solo home runs in his most recent start, Nolasco comes off his shortest outing of the season. The right-hander worked 2 1/3 innings in a loss at Tampa Bay, giving up five runs on nine hits. In his past two starts, he has struggled, allowing eight runs in 7 2/3 innings with four walks and four strikeouts. Finding consistency has been a struggle for Nolasco, who is 2-3 with a 5.73 ERA in six home starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers decided on Nippert over left-hander Matt Harrison because the Marlins have a predominantly right-handed lineup. Last year, he was 3-3 with a 4.65 ERA in 10 starts and 2-0 with a 1.86 ERA as a reliever. His longest outing this season is three innings and 47 pitches against the Blue Jays on May 14. He threw 37 pitches over two innings against the Rays on June 6 and has pitched just once since then. He threw 22 pitches over 1 1/3 innings against the Mariners last Thursday in Arlington. He has not pitched on the road trip but has a 2.53 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: The reigning world champions had their way with Rodriguez in his last start. Rodriguez lasted five innings, surrendering eight earned runs on seven hits and five walks while striking out four. Rodriguez will look to lower his 5.60 ERA as he opens up a three-game series against the Rangers. A key for Rodriguez will be to limit the hits allowed, as he has given up 91 hits this season in 72 1/3 innings pitched.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman beat the Brewers, 4-3, on Saturday, holding them scoreless through six innings. He allowed four hits, three walks and hit a batter while striking out a season-high six batters. He is 3-2 with a 4.45 ERA in his last five starts, pitching at least six innings in four of those five starts. He is 2-4 with a 6.03 ERA in six starts on the road this season. Left-handed hitters are batting ,315 off him this season while right-handers are hitting .288. He is 2-4 with a 5.12 ERA in eight starts and 11 relief appearances in Interleague Play, but has never faced the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Making just his fifth start of the season, Moehler is still eyeing that elusive first victory. Through his first 16 appearances, Moehler is 0-3 and will look to pick up his first win against the Rangers. If he wants to find that first win Saturday, he will need to silence the hot bats of the Rangers. In his last start, Moehler lasted 4 2/3 innings, allowing four earned runs on four hits and five walks.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis is 3-2 with a 2.70 ERA in his past five starts. He beat the Astros, 7-2, on Sunday and had two hits and two RBIs. He also struck out 10 batters and is the first Rangers pitcher to have at least four 10-strikeout games since Nolan Ryan in 1991. Opponents are hitting .197 off him, including .147 with runners in scoring position. He is 2-4 with a 3.68 ERA in in eight starts on the road. He has made two starts this year against National League teams and is 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino would like to forget his last start ever happened. On Tuesday night, Paulino was done in by a seven-run fifth inning by the Royals. He lasted just 4 2/3 innings, while giving up 10 runs (eight earned) and 11 hits, as he picked up his eighth loss of the season. Paulino will look to start inching closer to .500 as he faces the Rangers in the finale of a three-game home series.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson went six innings in his last start against the Marlins and allowed two runs on two hits while walking a season-high six batters. He is 2-0 with a 3.50 ERA in his past three starts after going 1-2 with a 4.62 ERA in six starts in May. He is 1-2 with a 3.13 ERA in five starts on the road. He has held left-handed hitters to a .107 average while right-handers are hitting .250. He is 1-1 with a 5.00 ERA in ten relief appearances against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter won his first two starts but had to come out of his last start against the Marlins on Wednesday when he strained his right hip flexor. The Rangers don't think it's serious and they still expect Hunter to make that start. He pitched 2 1/3 innings against the Marlins. Hunter started the season on the disabled list and had to make six starts at Triple-A Oklahoma City. He is 11-8 with a 4.81 ERA in 25 Major League starts over the past three seasons, including 8-4 with a 3.87 ERA in 14 starts at the Ballpark. This will be his first start ever against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Now nine starts into the season, Ohlendorf is still in search of that first season win. His outings haven't been terrible, but they've certainly not been up to par with what the Pirates were expecting out of the right-hander at the start of the year. He's been average, at best, and continues to struggle pitching out of the stretch. Batters are hitting .310 off of him with runners on base, compared to .243 in the same situations last year. In his last start, Ohlendorf was especially plagued by command issues with his breaking pitches. The Austin, Texas, native will be making his first career appearance against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Nippert will be making his second start. He was called out of the bullpen after 22 relief appearances when Derek Holland and Rich Harden went on the disabled list. The Rangers could also go with Matt Harrison, but Nippert made the last start in this spot, pitching three innings and giving up three runs on Thursday against the Marlins. He is now 6-8 with a 5.81 ERA in 22 career Major League starts. He is 6-6 with a 5.25 ERA in 82 relief appearances. He has a career 4.53 ERA at the Ballpark in Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm was charged with four runs his last time out, though his performance was much more dominant than that would suggest. The left-hander breezed through six scoreless innings before an array of singles just squeaked through during a four-run seventh. Still, with the Pirates' offense struggling, it was enough to send Maholm to his first loss since May 20. He continues to be the most consistent starter Pittsburgh has, having gone at least six innings in his past seven starts. The loss snapped a streak of four straight quality starts, too. This will be Maholm's first career start against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 3-1 with a 3.71 ERA in four starts in June after going 1-3 with a 6.97 ERA in five starts in May. He won his last start by holding the Astros to three runs in seven innings in a 9-3 victory on Friday in Houston. He is now 3-1 with a 3.44 ERA in six starts against National League teams over the past two years. He is 2-2 with a 4.58 ERA in seven starts at home this season. Opponents are hitting .300 off him.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens would like just one pitch back from his last start. Until allowing a three-run homer to Austin Kearns in the sixth, Karstens was rolling through Cleveland's batting order with ease. Kearns would be the last hitter Karstens faced in his 5 1/3-inning effort. The fact that he threw just 68 pitches is evidence of how efficient he was before getting into some sixth-inning trouble. Karstens has now made four straight starts and appears to be sticking in the rotation for the time being. He continues to consistently give the Pirates a chance to win, and has come up with some big performances when the Pirates needed it most. This will be Karstens' first career appearance against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis beat the Astros, 2-1, with his first Major League complete-game performance on Saturday. He allowed two hits, struck out nine and did not walk a batter. He has won three straight games and is 4-2 with a 2.34 ERA in his last six starts. He has made three starts against National League teams and is 3-0 with a 1.57 ERA against them. Opponents are hitting .187 off him, including .143 with runners in scoring position.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler certainly pitched well enough to earn a win last Saturday against the Rangers. He only gave up one hit over six innings. Yet that one hit was a two-run homer to Justin Smoak, which was the difference in a 5-1 loss. Moehler gave up only the two earned runs but walked four in the defeat. Despite the fact that starter Bud Norris is available to be activated from the disabled list, Moehler's performance earned him another start against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson started against the Astros on Sunday and allowed four runs, two earned, in seven innings in a game the Rangers won in 10 innings. He is now 2-0 with a 3.24 ERA in his last four starts and he is 0-1 with a 4.34 ERA in his three starts against National League teams. He has made eight starts at home and is 4-1 with a 3.71 ERA. He has held left-handed opponents to a .105 average while right-handers are hitting .250.
away_pitcher_note: Banks, a non-roster invitee to Spring Training who has spent the entire season at Round Rock, is 8-5 with a 2.97 ERA in 15 starts. In 97 innings, he's allowed 92 hits, 40 runs (32 earned), 24 walks and struck out 34 batters. He is 4-7 with a 5.38 ERA in 26 career Major League games with the Blue Jays and Padres.

home_pitcher_note: The Rangers have won all four starts since Hunter has returned from the Minor Leagues. He left a start against the Marlins on June 16 with a strained right hip flexor and pitched just 2 1/3 innings. But he came back and started on Tuesday against the Pirates, holding them to three runs in six innings in a 6-3 victory. He is now 3-0 with a 2.14 ERA in three starts at home. This is his first start against the Astros and he is 1-1 with a 3.07 ERA in three starts in his career against the National League.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt's third attempt to beat Giants ace Tim Lincecum on Tuesday went similar to his first two. He pitched well enough for a win but didn't receive enough runs to get the victory. Oswalt pitched his 13th quality start of the season and fourth consecutive start of seven or more innings. In June he has an ERA of 2.25.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough start, yielding six hits and one run through three innings on Wednesday, Pineiro found his command and his comfort zone, retiring 14 in a row before his first walk with one out in the eighth ended his night against the Dodgers at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman is 4-2 with a 4.76 ERA in his last seven starts. He is 3-4 with a 5.68 ERA in seven starts on the road. He has made nine starts and 18 overall appearances against the Angels in his career and is 4-4 with a 5.31 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir's run of four consecutive wins ended in a wild and fitful fourth inning against the Dodgers on Thursday night. He yielded four hits and a walk and hit a batter, his night ending when he went to second trying to get a force after bobbling a comebacker.
away_pitcher_note: Beltre will be added to the Rangers' active roster before this game, with a corresponding move to follow. "Beltre has been throwing well for Oklahoma City, and we wanted to give him an opportunity when he's going good," manager Ron Washington said.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver continues to sit atop the AL leaderboard in strikeouts with 11 in each of his past two outings. He has been remarkably consistent, allowing three or fewer earned runs in 13 of his 16 starts. Deception and quality breaking stuff complement his low-90s heater.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson is 3-0 with a 3.09 ERA in his last five starts after a 7-2 victory over the Astros on Saturday. He allowed seven runs in 4 1/3 innings in a start against the Angels on May 18 but the Rangers rallied for an 8-7 victory. Wilson is 1-2 with a 3.03 ERA in six starts on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Hoping to give Lewis as much rest as possible, the Rangers pushed him back from Wednesday to Friday. He had a three-game win streak snapped in a 7-4 loss to the Astros on Friday, allowing a season-high nine hits. Opponents were 4-for-8 with RISP.
away_pitcher_note: Freddy Garcia continued to be the improbable ace of the White Sox, collecting his ninth win of the season in holding the Cubs to just two runs despite giving up eight hits. Garcia's nine wins are most on the staff, ahead of Jake Peavy's seven.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Hunter allowed one run on five hits with a strikeout in six innings. He's held opponents to two earned runs or fewer in all five starts this season and has registered quality starts in four of those. His only non-quality start was cut short due to injury.
away_pitcher_note: John Danks presided over the Sox first loss in some 11 games in his last start, a 8-6 defeat to the Cubs. After the game, Danks said, "I flat-out stunk; there's no other way to put it. You have to credit them for hitting my mistakes."

home_pitcher_note: Feldman kept the Rangers in the game against the Angels on Tuesday, exiting with a 3-all tie and two runners on, but both runners later scored on a three-run double by Bobby Abreu. As a result, Feldman allowed five runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings and took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Buehrle struggled with his control as he walked five of the 30 batters he faced en route to his sixth loss of the season. In previous three starts, he had only walked two of the 81 batters he faced. Buehrle will look to climb back to .500.

home_pitcher_note: Beltre earned a no-decision in his first career big league start Wednesday against the Angels despite a rocky beginning. After surrending a homer to the first major league batter he faced before giving up two more runs an inning later, Beltre settled down.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey on Wednesday earned his first victory as a starter since Aug. 16, 2009, with a six-inning effort against the Blue Jays. The 25-year-old lefty yielded one run on five hits with two walks and five strikeouts in a 97-pitch outing. He had lost his previous seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson was bothered by his lack of command against the Angels on Thursday -- he walked four batters -- but other than that he was effective. He allowed just two runs on five hits over 5 2/3 innings, but took the loss as the Rangers' offense was held in check by Jered Weaver.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Blue Jays on Thursday, Masterson gave the Indians a strong 8 1/3-inning performance in which he allowed just a run on eight hits with five strikeouts and didn't walk a batter. It was the kind of outing that restores faith in Masterson's abilities as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis received an extra two days of rest prior to his last start vs. the White Sox, but received no decision after yielding three runs over six-plus frames with three K's. Lewis thought his breaking pitches were much better than his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot suffered his third loss in four decisions Friday. The Athletics tagged the rookie right-hander for three runs -- two earned -- on five hits and four walks with five strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. He is 3-4 with a 3.83 ERA over his past eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter pitched seven-plus innings while allowing only one run in a 3-1 win Saturday over the White Sox, despite allowing nine singles. He's won a club record five consecutive games at home to start the season and is 11-4 with a 3.51 ERA in 17 career starts there.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie turned in his worst outing of the season against Boston on Saturday, allowing six earned runs over four innings. He has taken the loss in six of his past seven starts, pitching to a 6.17 ERA over that span.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the White Sox, Feldman took the loss after giving up five runs on eight hits in six innings. In four career starts against the Orioles, he's 4-0 with a 3.77 ERA and 13 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Getting his first win since April 18, Matusz was simply brilliant against the hot-hitting Red Sox, going seven innings and giving up no runs on two hits. Matusz has a career 1-1 record and a 10.61 ERA vs. Texas after giving up seven runs in 2 1/3 innings on May 20.

home_pitcher_note: Lee will make his debut for the Rangers after being traded from the Mariners on Friday. He'll replaced left-handed pitcher Matt Harrison, who had recently been recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. In 13 starts for the Mariners, Lee led the AL in ERA and complete games.
away_pitcher_note: The Orioles are giving Chris Tillman another shot after watching him dominate in the three starts at Triple-A. The 22-year-old Tillman averaged less than four innings in four starts earlier this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson picked up the win in his last start against the Indians, allowing one run on two hits with four strikeouts in six innings. He's recorded a quality start in five out of his last six starts. In 10 starts at Rangers Ballpark, Wilson is 6-1 with a 3.38 ERA in 64 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta turned in one of the best outings of his young career on Tuesday, holding the Tigers to just one run over 6 1/3 innings. The 24-year-old struck out four and walked two in the no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield has struggled at Fenway this season, going 1-4 with a 5.89 ERA. He didn't have much command in his last start, walking six and allowing four hits and six runs over 5 2/3 innings in a loss. Wakefield is 3-7 with a 5.12 ERA as a starter this season.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Orioles, Hunter earned the no-decision after pitching six innings while giving up three runs on seven hits with a career-high seven strikeouts. Hunter has two career starts against the Red Sox, going 1-1 with a 11.74 ERA in only 7 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old lefty will make his third start of the season, and second in place of the injured Clay Buchholz. In his last start, Doubront gave up five hits and two runs over 5 2/3 inning. Doubront won his Major League debut at Fenway on June 18.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Indians, Lewis picked up the win after throwing six innings while giving up three runs on six hits with eight strikeouts. In his only start this season against the Red Sox, Lewis picked up a no-decision after throwing five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey will try to improve after a first half that was a bit below his standards. Opponents are hitting .298 against the righty. Lackey has pitched better at Fenway (7-2, 4.45 ERA) than on the road (2-3, 5.19). This is his first start of the season against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start for the Rangers on Saturday against the Orioles, Lee picked up the loss after giving up six runs on nine hits with two strikeouts. Despite that, he still threw a complete game on only 95 pitches. In nine career starts against the Red Sox, Lee is 2-4.

home_pitcher_note: The All-Star lefty will try to build off his dominant first half. Opponents are hitting just .203 against Lester. In nine Fenway starts, he is 6-1 with a 2.77 ERA. This will be Lester's first start of the season against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson will get the ball in the finale with the Red Sox. In his only start against Boston this season, Wilson picked up the win after not allowing a run through 6 2/3 innings. In that span, he gave up only four hits and two walks while striking out two.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman worked six innings of three-run ball in the Tigers' 7-4 victory against the Twins on July 10, his first quality start since June 17. The 27-year-old right-hander is 3-3 with a 3.63 ERA in nine appearances at Comerica Park this season.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Orioles, Feldman earned the no-decision after a late O's rally. He pitched seven innings while giving up two runs on eight hits with two strikeouts. It was just the third time in his last 11 starts that he pitched into the sixth inning.

home_pitcher_note: Detroit plans to recall Galarraga after a one-start stint with Triple-A Toledo. The 28-year-old righty worked 6 2/3 innings of three-run ball against the O's on July 6, his first quality start since June 13. He's 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA in six appearances at Comerica in '10.
away_pitcher_note: Hunter is the first Rangers pitcher since Esteban Loaiza to win his first six decisions in a season. This is only his third start on the road this season and he is 4-4 with a 5.90 ERA in 12 road starts in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer yielded five runs on five hits and five walks over five laborious innings in the Tigers 8-2 loss to the Indians on Friday. The setback snapped a four-game winning streak for the 25-year-old right-hander, who is 4-1 with a 2.32 ERA in his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis is 5-1 with a 3.13 ERA in his last seven starts after beating the Red Sox on Friday at Fenway Park. He is 4-4 with a 3.44 ERA in 10 starts on the road. Opponents are hitting .209 off him, including .175 with runners in scoring position.

home_pitcher_note: Lee is making his third start for the Rangers since being acquired from the Mariners. He has pitched nine innings in both games, but the Rangers have lost both times. He is 6-3 with a 3.19 ERA in nine starts against the Angels in his career.
away_pitcher_note:
Weaver bounced back from one of his worst starts of the season to throw seven solid innings against the Mariners in a 3-2 win on Friday.
Weaver allowed just two runs, both coming on a seventh inning two-run homer from Justin Smoak, and struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson is 6-2 with a 3.54 ERA at the Ballpark in Arlington this season. He has made two starts against the Angels and is 0-1 with an 8.10 ERA against them. The Angels scored seven in 4 1/3 innings against him at the Ballpark on May 18.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders struggled against the Mariners on Saturday, allowing five runs, four earned, on 10 hits over six innings while the Angels let an early five-run lead slip away. But Saunders got the no-decision in an eventual Angels victory.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is looking for his first win since June 18. He is 0-2 with a 6.37 ERA in his last five starts, including a 6-5 loss to the Angels on June 29 in Anaheim. Feldman has made six starts against the Angels over the past two seasons and is 3-2 with a 4.76 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Santana was certainly effective against the Mariners on Sunday, as he allowed just one run on three hits but was saddled with the no-decision. But he's been on a roll recently with a 7-4 record and a 3.19 ERA over his last 12 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter is the first Texas starter to win his first seven decisions of a season after pitching seven scoreless innings in an 8-0 win over Detroit Tuesday. He is 5-0 with a 2.25 ERA in six starts at home this season. He is 0-2, 9.82 in two starts vs. the Angels, both in '09.
away_pitcher_note: Bell is consistently in the 93-95-mph range. He showed poise in his MLB starting debut last year against the Rays and then beat the Indians in Cleveland. A reliever earlier, he feels he can get to 100 pitches after three Minor League starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lee picked up his first win as a Ranger in his last start, vs. the Angels, tossing 8 1/3 frames while yielding two runs on five hits. He's pitched into the eighth in seven straight starts, the first to do that since Toronto's Pat Hentgen in 1996.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez is 3-1 with a 3.80 ERA in his last four starts. Against the Red Sox on Wednesday, Gonzalez earned the win after allowing four runs over six innings in a 6-4 A's win. He struggled in his lone start at Texas this season, allowing four runs over four frames on May 12.
